💠No EBITDA or PAT number guided for H2; more detail to be shared at a factory visit for investors

▫️Cell contribution: ~500–600 MW of cells expected to be produced and sold, as cells or in panels, over the next ~4–4.5 months
💠Cell EBITDA margin expected at ~35%
💠Average realisation of ~₹22 for TOPCon
💠If the module business does not generate enough cash, cells will be sold in the market instead

▫️Blended margin: expected to be a little lower than earlier expectations as module margins stay under pressure; pressure expected to ease from April 2027
💠Cells to be the major profit contributor in the short run

▫️Cell utilisation: ~50% in December, 100% (industry standard 95–96%) from 1 January 2027

▫️H1 FY27 revenue: ₹885.01 Cr (H1 FY26: ₹903.24 Cr)
💠EBITDA ₹130.98 Cr (H1 FY26: ₹144.10 Cr)
💠PAT ₹60.06 Cr (H1 FY26: ₹94.95 Cr)

▫️Q2 FY27: revenue ₹381.59 Cr, EBITDA ₹53.20 Cr (13.94% margin), PAT ₹20.20 Cr (5.29% margin)
💠Q2 revenue was lower than Q1 as panels were not sold at a loss

▫️Module industry: capacity of ~225–250 GW vs demand of ~60–70 GW, with some imports still allowed
💠Standalone module makers are under the most stress; this scenario is expected to last another 3–4 months, followed by consolidation and closures
💠Orders expected to move towards integrated players

▫️FY28: ₹4,000 Cr revenue is possible
💠On that turnover, ₹500–600 Cr PAT (15–16% margin) is possible
💠Current margins (historically EBITDA 16–17%, PAT 8–9%) are expected to nearly double at both levels with cell operations

▫️Long term: only integrated players expected to thrive as the industry cleans up; module margin contribution to return after consolidation

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Order book: ~₹1,600–1,700 Cr, expected to rise after ALMM List II listing

▫️2.2 GW G12R TOPCon cell plant (Kosi Kotwan, Mathura):
💠Trial production started and now in ramp-up; complete line with utilities running
💠Line 1 completes around 18 November, line 2 about 6–7 days later, line 3 about 6–7 days after that, taking the full 2.2 GW to operational by 30 November
💠Built in 16–17 months; fully stable ~10 days after full capacity
💠Raw materials for >200 MW of cells already stocked
💠~80% of machinery from China, some from Taiwan; Taiwan, Korea or Germany are options for future expansion

▫️ALMM List II (cells) listing:
💠Fees paid and process completed; inspection by officials expected on 24–25 November
💠Listing expected within ~10–12 days of inspection
💠Capacity may be listed in parts (a later visit can follow within ~1 week); the factory is ~1.5 hours from the approving agency (NISE)
💠Cells can be sold as non-DCR before listing; DCR-compliant sales begin after listing
💠C&I demand, given a 6-month reprieve, comes under the cell requirement from 1 January 2027

▫️Ingot and wafer (5 GW by FY30; first phase production by June 2028):
💠Technology tie-up in place, factory almost ready, financial arrangements largely complete
💠Paused because of China's restrictions on technology and equipment transfer; Tata and Adani have also paused
💠Decision expected around 5–10 January 2027, once the Chinese policy is public
💠100 MW pilot plant targeted by end Q1 FY28
💠12–18 months to build; 5 GW of cells expected to be in place by FY30

▫️Aluminium frame (12,000 MT today):
💠Capacity expansion started, to double or triple
💠BIS now applicable on frames from December; anti-dumping investigation started, duty likely in 2–3 months
💠Frame is ~10–11% of panel cost; in-house supply insulates against disruption

▫️Module capacity: 2.4 GW operational; 3.6 GW module expansion paused, with leasing of capacity possible if needed

▫️Solar glass: 5 GW by FY30

👉Q&A :
▫️Solar cell pipeline demand:
💠~60% of module capacity is TOPCon
💠Strong demand for DCR TOPCon cells, with many queries from the industry

▫️Ingot/wafer vs cell build time:
💠Similar timelines of 12–18 months, possibly shorter with the experience gained

👉 Others :
▫️Inventory: elevated due to the second (G12R) module factory, raw materials for the cell line and unsold finished goods
💠Expected to come down by 31 March 2027, though cell raw material inventory will keep rising in the short run

▫️Warrants: ~₹97 Cr pending, with the deadline around 20–23 March 2027
💠Management expects exercise; business is not dependent on the warrant money

▫️Credit rating upgraded from BBB to A-

▫️Main board migration targeted for ~15 February 2027

**Ego death** (also called ego dissolution) is the temporary fading or collapse of the ordinary sense of being a separate, bounded “I.” The personal narrative, body boundaries, and feeling of a fixed self looking out at a world of objects loosen or disappear. What remains is often described as awareness without a clear center—sometimes as pure presence, unity, or simply “everything and nothing.”

It is not literal death, brain damage, or the clinical loss of personality. “Ego” here means the constructed sense of self (the ongoing story of who you are, what you want, and how you stand apart from everything else), not arrogance or vanity.

### Roots in spiritual traditions
The experience appears across many contemplative paths under different names:

- **Buddhism**: Realization of *anatta* (no-self). The five aggregates that make up ordinary experience have no permanent, independent core. Enlightenment involves seeing this directly rather than intellectually.
- **Hindu traditions** (especially Advaita Vedanta): Dissolution of *ahamkara* (the ego-principle or “I-maker”). The individual self (*atman*) is recognized as never having been separate from ultimate reality (*Brahman*).
- **Sufism**: *Fana* — annihilation of the self in preparation for union with the Divine (“Die before you die”).
- **Christian mysticism**: The “dark night of the soul” (St. John of the Cross), kenosis (self-emptying), and descriptions of the soul losing its ordinary identity so that divine life can inhabit it.
- **Other lineages**: Similar reports appear in shamanic traditions, Jewish Kabbalah, and various forms of intense meditation or religious ecstasy.

Carl Jung later described a related process of psychic death and reordering that could realign consciousness with a deeper self. Modern spiritual teachers often frame it as the temporary loss of identification with thoughts, roles, and the body so that something larger (or more fundamental) can be experienced.

### What it typically feels like
Accounts commonly include:
- Dissolution of the boundary between self and world
- Loss or radical alteration of personal history and time
- A sense of being “no one” and “everything” at once
- Profound peace, love, or awe—or, if resisted, intense fear and disorientation

The same loosening of self can feel liberating to one person and terrifying to another, often depending on preparation, context, and whether the experience is met with surrender or struggle.

### Common triggers
It can arise through:
- Deep or prolonged meditation (especially non-dual practices)
- Intense spiritual practice, fasting, or ritual
- Near-death experiences
- Major life crises or “dark nights”
- High-dose psychedelics (psilocybin, LSD, ayahuasca, etc.), which modern research often calls “ego dissolution”

Neuroscience links many of these states to reduced activity and connectivity in the brain’s default mode network (the system associated with self-referential thought, mind-wandering, and the ongoing sense of a stable “me”). Similar patterns appear in both deep meditation and psychedelic states.

### Relation to being “the conduit”
This is where the phrase “I am the conduit” often points. When the ego is less in the driver’s seat, there is less personal filtering, agenda, or resistance. What flows through—awareness, compassion, creativity, insight, or whatever a tradition calls grace or the divine—can move more freely. Many contemplative paths treat the ego not as an enemy to be permanently destroyed, but as a habitual contraction that can be relaxed so the person functions more as a clear channel than as a self-enclosed source.

### Important nuances and cautions
Most serious traditions do **not** treat permanent ego erasure as the goal. A functional sense of self is needed to navigate ordinary life, relationships, and responsibilities. The insight is usually about not *identifying* with the ego as the ultimate reality, rather than annihilating it forever.

Advaita Vedanta makes a profound claim: Our true self is Brahman, the ultimate reality. Divine consciousness exists within every human being.

Sounds beautiful. But does this philosophy have any practical impact on human behaviour?

When a politician steals public money, when a government officer demands a bribe from a poor citizen, or when the powerful exploit the helpless, where is this divine consciousness?

The standard response is that such people are trapped in ego, ignorance and Maya. And if they escape punishment in this life, karma will catch up with them in the next.

But isn’t this an extraordinarily convenient explanation? Every failure of divine justice is postponed to an invisible future that nobody can independently verify.

Meanwhile, corrupt individuals enjoy luxurious lives, while their victims struggle for survival.

Then comes the religious solution to wrongdoing: take a dip in the Ganges, perform a puja, donate to a temple and seek forgiveness.

But can a holy dip return stolen public money? Can a religious donation compensate a poor family exploited by a corrupt official? Can rituals undo the suffering caused by injustice?

Forgiveness may be religious. Accountability must be real.

Let’s look at what actually makes societies less corrupt. Countries with stronger institutions, transparency and rule of law generally perform better on corruption measures.

They don’t depend on the assumption that everyone has divine consciousness. They build systems where corruption is investigated, prosecuted and punished.

Strict laws, independent institutions, swift trials and certain punishment are far more practical deterrents than promises of divine justice.

And here is the fundamental problem with claiming that religion is necessary for morality:

An atheist can be honest without believing in God. A religious person can be dishonest despite worshipping God every day.

This does not make all religious people corrupt or all atheists virtuous. It simply proves that religious belief is neither necessary nor sufficient for moral behaviour.

So, to those who claim that God is the foundation of morality, I ask:

If divine consciousness cannot guarantee honesty, karma cannot provide demonstrable justice, and religious rituals cannot repair the damage caused by wrongdoing, why should religion be considered the foundation of a moral society?

A society doesn’t become moral by having more temples, more rituals or more believers. It becomes moral when people stop exploiting one another and institutions ensure that nobody is above the law.

Perhaps what humanity needs is less preaching about divine consciousness and more practice of human conscience.

MAHANADI COALFIELDS LTD IPO – DETAILED REVIEW 

₹9,001 Cr IPO | ₹90,010 Cr Market Cap

MY VERDICT: PERSONALLY AVOIDING FOR BOTH LISTING GAINS & LONG TERM.❌❌

Risk takers may apply for small listing gains, but expectations should remain limited

1. BUSINESS OVERVIEW

Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd (MCL) is a wholly owned subsidiary of Coal India Ltd.

✅ India's largest single coal-producing company in FY26.

✅ Contributes 21% of India's domestic coal production.

✅ Accounts for 28% of Coal India's total production.

✅ Operates 17 mines across Odisha:

- 14 opencast mines
- 3 underground mines

✅ Coal resources of 40.34 billion tonnes, representing 9.8% of India's total coal resources.

Revenue Mix (FY26):

- Raw coal: 97.4%
- Washed coal: 2.6%

Major customers include power generation companies, captive power plants, cement and sponge iron industries.

2. IPO DETAILS

Closing: 23 November 2026

Price Band: ₹129–₹136

Issue Size: ₹9,001 Cr

Minimum Investment: ₹14,960

Post-Issue Market Cap: ₹90,010 Cr

Fresh Issue: NIL

Offer for Sale: ₹9,001 Cr

3. FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE

Revenue (₹ Cr)

FY24: ₹31,634

FY25: ₹31,353

FY26: ₹30,550

1H FY27: ₹16,093

EBITDA (₹ Cr)

FY24: ₹14,681

FY25: ₹13,655

FY26: ₹12,735

1H FY27: ₹6,449

PAT (₹ Cr)

FY24: ₹11,841

FY25: ₹10,824

FY26: ₹10,678

1H FY27: ₹4,879

FY24–FY26 Revenue CAGR: -1.7%

FY24–FY26 PAT CAGR: -5.0%

4. VALUATION & PEER COMPARISON

At the upper price band of ₹136:

- Market Cap: ₹90,010 Cr
- FY26 P/E: 8.4x
- EV/EBITDA: 5.9x
- P/B: 4.2x
- ROE: 50.2%
- ROCE: 68.0%

Peer P/E Comparision:

Mahanadi Coalfields: 8.4x

NMDC: 8.1x

Bharat Coking Coal: 113.3x

Note: Bharat Coking Coal's P/E is distorted by its exceptionally low FY26 earnings, making it a weak valuation benchmark.

My View: Valuation looks fairly priced rather than deeply undervalued. I don't see a significant margin of safety at the IPO price.

5. KEY STRENGTHS

✅ India's largest single coal producer by production.

✅ Strong Coal India parentage.

✅ Low-cost mining operations supported by favourable geology.

✅ FY26 EBITDA margin of 41.7%.

✅ Strong ROE of 50.2% and ROCE of 68%.

✅ Negligible financial debt.

✅ FY26 operating cash flow of ₹12,478 Cr.

✅ FY26 free cash flow of ₹10,241 Cr.

✅ Cash and bank balances of ₹20,292 Cr as of 1H FY27.

✅ Plans to expand coal washery capacity from 10 million tonnes to 37 million tonnes annually.

6. KEY RISKS

❌ Declining Financial Performance

❌ Margin Compression

❌ High Dependence on Coal

97% of product sales come from raw coal.

69% of product sales depend on power generation customers.

❌ Contingent Liabilities

₹8,506 Cr as of FY26, approximately 40% of net worth.

❌ Contractor Dependence

Contractual expenses represented 22% of FY26 revenue.

❌ Energy Transition Risk

Increasing renewable energy adoption, environmental regulations and changing energy policies could affect long-term coal demand.

Why am I avoiding?

1. Revenue and PAT declined over FY24–FY26.
2. EBITDA margins are under pressure.
3. The IPO is entirely OFS.
4. Valuation doesn't offer enough margin of safety for my expectations.
5. Long-term growth potential appears relatively limited compared with my preferred investment opportunities.

I prefer businesses with stronger earnings growth potential and a better risk-reward profile.

Risk takers may consider applying for modest listing gains, but listing performance will depend on subscription demand and prevailing market sentiment.

DISCLAIMER: This is my personal analysis and investment view, not a buy/sell recommendation. I am not a SEBI-registered research analyst. Please conduct your own research before investing.

Aham Brahmasmi (Sanskrit: अहं ब्रह्मास्मि) translates to "I am Brahman" or "I am the infinite, divine consciousness". 

Word-by-Word Breakdown:- 

•Aham (अहं): Means "I" or the individual self.
•Brahma / Brahman (ब्रह्मन्): Refers to the ultimate, formless, and all-pervading reality or universal consciousness.

•Asmi (अस्मि): Means "am," establishing the identity or oneness between the two.

Origin and Context:-

•Source: It is one of the four principal Mahavakyas (Great Sayings) found in the ancient Hindu texts called the Upanishads, specifically from the Brihadaranyaka Upanishad of the Yajur Veda.

•Advaita Vedanta Philosophy: The phrase represents the core of non-dualism (Advaita). It signifies that the individual soul (Atman) is not separate from the universal reality (Brahman).

•True Meaning vs. Ego: It is not an egoistic claim that "I (the small personal ego) am God". Instead, it is a meditative realization that the deepest observer or pure consciousness inside every person is the same single consciousness that powers the entire universe.

Very Wrong Signal: Vedanta Chief Anil Agarwal Flays ONGC Takeover of Cambay Oilfield and Calls for Policy Stability; Vedanta Oil & Gas Commits $5 Billion to Scale Output to 300,000-500,000 Barrels Per Day

Core Theme 
Agarwal is using the Cambay dispute to argue that handing a producing field to state-run ONGC undermines investor confidence just as Vedanta pledges $5 billion to lift output from about 72,200 to as much as 500,000 barrels a day, with the division bench’s reserved judgment now the next key milestone.

The Statement: Policy Stability
Vedanta Group Chairman Anil Agarwal said on Tuesday that ONGC’s takeover of the company’s producing Cambay offshore block “will send a very wrong signal to investors” and called for policy stability in the country’s oil and gas sector

Agarwal, in a social media post: “Recently, our running field has been given to ONGC which will send a very wrong signal to investors. We are seeing such great energy and enthusiasm from global investors. This is the time to keep the policy hand steady and not disrupt any existing operator. That shall go a long way in building and boosting global investor confidence”

The remarks come amid an unresolved legal dispute over the Cambay block’s production-sharing contract

State-run ONGC took over the block from Vedanta in July following a Delhi High Court ruling; Vedanta has challenged the verdict before a division bench

The Dispute: Timeline
Vedanta held a 40% participating interest in the Cambay offshore block in Gujarat, with ONGC having 50% and Invenire Petrodyne the remaining 10%

The block’s production-sharing contract (PSC) expired on June 29, 2023

Vedanta and its partners had sought an extension in June 2021 under the government’s 2017 extension policy

The government rejected the request on September 19, 2025, directing the operator to hand over the block to ONGC

Vedanta challenged the decision before the Delhi High Court, but a single-judge bench dismissed its petition on July 22, 2026, vacating an interim stay

ONGC subsequently assumed control and applied for a petroleum lease on July 28

Vedanta appealed against the ruling before a division bench, where hearings have concluded and judgment has been reserved

Vedanta’s Investment Plans
Agarwal said Vedanta Oil and Gas, India’s largest private sector producer, is committing $5 billion to scale up production to 300,000-500,000 barrels per day, without specifying a timeline for achieving the target

The company’s average daily gross operated production stood at about 72,200 barrels of oil equivalent during the July-September quarter

Agarwal: “India is on the verge of something big in oil and gas,” comparing the country’s emerging hydrocarbon opportunity with Guyana’s position a decade ago

He also highlighted Vedanta’s participation in the deepwater Samudra Manthan programme

INDIA’S JAW-DROPPING $14.5 BILLION STEEL BET 
One planned complex. Enough annual capacity to exceed FRANCE’s entire 2025 crude steel output

India laid the foundation stone for a new steel complex in Andhra Pradesh in March 2026. AM/NS India plans to build it in two phases. If both are completed, the complex will have the capacity to make 17.8 million tonnes of crude steel a year.

Here’s how that compares with what three countries actually produced in 2025:
🇫🇷 France  9.9 million tonnes. The complex would have 1.8 times that capacity.
🇪🇸 Spain  11.8 million tonnes. That’s about 50% more than Spain produced.
🇹🇷 Türkiye  38.1 million tonnes. The complex’s capacity would equal 47% of Türkiye’s output.

Additionally, this complex alone would have the equivalent of 8% of India’s entire steelmaking capacity as of June 2026.

The two-phase project was announced at about $14.5 billion at the exchange rate on the day of the ceremony. The plans include a dedicated port and a pipeline connection for iron ore. The first phase accounts for 8.2 million tonnes of annual capacity, with primary steelmaking targeted for 2030–31.

India's output grew 10.4% that year, even as global production fell about 2%.

One detail worth watching. The first phase will use coal-based blast furnaces. A lower-emissions process is still an option for phase two, but no decision has been announced.
Sources: CRISIL Ratings, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel India, World Steel Association

Meet ESDS Software Solution Ltd.

It started as a simple web hosting company. Today, ESDS is trying to become a full-stack AI infrastructure player. And it wants to do it using India's surplus power to serve global AI labs.

First, what does ESDS actually sell? 

Think of it as one company that does three things for a customer's entire tech life.

🏗️ IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) Simply put: ESDS gives you the "land and building" for your tech.

- Colocation and data centers: you rent space and power to keep your servers.
- Cloud computing: you rent computing power instead of buying machines. It comes as public, private, hybrid and community clouds, including a Government cloud and an SAP HANA cloud.
- Newly launched GPU-as-a-Service (GPUaaS): you rent very powerful AI chips by the hour to train and run AI.

🛠️ Managed Services Simply put: ESDS becomes your IT team.

- 24/7 IT support
- Data backup and recovery
- Migration (moving you to the cloud)
- Database administration (including SAP Basis and HANA)
- Security operations center (SOC), meaning a team that watches for hackers

The Indian IT industry is finally showing positive signs with the Q2 FY27 results complete!

For almost 2 years, Indian IT was unloved, written off & underperforming. Down 44% from the Dec ‘24 peak, this was a fair understanding until the start of the current FY. 

The recovery is underway in FY27:

(1) AI is keeping growth alive: AI projects is ~10% of total revenue. AI revenue is growing 20% QoQ! BTW, FY27 industry growth is positive ONLY because of AI projects. If you were to look at non-AI revenue, it would be -1% growth.

(2) Hiring is back: After 3 quarters of reduction in overall headcount, FY27 has been 2 quarters of headcount addition. We’re back to Q1 FY26 headcount levels.

(3) Headcount growth is matched with higher utilization: For most Indian IT cos, the utilization rate (% of billable hours) is above the 5yr long term average. Cos like Tech M, Coforge & Hexaware are at their 5 yr highs! Higher utilization combined with positive headcount edition is a signal of demand for project work.

(4) Subcontracting of work has grown 4 quarters in a row (from ~8.77% of revenue in Q2 FY26 to ~9.74% of revenue in Q2 FY27). It is hard to pinpoint the underlying driver. But, it is a mix of outsourcing to AI specialist subcontractors (Indian IT is still building this talent) and outsourcing to local contractors (due to visa issues).

(5) Ways of working have changed: Coforge leads here with Momentuum AI (their FDE + AI agent pod structure which is live at client sites). Wipro is hiring FDEs. TCS is taking over Best Buy’s GCC. Outsourcing isn’t going anywhere 😉

Is India IT all clear? No. Change is constant. Investors will want to see another 4+ quarters of growing AI revenue (outpacing legacy biz decline), stable to growing utilization & reduction in outsourcing to truly declare “all is well”

Most investors who wrote off Indian IT assumed that a magical fairy with digital fangs would show up in Minnesota to get an old school life sciences company to use AI.

These investors conveniently forgot that 80% of the value lies in the 70% of “non-tech people & process work” which needs to be done at the last mile i.e. change management workshops, management team alignments, offline POC demos etc.

In 2008, Amazon founder Jeff Bezos said during a keynote address: “focus on what makes your beer taste insanely better”. This will remain true for most company's relationship with Technology & outsourcing to IT.

Bob from Minnesota doesn’t give 2 shits about Grok Bot, Instinct, Deepseek etc. He simply wants Bharat to show up and automate the crap out of his team’s manual tasks so that he can get home early to watch the Vikings with his son.

Until Optimus Prime shows up at your doorstep, Indian IT will have enough & more work to do.

The Petroleum Ministry has rewritten the rules for extending old oil and gas contracts. The gazette notification is dated 10 Nov and was published on 17 Nov.

It covers 22 small and medium fields run by private JVs, including Ravva, Kharsang, PY-1, Dholka and Cambay.

What changes:
• Extension can now run till the field's economic life, in blocks of up to 30 years
• Govt's profit petroleum share goes up 10 points in years 1-10 of the extension, 5 points in years 11-20 and 2.5 points in years 21-30
• Royalty and cess move to full nomination-regime rates, not the concessional PSC rates

So if the normal formula gives the government 20%, it takes 30% in the first decade.

My read: operators get something they never had, a clear runway to keep investing in mature fields. They pay for it with a thinner margin on every barrel.

The market liked the certainty first. HOEC was up about 5.5% this morning and is already up over 40% in a month. Vedanta Oil & Gas barely moved.

The fine print: extensions need a third-party reserves audit, a revised field plan and a 70% track record on wells or output. Operators who don't agree face rebidding, or the field can go to ONGC or OIL.

In 1962, a chemical factory and 16,000 people in Mithapur, Gujarat, went an entire week without drawing water from either of the 2 lakes they depended on.

The factory made soda ash, a raw material for glass, ceramics and textiles. Building it had already meant developing a process whose know how was closely guarded by a handful of companies abroad.

Darbari Seth, a chemical engineer and University of Cincinnati grad, had argued for a larger factory....

In 1957-58, when Tata Chemicals was considering foreign help to raise daily capacity from 80 tonnes to 200, he proposed designing the expansion themselves and aiming for 400 instead. Of the 16 board members, only JRD Tata initially backed him.

The team, with an average age of 29, took on the design, engineering, fabrication and installation. It was a whole chemical complex that had to work together, not a single machine.

Then the 1962 monsoon failed. The factory needed huge quantities of fresh water, and the lakes supplied the town too. By October, there was talk of evacuating Mithapur.

Seth's team began changing how the factory used water. They brought in seawater and treated it to replace fresh water in the process, while redesigning the system to reuse water. They also laid five and a half miles of pipes from wells to Mithapur's waterworks.

The company declared a "Lakeless Week". The factory and the town's 16,000 people went 7 days without taking water from the lakes. The plant's daily water requirement fell from 22 lakh gallons to 5 lakh.

By February 1990, Mithapur was Asia's largest inorganic chemical complex, Japan included. In 2025-26, Mithapur's chemical works recorded zero net freshwater withdrawal.

Sources: Gita Piramal, Illustrated Weekly, 4 February 1990; Tata Investment Corporation; Tata group histories.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) has the potential to drastically cut the time required to take a drug molecule from the lab to patients, compressing the current five-to-seven-year timeline into just one or two years, Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw of Biocon said .

Describing biology as the "most important frontier for AI to be deployed," she said AI will help simplify complex biological systems and allow scientists to "connect the dots" rather than studying one target at a time.

According to Shaw, converging genomics, chemical pathways, and neural networks through AI will enable next-generation drugs, next-generation diagnostics -- such as detecting the first cancer cell to overcome late-stage diagnosis -- as well as advancements in agriculture and bioenergy.

Vedanta Chairman Anil Agarwal has raised concerns over the transfer of a producing offshore oil & gas block to ONGC, warning that it could send the wrong signal to investors.

• The disputed Cambay offshore block was taken over by ONGC following a legal dispute.
• The matter remains under appeal.

📊 Why Does This Matter?

India needs higher domestic oil & gas production to reduce import dependence and strengthen energy security.

However, attracting long-term investment requires more than attractive opportunities. Investors also need regulatory clarity, contractual stability and predictable policies.

📈 Potential Market Impact:

ONGC, Vedanta, Oil India and oilfield services companies could remain in focus as India's domestic exploration and production ambitions evolve.

My Take:

India's energy ambitions require both strong public-sector participation and private investment.

The key is to ensure that contractual obligations, regulatory decisions and investor confidence move together.

Energy security is not just about finding more oil and gas. It is also about creating a policy environment that encourages long-term investment.

Aleister Crowley's remarkable identification of Thelema with Vedānta

One particularly revealing passage occurs in Liber II: The Message of the Master Therion.

Crowley explains that when an individual discovers and perfectly performs the True Will, that individual comes into harmony with the universal Will.

He concludes:

If thy will be God's will, Thou art That.

The final words are unmistakably reminiscent of the Upaniṣadic Tat Tvam Asi—"Thou art That."

In the same work, Crowley describes perfected Will as a form of Nirvāṇa, but dynamic rather than static. Hermetic Library

This is important because it establishes that Crowley was not merely proposing a philosophy of individual self-assertion.

He was proposing a spiritual discipline through which the individual could discover an identity or harmony with ultimate reality.

Nevertheless, his identification of individual and divine Will is not identical to Śaṅkara's doctrine of the absolute identity of Ātman and Brahman

Was Crowley's salvation a permanent state?

This is an especially interesting question.

Crowley distinguished temporary mystical experiences from stable initiatory attainments. A momentary experience of samādhi was not necessarily equivalent to the enduring transformation represented by an initiatory grade.

His system therefore presupposes that spiritual realization can become established rather than remaining an occasional extraordinary experience.

Yet Thelema also emphasizes the active expression of realization in ordinary existence. Liberation does not mean abandoning action or withdrawing permanently from the world.

In this respect, Crowley's ideal has something in common with the conception of jīvanmukti, liberation while living, although the two are not doctrinally equivalent.

Crowley's occult philosophy is fundamentally soteriological, but its salvation is conceived as spiritual realization rather than forgiveness of sins.

Its characteristic movement is:

Ordinary consciousness

Ignorance, divided desires, identification with personality

Discovery of True Will

Recognition of one's authentic spiritual direction

Knowledge and Conversation

Attainment of the Holy Guardian Angel

Crossing the Abyss

Surrender of the limiting personality

Supernal attainment

Transcendence of dualistic limitation and realization of higher spiritual grades

What I find especially significant from the perspective of comparative religious philosophy is that Crowley's system combines the Western Hermetic tradition of the Great Work with an explicitly liberation-oriented interpretation of Indian yoga and mysticism.

His magick is therefore not adequately characterized as the manipulation of occult forces for personal advantage. In its highest conception, it is a method of transforming the practitioner.

The distinction between magical power as an intermediate accomplishment and liberation from the limiting personality as a higher attainment is central to understanding Crowley's religious philosophy.

My detailed thoughts on NVDA's earnings and call:

1. Goldman asked NVIDIA how it would balance buybacks with financing its customers. Colette Kress answered: “The top priority is going to be our suppliers.” Fair enough. Let's look at what NVIDIA actually signed. Three months ago it had committed 87bn to supply and capacity for FY2028. By October that was 203bn for the same fiscal year. Across all years, commitments rose from 279bn to 390bn, principally to secure memory. Over the same quarter, its separately disclosed commitments under neocloud agreements fell from 36bn to 32bn. For all the attention paid to whom NVDA is financing, the biggest change was in what NVDA itself had to buy.

2. Put 203bn against the forecast. Nine-month revenue plus the 130bn Q4 midpoint gives roughly 424bn for FY2027. Kress raised expected FY2028 growth from 70% to 75% on that higher base. That implies about 741bn of sales. At management’s 72-73% gross margin outlook, the implied cost of those sales is 200–208bn. Procurement and cost recognition run on different schedules, so the resemblance is a measure of scale. NVIDIA has made supplier commitments for next year comparable to the entire annual cost of delivering its forecast. For anyone debating the durability of AI memory earnings, that is evidence from the buyer’s books.

3. The answer to TD Cowen explains why NVIDIA is willing to do it. When supply is scarce, Kress said customers get the same pricing. What influences who gets the racks is whether the building has power, the financing is in place and the customer can use the equipment in the quarter it ships. For customers below investment grade, NVIDIA also wants evidence that someone has contracted to buy the compute. Rubin generated nearly 20bn in its first production quarter. Hyperscalers brought it into production in about a month, half the time Grace Blackwell took. NVIDIA can grow sales by getting an existing buyer earning a month earlier. That is a source of growth a model driven solely by new AI demand will miss. 

4. There is a price for doing this, and it shows up next quarter. Q3 produced 115.8bn of revenue, 65.3bn of net income and 43.8bn of free cash flow. The 130bn Q4 guide looks like another 12% sequential revenue increase, but Q4 has 14 weeks against Q3’s 13. At the guided margin midpoint, gross profit per week goes from 6.67bn to 6.64bn. Essentially flat. Kress told UBS that NVIDIA was absorbing some component inflation to honour existing purchase orders ahead of new pricing. The same scarcity that gives NVIDIA the confidence to raise its sales forecast gives its suppliers bargaining power. 

5. The reaction was more discriminating than “blowout” headlines suggest. UBS had already anticipated a 130bn guide. Aptus highlighted the strength of the outlook with zero assumed China data-centre compute revenue. D.A. Davidson and Ocean Park focused on succession. Deepwater’s Gene Munster picked up the significance of 75% growth off a larger base. Bernstein’s downgrade preceded earnings. 

My read: 
Yesterday we asked where the semiconductor downturn was showing up in the business. NVIDIA just gave us an unusually good way to test it. Inventory rose by 8.1bn, yet finished goods fell by 700m. Raw materials and work in process accounted for the increase. Today the company is accumulating the inputs it needs to build systems and drawing down the stock it has finished. The figure I’d watch alongside that is collection time, already up from 45 days to 60 to 64 over three quarters. If finished systems start piling up while customers take longer to pay, the bears will have an operating case. Right now, the world’s largest buyer of AI memory has more than doubled its commitments for next year, and the argument for a downturn has to explain why that buyer is wrong. And maybe have a stab at the 3 handles on forward PEs for MU and SNDK whilst at it.

*The AI Trio of India: Netweb vs E2E vs ESDS*

All 3 are called "AI stocks" but they sell completely different things. Don't buy them as one basket.

Here's the breakdown 🧵

*1/ NETWEB - The Seller*

Sells the box.
Makes AI servers / HPC systems for Govt, Neoclouds, Enterprises.

Q2 FY27:
Revenue: ₹1,323 Cr (+336% YoY)
PAT: ₹137 Cr (+335% YoY)
EBITDA margin: 14.9%
PAT margin: 10.2%

Order Book: ₹2,629 Cr + L1 ₹653 Cr + Pipeline ₹11,152 Cr

Valuation: ~₹24,800 Cr mkt cap, ∼66x PE
Balance Sheet: Net cash, QIP ₹1,200 Cr done. Cleanest of the 3.

Risk: Lumpy orders, Govt dependence, only 15% margin.
Strength: Scale + execution proven. H1 PAT already > full FY26 PAT.

In one line: Biggest, most proven, but low margin.

*2/ E2E NETWORKS - The Landlord*

Rents the box.
GPU-as-a-Service, rents NVIDIA GPUs by the hour.

Q2 FY27:
Revenue: ₹224 Cr (+411% YoY)
PAT: ₹73 Cr (vs loss last year)
EBITDA margin: 76.6% - highest
PAT margin: 32.5%

Order Book: ~₹1,000 Cr Sovereign AI deal till Jun-29

Valuation: ~₹10,600 Cr mkt cap, ∼90-160x TTM PE - meaningless, earnings just turned.
Balance Sheet: Debt ₹450 Cr, up from ₹103 Cr. Capex heavy.

Risk: Utilisation risk, GPU price crash, depreciation eats PAT. ROE only ∼6.5% despite 76% margin.
Strength: Operating leverage. Every extra GPU = almost pure profit.

In one line: Highest margin, highest leverage, highest risk.

*3/ ESDS - The Option Bet*

Sells cloud + services.
Own data centres, cloud, managed services, SaaS + GPUaaS.

Q2 FY27:
Revenue: ₹138 Cr (+48% YoY)
PAT: ₹31 Cr (+41% YoY)
EBITDA margin: 41.8%
PAT margin: 22.5%

Balance Sheet: IPO ₹720 Cr, ₹673 Cr still unused. Debt low.

Risk: Single-customer risk. SharonAI = 4.5x its current annual revenue. If delayed, stock collapses.
Strength: Diversified, sticky. 86.7% revenue from existing customers. 2,545 customers.

In one line: Smallest base today, but revenue can 5x in 1 year if deal bills.

Netweb = Execution
E2E = Leverage
ESDS = Lottery ticket on one contract

In 1962, a chemical factory and 16,000 people in Mithapur, Gujarat, went an entire week without drawing water from either of the 2 lakes they depended on.

The factory made soda ash, a raw material for glass, ceramics and textiles. Building it had already meant developing a process whose know how was closely guarded by a handful of companies abroad.

Darbari Seth, a chemical engineer and University of Cincinnati grad, had argued for a larger factory....

In 1957-58, when Tata Chemicals was considering foreign help to raise daily capacity from 80 tonnes to 200, he proposed designing the expansion themselves and aiming for 400 instead. Of the 16 board members, only JRD Tata initially backed him.

The team, with an average age of 29, took on the design, engineering, fabrication and installation. It was a whole chemical complex that had to work together, not a single machine.

Then the 1962 monsoon failed. The factory needed huge quantities of fresh water, and the lakes supplied the town too. By October, there was talk of evacuating Mithapur.

Seth's team began changing how the factory used water. They brought in seawater and treated it to replace fresh water in the process, while redesigning the system to reuse water. They also laid five and a half miles of pipes from wells to Mithapur's waterworks.

The company declared a "Lakeless Week". The factory and the town's 16,000 people went 7 days without taking water from the lakes. The plant's daily water requirement fell from 22 lakh gallons to 5 lakh.

By February 1990, Mithapur was Asia's largest inorganic chemical complex, Japan included. In 2025-26, Mithapur's chemical works recorded zero net freshwater withdrawal.

Sources: Gita Piramal, Illustrated Weekly, 4 February 1990; Tata Investment Corporation; Tata group histories.

CLSA on Coforge
High Conviction O-P TP Rs 2522
Conf takeaways
Revenue synergies from Encora will start accruing from 3QFY27, with Encora’s growth being at par with Coforge’s standalone entity.
One of its largest deals in the pipeline currently is with Encora’s hitech vertical client.
Around Encora, its strategy remains on improving the go-to-market and focusing on client mining.
Key consideration areas of any potential acquisitions will be to strengthen delivery presence in the EU and to acquire new client logos.

JPM on Tech Mahindra
OW. TP Rs 1900
Management meet  Key takeaways
1) Growth recovery has been driven by consistently winning large deals (net new TCV of $1bn for four consecutive quarters) as well as investments in sales and AI teams.
2) TechM is on track to achieve FY27 (revenue and margin) targets with focus shifting to accelerating revenue growth while margin expansion would be more gradual.
3) It sees further scope for margin expansion driven by scope to improve Fixed price project margins, decreasing subcontractors, employee pyramid correction, and tailwinds from AI productivity.
4) It is open now to restarting the M&A engine.

CLSA on HCL Tech
Conf takeaways
Hold, TP Rs 1094
HCLT offers a wide variety of AI services given its portfolio of offerings including services, software, ER&D, datacentre investment plans and investment in India’s sovereign AI unicorn Sarvam. HCLT is seeing a net deflation of 2%-3% annually with c.55% of its overall business more prone to AI deflation.
It expects non-linearity between revenue growth and headcount growth to continue.
Advanced AI revenue for HCLT offer higher than company average margins.

CLSA on JSW Steel
O-p, TP Rs 1500
Conf takeaways
Management highlighted its sizeable capacity expansion pipeline and strong volume growth outlook (c.13.5 Cagr through FY32).
It targets Rs2,000/t of structural cost savings over the next three years, driven by greater raw-material integration and logistics efficiency.
Leverage remains comfortable despite a sizeable Capex programme.
Elevated Chinese exports remain a key industry debate, & management believes the anti-dumping duty (ADD) could offer long-term protection.

CLSA on Havells
O-P, TP Rs 1290
Conf takeaways
Management focus is now on core businesses of switches/switchgears, cables & wires (C&W), electrical consumer durables (ECD), and new businesses (rooftop solar) in addition to large appliances entity Lloyd.
It has taken adequate price increase to largely offset commodity pressures, while the recent correction in input costs is likely to reflect in back half of 4Q earnings, if this sustains.
It expects double-digit growth across segments over medium term, with a steady growth in fans to be offset by other fast-growing segments in ECD.
Similar to other C&W companies, it also indicated signs of destocking given fall in copper prices

CLSA on RR Kabel
O-P, TP Rs 2815
Conf takeaways
RR Kabel indicated industry demand has been moderate in 3Q so far.
While October was strong (given a low base due to festivities last year), November/December comps are higher, and the copper price correction has led to a gradual destocking.
Its medium-term growth drivers remain intact, with a richer cable mix, cost initiatives and backward integration to support margins.
Calibrated capacity additions and exports provide meaningful growth headroom.
It maintained its guidance for 14-15% volume growth and 9.5% margin and FMEG breakeven for FY27.
Strong brand/distribution and dealer relationships should limit disruption, while improving FMEG profitability provides an additional earnings lever.

CLSA on L&T
O-P, TP Rs 4842
L&T remains optimistic about a pickup in execution in 2HFY27, supported by its record backlog, while strong order momentum could drive inflows above its FY27 guidance
See multiple growth engines: an own-IP-led electronics platform across power electronics, EVs and industrial automation; a 10-fold expansion in AI-factory and datacentre capacity; and a broadening energy-security capex cycle in India spanning thermal, nuclear, renewables and new energy.
L&T has already confirmed its first major wins in these new businesses, including a US$1.4bn Nvidia AI-factory and the 500k Make in India EV motor.
Together, these initiatives should expand L&T’s addressable market, diversify its growth drivers and strengthen its position across high-growth infrastructure and technology verticals.

Poslední popravený odbojář 

Vladivoj Tomek, popravený 17. listopadu 1960 v pankrácké věznici, byl poslední osobou, kterou komunistický režim odsoudil k trestu smrti a popravil z politických důvodů.

Tomek vedl odbojovou skupinu nazvanou Othello, jejímž hlavním cílem bylo svržení komunistické vlády. Boj proti režimu vedl různými způsoby: vytvářel a šířil protikomunistické letáky a karikatury, které zesměšňovaly přední činitele Československa a Sovětského svazu. 

Skupina Othello měla ambiciózní plány, které zahrnovaly atentáty na politické představitele, výrobu a distribuci propagačních materiálů, shánění zbraní a v konečné fázi ozbrojené povstání.

Jejich nejznámější akcí se stalo přepadení ozbrojené vojenské hlídky v Praze-Strašnicích v prosinci roku 1952. Cílem přepadu, který Tomek provedl se třemi dalšími mladíky v ulici Nad Vodovodem, bylo získání samopalů a další munice. Situace se však vymkla kontrole a došlo k intenzivní přestřelce. Výsledkem bylo zranění dvou vojáků a smrt jednoho z nich.

Po tomto incidentu Tomkova skupina na několik let ustoupila od násilných akcí a soustředila se na méně nápadné formy odporu. I přes tuto změnu taktiky se StB nakonec dostala na jejich stopu a členy skupiny zatkla. Následný soudní proces vynesl rozsudek trestu smrti pro Vladivoje Tomka, zatímco jeho spolubojovníci byli odsouzeni k trestům odnětí svobody v rozmezí dvou až pětadvaceti let.

Andrej Babiš chce další protivzdušnou obranu co nejdřív, ne až v roce 2030, a armáda má po návratu z Izraele rychle rozhodnout, co si pořídí. Konkrétní harmonogram neoznámil, ministr obrany mezitím připomíná běžné dodací lhůty čtyři až šest let. Výborně, můžeme svolat steering committee. V naší pomyslné poradě se nejdřív vyhodí roadmapa, protože ji připravovali lidé, kteří ještě neznali dnešní strategickou vizi. Pipeline a dohodnuté milníky si strčte do prdele, máme nový leadership alignment. Product owner dostane ownership za něco, co před minutou přislíbil někdo jiný, procurement má okamžitě zajistit time to market a risk manager může rizika eskalovat rovnou do skartovačky. Jediné závazné KPI je, aby šéf vypadal, že už to zařídil. Jestli výrobce potřebuje šest let, měl si holt lépe prioritizovat backlog. My jsme si doteď naivně mysleli, že protivzdušná obrana vzniká objednávkou, výrobou, výcvikem a integrací. Jenže skutečný korporátní vizionář potřebuje hlavně buy-in a mikrofon. Ostatní korporace by samozřejmě byly strategickými partnery, dokud by nepřekážely expanzi hlavního impéria. My bychom v tom domácím datadisku dostali Honzu Tleskače Stříbroruku, který přijede na kole s atomovkou a požadavkem na zásadní změnu korporátní kultury. Jenže než stihne slézt, management mu přidělí nový deliverable, přesune scope a vezme mu zadní kolo kvůli optimalizaci nákladů. Honza se může posrat, ale prezentace musí zůstat zelená. Tak šlapej, Stříbroruko. Že nemáš na čem, to je problém implementace. Šéf právě oznámil, že už létáš.

Ukrajinský útok na Krymský most byl úmyslně naplánován tak, aby ztrapnil Vladimira Putina před jeho setkáním s Donaldem Trumpem a Si Ťin-pchingem ve čtvrtek 19. listopadu. Informoval o tom britský deník The Times s odvoláním na ukrajinského důstojníka, který se operace zúčastnil.

„Plánovali jsme to jako symbolické gesto před setkáním Trumpa, Putina a Si Ťin-pchinga, abychom ukázali, že Putin je slabý,“ uvedl.

Podle vojenského důstojníka měla operace i další důležitý cíl: demonstrovat, že Ukrajina je schopna provádět takové přesné údery bez použití amerických satelitních systémů Starlink a Starshield. To je obzvláště důležité vzhledem k nedávným americkým omezením jejich používání ukrajinskou armádou.

„Američané se snažili paralyzovat naši komunikaci nezbytnou pro takové operace, ale tato mise dokázala, že si dokážeme vytvořit vlastní komunikační systémy pro přenos rádiových signálů. Poprvé v historii jsme všechny tyto drony použili k přenosu video signálů do raket, aby mohly zasáhnout konkrétní body na mostě. Ukázali jsme, že jsme schopni provádět takové operace bez Starlinku,“ uvedl ukrajinský důstojník.

Úder vedl ke zřícení 227 metrů dlouhého centrálního pole automobilové části mostu. Trosky skončily ve vodě a zablokovaly přepravní kanál mezi Azovským a Černým mořem. Podle publikace to také vážně zkomplikuje zásobování ruských námořních sil v okupovaných přístavech Mariupol a Berďansk.

„Rusové léta přesvědčovali celý svět, že Krymský most je jednou z nejbezpečnějších konstrukcí na planetě. Dnes jeho části leží na mořském dně,“ uvedl zástupce SBU.

Kreml již slíbil, že konstrukci obnoví. Ukrajinský důstojník však varoval, že ukrajinské ozbrojené síly hodlají zaměřit útoky i na opravářské čety, což by v blížící se zimě mohlo rekonstrukci mostů prakticky znemožnit.

हिंदू धर्म द्रौपदी के चीरहरण के बाद कुरुक्षेत्र के युद्ध में गीता के उपदेश का धर्म है 

हिंदू धर्म वो धर्म है जहाँ देवताओं ने मिलकर शक्ति स्वरूप दुर्गा से महिषासुर के नाश का अनुरोध किया

हिंदू धर्म में माँ लक्ष्मी विष्णू के चौथे अवतार नरसिंह की गोद में बैठती हैं 

इसीलिए हिंदू धर्म को समझने वाले और उसमें आस्था रखने वाले हिंदू शक्ति स्वरूप महिला का सम्मान करते हैं 

असली हिंदू पति पत्नी के प्रेम, उनके परस्पर विश्वास और उनके आपसी सामीप्य को समझते हैं

📌 H1 FY27 Performance & Segment Mix Drivers:

• End-Market Surge (H1): Consumer (+46.2% YoY), Aerospace (+31.5% YoY), Medical (+22.7% YoY), Automotive (+19.4% YoY), and Defence (+19.3% YoY) drove structural mix upgrade

🎯 Full-Year Guidance, Return Ratios & Balance Sheet Monitorables:

• FY27 Guidance & Margin Normalization: Management set full-year FY27 targets of ₹5,000 Cr revenue and ₹850 Cr PAT (noting expectations to outperform), while flagging a normalized EBITDA margin corridor of 20–25% and PAT margin of 13–18% as Q1/Q2 benefited from lumpy tooling income and high defence/medical mix.

1. Structural Margin & Profit Inflection: Consolidated Q2 PAT doubled YoY to ₹215.19 Cr (+100% YoY) as revenue mix shifted heavily toward high-margin Aerospace (+31.5%), Medical (+22.7%), and Defence (+19.3%) alongside lower post-IPO finance costs.

2. Sequential Normalization Is Built In: While Q2 EBITDA (₹393.69 Cr) and PAT (₹215.19 Cr) dipped sequentially against a Q1 peak boosted by one-off tooling revenues, H1 EBITDA margins at 32.0% remain well above management's steady-state 20–25% guidance band.

3. Inventory Build vs. H2 Cash Conversion: With H1 revenue at ₹2,490.6 Cr (~50% of the ₹5,000 Cr full-year target) and H1 PAT at ₹455.3 Cr (~54% of the ₹850 Cr target), executing against the 441-day inventory buildup in H2 will be critical to restoring 90%+ CFO/EBITDA conversion.

Tata Technologies: an engineering-services company in the middle of a reset

1. What it does to make money
Tata Technologies is paid by manufacturers (mostly carmakers) to design, engineer and build their products, and to run the software that supports that work. Revenue splits into two segments in Q2 FY27:
a. Services (80% of revenue, ~30% gross margin): ER&D and embedded software
Engineers billed to clients on projects, from a single component to a complete vehicle. Within services, automotive is 80% and non-automotive (aerospace, heavy machinery, others) is 20%. Delivery is 35% offshore and 65% onshore, since onshore work is billed at higher rates but at lower margin. 
b. Technology Solutions (20%, ~19% gross margin): software, education, PLM
Resale and implementation of product-lifecycle software, plus education and skilling projects. It is lumpier: it fell 6.7% sequentially in Q2 on education timing.

2. Aerospace: revenue impact and visibility
Management calls aerospace the “second growth engine” after auto, says it is growing faster than auto.
Aerospace revenue is not disclosed.
The CEO said most aerospace programmes run 8–10 years, compared with a vehicle development cycle of a few years. Airbus has publicly said it will launch a next-generation single-aisle aircraft, the first new programme in about a decade; Tata Technologies expects to benefit from its incumbency.

3. Q2 FY27 results and consistency
Revenue :  +28.4% YoY, +2.1% QoQ
For two years to Dec 2025, revenue hovered at ₹1,244–1,366 Cr, with YoY growth between −2% and +4%. Growth then jumped to +22%, +34% and +28%, helped by the ES-Tec acquisition
Net income :  +3.6% YoY (₹166 Cr)
Profit grew far slower than sales as depreciation and lease interest rose.
Margins are stable but below the old peak: 16.1% against about 18% in FY24–FY25. A 100 bps wage-hike headwind was absorbed, but subcontracting costs also rose, which the CFO said should fall as permanent hires replace them.

4. Guidance given
FY27 revenue : “Strong double-digit” growth, reiterated; no number
Margins : Sequential improvement in Q3 and Q4, even though Q3 is seasonally soft; 18–20% described as the “North Star” with no date
H2 drivers : Large programmes ramping, including the $138 Mn win; product business to recover in Q3
Headwinds flagged : ES-Tec softness in Q3, education projects delayed, stabilisation expected in 2027
Medium term “Strong double-digit” for several years; 20%+ is increasingly hard, with capability and AI investment the constraint

The bull case
Large full-vehicle wins are scaling, management reports a strong pipeline, the BMW JV is ahead of plan, aerospace gives longer visibility, and there is Tata Group backing plus a high dividend payout (87% in FY26). If margins move toward 18%+ on 25% growth, profit growth catches up with revenue.

The bear case
At 41× earnings and 7× book, a lot is priced in while PAT is flat. 
Growth is recent and partly acquired, the German auto exposure is weak, the margin “North Star” has no date.
Anchor clients are concentrated in the Tata Motors group. 
Cyclical auto R&D budgets and AI-driven pricing pressure on engineering hours are industry risks.

Rentomojo Ltd - Q2 FY27 Concall Summary

Revenue Grew 52%;  Live Subscribers Grew 42%, with 43% Expansion in Stores and Warehouse Capacity, ₹690 Cr Contractual Revenue and 40-50% Growth Ambition, Supported by Rising Rental Penetration

1.  Financials (Consolidated)

Q2 revenue +52% YoY; +12.5% QoQ 
Normalised EBITDA ~₹58.8 Cr (₹38 Cr last year); 
+52% YoY; +12.6% QoQ
Reported EBITDA +53% YoY; +44% QoQ (Q1 ~₹40 Cr after fire loss)

Q2 one-offs: gratuity and leave liability reversal ~₹1.2 Cr; IPO expense ~₹0.8 Cr
Normalised PAT ~₹24 Cr (₹15.7 Cr last year); +9.4% QoQ
Reported PAT down 62% YoY (last year's ₹48 Cr included ~₹33 Cr deferred tax asset) and up 132% QoQ
Q1 reported PAT ₹7.8 Cr vs normalised ~₹22 Cr (fire ~₹11 Cr, deferred tax ~₹2.7 Cr)
ROCE and ROE slightly lower after IPO; still above the 20% aspiration

2.  Business Performance

Purchase value displaced ~₹450 Cr in Q2 (+60% YoY); ~₹850 Cr in H1
Items ordered ~3.8 lakh in Q2 (+45% YoY); ~7 lakh in H1
Live subscribers +42%; live items +44%
Warehouse capacity +51%; store count +43%
Revenue per item +4.65% QoQ; +6% H1; items per user ~2.8; occupancy 83-87%

Website traffic +~50%; 'Rento' keyword searches +~66% (industry keyword +20-25%)
Growth broad-based across categories; water purifiers and air purifiers added (no selling, rental only)
Seven new experience stores in Q2 (Delhi, Mumbai, Pune)

Core cities ~90-91% of revenue; new cities perform well but contribute less
Free relocation is a key differentiator
Average customer life ~18 months (16 earlier)
Growth rates: 35% to 40% to 45% to 50% (Q1) to 52% (Q2)

3.  Order Book & Demand

Contractual revenue ~₹690 Cr at end of Q2
Business starts each quarter with an existing subscriber base
~4.8 crore rental apartments; ~3.8 crore addressable
Only 10-15% of rentals are furnished (Vietnam: 40-50%)
Industry rental households ~15-20 lakh so far
Awareness is the main constraint; marketing spend stable as share of revenue
Competition: market largely a duopoly; Rentomojo is larger
NCLT matter: hearing in December; no further comment

4.  Capacity & Capex

H1 capex ~₹190 Cr (FY26 full year ~₹175 Cr); capex growth ~140%
Capex front-loaded; occupancy rose from 83% to 86%
AC capex is 3-4x normal in April-July season
Gross block ₹529 Cr to ~₹702 Cr; net fixed assets ₹426 Cr to ₹565 Cr
Run-rate suggests about double H1 for the year (management hint)
Capex growth faster than revenue growth
Implied value per item ~₹11,700 (₹10,600 a year ago): mix and AC

5.  Balance Sheet & Cash Flow

IPO proceeds ~₹150 Cr
Debt ₹187 Cr to ~₹230 Cr; net debt ~₹130 Cr
Funding waterfall: internal accruals first, then debt, then free cash flow focus
Marginal cost of debt ~8.6%; long-term debt from large banks
Rated by CRISIL; revised rating process started
Negative working capital business
Comfortable up to ~1x debt-to-equity if growth requires

6.  Margins & Costs

EBITDA margin ~40-41% on normalised basis
Costs linked to items deployed, revenue is cumulative
H1 deploys more items, so H2 margins are historically better (H1 ~40-41%, H2 ~42-43% last year)
Marketing is a stable share of other expenses
Buffer exists to trim experience investment if needed
Cost of funds less critical than occupancy and useful life

7.  Guidance & Outlook

FY27 PBT indicated ~₹90-95 Cr; no item-per-user growth built in
No revenue guidance; growth aspiration 40-50%+
Aims for ROCE above 20% while growing faster
Stronger H2 profit and cash flow historically
Ambition to grow aggressively; depth in core cities

8.  Key Risks

NCLT matter
Reported profit volatility from one-offs
Rising capex and debt
Seasonality in AC capex and revenue per item
Competition from furniture and appliance rentals and online
Customer awareness and acquisition cost

India's AI champion just opened a shop. Most of what it sells is Chinese.

So is Sarvam really India's answer to AI? Let's look.

Sarvam is a Bengaluru AI startup. In April 2025, it was the first company the government picked to build India's own AI model. The government now pays its full chip bill: ₹246.72 crore ($26.4M) for 4,096 NVIDIA chips.

On 16 Nov, Sarvam opened Token Factory. Think of it as an AI shop. Companies send in text, get AI answers back, pay in rupees, and their data stays in India.

The shop has 7 chat models. Only 1 is Sarvam's own. Five are Chinese, including DeepSeek. One is Google's.

So how good is Sarvam's own model? Artificial Analysis, an independent tester, scored it 18 at launch. A similar-sized free model from OpenAI scored 33. Sarvam shines in Indian languages and voice. But it's not close to the top labs.

Now the money. Sarvam has raised about $341M (₹3,190 crore). Backers include Lightspeed, Peak XV, Khosla, HCLTech, Bessemer, and NVIDIA. It's valued at $1.5B.

Its revenue last year? ₹45.1 crore ($4.8M), unaudited. So it's valued at about 311 times revenue. OpenAI is valued at about 25 times its revenue run rate (reported).

And the shop isn't the cheapest. E2E Networks (@e2enetworks), an Indian cloud company, sells the same DeepSeek model for ₹4.2 per million tokens in. Sarvam charges ₹14.

Token Factory keeps the data at home. But most of the intelligence on its shelves is still imported.

My read: Sarvam isn't India's OpenAI yet. Today it's India's AI landlord. That pays the bills. The real test is whether its own models get good enough to fill the shelves.

•Wagon deliveries increased to 1,106 units; foundry production reached 6,468 MT.
•Management expects stronger execution and profitability in H2 FY27.

Order Book & Revenue Visibility
•Total order book ~₹11,000–11,500 Cr, including ~₹8,000 Cr freight rolling stock and ₹3,000–3,500 Cr other businesses.
•~54% of order book comprises exports versus 9% YoY, supporting potential margin improvement.
•Private and export orders account for ~80–85% of the freight order portfolio, reducing dependence on Indian Railways.
•Rolling stock orders provide execution visibility over approximately 10 quarters.

Exports – Major Growth Driver
•South African wagon orders ~₹4,000 Cr, alongside ~₹1,300 Cr locomotive orders.
•South African contract revenue expected from FY28 onwards, with deliveries extending into FY29.
•Long-term maintenance obligations provide additional recurring revenue opportunities.
•Export contracts carry better margins than conventional domestic railway orders.

Rail Infrastructure & Electrical Business
•Rail infrastructure revenue grew ~41–42% QoQ; electrical infrastructure ~38% QoQ.
•Electrical business approaching ₹250 Cr quarterly revenue, with potential to reach ₹1,000 Cr annual run rate.
•Electrical order backlog ~₹1,600 Cr, executable over FY27 and FY28.
•Legacy EPC issues largely addressed; infrastructure business returning to profitability.

Foundry & Railway Adjacencies
•Foundry capacity expanded to 60,000 MT annually, with no immediate capacity constraints.
•Management indicated potential dispatches of ~35,000–40,000 MT, with 25–30% exports.
•Wheel manufacturing JV, NYMWAG rolling stock JV and RVNL partnership provide future diversification opportunities, though commercial ramp-up timelines remain uncertain.

Margins, CapEx & Balance Sheet
•Higher-margin exports, operational efficiencies and cost reductions expected to support margin expansion.
•~₹200 Cr CapEx initially earmarked for growth initiatives; core wagon business requires limited incremental CapEx.
•Debt declining sequentially; management expects near-term CapEx to be funded through internal accruals.
•CRISIL long-term credit rating upgraded to A+.

Long-Term Growth Ambition
•Texmaco 2.0 targets ₹9,000–10,000 Cr annual revenue by FY30.
•Core railway businesses targeted to contribute ₹4,000–5,000 Cr, with ₹5,000–6,000 Cr from adjacencies and diversification.
•Potential expansion into passenger rail components, wheels, defense and renewable energy.

Key Takeaway
•Strong multi-year revenue visibility from export-heavy order book, South African contracts and expanding electrical infrastructure business.
•Major earnings trigger: Higher export execution from FY28, improving product mix and operating leverage.
•Key monitorables: H2 execution recovery, South African project ramp-up, margin sustainability and clarity on the earlier ~₹700 Cr risk-related provision.

It's officially Nvidia's earnings day.

Today's earnings report and call will likely be the most watched earnings event in history.

We are watching two key things:

1. Do executives show any willingness to reinstate Jensen Huang

2. What has CHANGED from a business perspective

As of now, considering the information over the last 48 hours, we believe there is an <20% chance that Jensen returns.

Any indication that the probability is higher would be strongly bullish for the stock.

But, if not, then what has changed for Nvidia? With or without Jensen, this company remains one of the best businesses in the world.

We are looking to see if the company still expects revenue growth of 70%+ in FY2028, as management previously indicated.

We also look for any changes to AI infrastructure spending, demand for Blackwell and Vera Rubin chips, and the company's relationships with its largest customers.

If the fundamental outlook remains intact, then investors must ask: Does Jensen Huang's departure justify the -$750 billion in lost market cap?

We believe the market has already priced in a significant portion of the uncertainty surrounding Jensen's departure.

At the same time, the long-term AI infrastructure investment cycle remains intact, and Nvidia continues to sit at the center of it.

The burden is now on management to demonstrate that the business can continue executing at the same level without Jensen Huang.

More to come after earnings.

PVR INOX Limited · Credit Rating- Revision

Crisil Ratings revised the outlook on PVR INOX's long-term bank facilities and NCDs to 'Positive' from 'Stable', reaffirmed the rating at 'Crisil AA', and reaffirmed the short-term facilities and ₹200 crore commercial paper at 'Crisil A1+'.
The filing to NSE and BSE is signed by Murlee Manohar Jain, SVP- Company Secretary & Compliance Officer.
Crisil Ratings says net debt went from around ₹1,430 crore in fiscal 2023 to a net cash position of around ₹141 crore at the end of first half of fiscal 2027, aided by the sale of the 4700BC business for about ₹227 crore in January 2026.
Per Crisil Ratings, that net cash position comes after the company completed a ₹300 crore maiden share buyback in the first half of fiscal 2027.
Crisil Ratings puts fiscal 2026 revenue up ~17% to ₹6,646 crore, with average ticket price at ₹280 and spend per head at ₹147.
Crisil Ratings notes 192 underperforming screens were closed in the three fiscals through 2026, and headcount per screen fell from ~17.7 in fiscal 2020 to 12.1 in fiscal 2026.

Billionbrains Garage Ventures Ltd (GROWW)

#Q2FY27 #Nifty #GROWW

Groww Focuses on Cost Efficiency, Risk Controls, and Product Deepening 💡🛡️

A deep dive into their Q2 FY27 Concall ⬇️

Billionbrains Garage Ventures (Groww) detailed a divergence in its "Cost to Grow" and "Cost to Serve" frameworks for Q2 FY27, alongside anticipating a swift normalization of the CAS regulatory impact. The company also emphasized ongoing scaling of Margin Trade Funding (MTF) and other lending products.

Management highlighted significant tightening of risk controls post-prior quarter issues, a focus on competitive positioning, and iterative development of new products like derivatives "power trader" and US stocks. They reiterated a customer-first approach amidst competitive market dynamics.

🔹 Outlook & Guidance 🎯💡
    - CAS impact is expected to fade quickly once effective, with no structural impairment to derivatives anticipated.
    - Growth spend remains discretionary, flexible within an annual band of ₹400-500 crore based on market demand.
    - MTF book expects continued growth, averaging a quarterly build of ₹600-700 crore due to perceived underpenetration.
    - Management is awaiting the final UPI MDR framework and aims to avoid a material cost impact, intending to engage regulators.

🔹 Q2 Performance Highlights 📊💰
    - "Cost to Grow" fell sharply QoQ, primarily due to the absence of IPL branding expenditures.
    - "Cost to Serve" rose QoQ due to new AI-related costs, higher compute usage from more trading days, and a one-time operational penalty of ₹10-13 crore.
    - Brokerage revenue for F&O/commodities is order-linked (₹20 per order), not turnover-linked, allowing decoupling from ADTV.
    - Other operating income was boosted by heavy IPO activity (around 30 IPOs) and BSDA accruals, following a reclassification.
    - Employee expenses saw a QoQ decline, attributed to short-term headcount movements, with a structural expectation for costs to rise.

🔹 Management Tone & Strategy 🧭🛡️
    - Significant policy changes and real-time execution were implemented for risk management post-prior quarter issues, including industry-wide leverage monitoring.
    - Loan Against Shares (LAS) and personal loans, launched recently, are showing good traction and gradual growth.
    - The "915" web-based trading platform for "power traders" is not yet a significant contributor but aims to win market share from competitors.
    - US stocks platform is in very early beta testing with positive feedback, but no firm general availability timeline has been committed.
    - Groww maintains a customer-first pricing philosophy, focusing on delivering value over directly following competitive fee cuts.
    - More than 50% of customers are using over two products, reflecting a focus on need-driven product adoption rather than forced cross-selling.

Indo-MIM: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

A steady quarter, in line with Q1. Aerospace, consumer and automotive grew well, while the electronics business is running below last year, as expected.

Q2 Revenue: ₹1,271 Cr (vs ₹1,218 Cr in Q1)
Q2 PBT before exceptional items: ₹309 Cr (vs ₹325 Cr in Q1)
H1 Revenue: ₹2,490 Cr (up ₹263 Cr YoY, about +12%)
H1 PAT: ₹455 Cr (roughly flat YoY excluding exceptional items)
ROCE: 36.5% | ROE: 26.3% | Debt-to-equity: 0.27
Total debt: ₹941 Cr vs ₹1,255 Cr a year ago

MIM (Metal Injection Moulding) shapes fine metal powder mixed with a binder into small, complex parts, much like plastic injection moulding but with metal.

1.  Most segments growing-
Aerospace grew 31.5% (9% of revenue), automotive 19.4% (25%), consumer 46.5% (16%) and medical 22.5%. ECM (Electronic Component Manufacturing) fell about 40% and is now 11% of revenue, which was expected at the start of the year. ECM did ₹268 Cr in H1 against a full-year target of about ₹480-500 Cr.

2.  Gas turbine demand is booming-
IGT (Industrial Gas Turbines, used in power plants) demand is very strong as data centres need more electricity. Indo-MIM makes airfoils, casings and housings for this market through its Triax unit in the US and its Tirupati casting plant. Management said there have been zero order cancellations and customers are pulling orders forward.

3.  Aerospace parts count rising-
The company makes about 1,200 aerospace parts and aims to add at least 400 this year. It signed a long-term contract with Safran Aircraft Engines last month, as European OEMs outsource civil aerospace work to free up capacity for defence programmes. Triax should reach EBITDA breakeven by year end on about ₹310-335 Cr ($32-35 million) of revenue and turn profitable next year.

4.  Humanoid robots and private satellites-
The company has active development programmes with multiple humanoid robot and private satellite companies, across MIM, casting and machining. Management said even 10% of the volumes these customers are talking about would make a big year for suppliers. An update on the FY28 impact is expected in January.

5.  Backward integration into powders-
A new iron powder plant of about 3,000 tonnes a year is being set up, with 1,500-2,000 tonnes for own use and the rest for sale. The stainless steel powder unit already meets internal needs, and a large customer has asked for more supply. Capex will mainly go into machining and finishing, since there is enough capacity in the main processes.

6.  Inventory high, acquisitions in Europe-
Inventory days rose to 441 from 340 because of bulk raw material buying for casting and machining and higher work-in-progress in MIM. Management aims to cut this by about 75 days by year end. The company is looking at acquisitions of $20-50 million in Europe, and possibly the US and Singapore, and will build a greenfield plant in Europe within 12-18 months if no deal works out.

Key Guidance
- FY27 revenue of ₹5,000 Cr, which the company is on track for
- FY27 PAT target of ₹850 Cr likely to be met or slightly beaten; updated guidance in January
- Triax to reach EBITDA breakeven by end of FY27

Biocon's US cancer drug approval won't earn it a rupee before 2028

Biocon won US approval on 16 November for Pebrilzo, its copy of Roche's breast cancer drug Perjeta. new US sales, then? not soon. a patent settlement with Genentech (Roche's US arm), filed a month earlier, fixes the earliest US launch at July to September 2028, at least 19 months away.

Biocon makes biosimilars: near-copies of drugs grown from living cells, sold cheaper once patents end. Perjeta treats breast cancer driven by HER2, a protein that makes tumours grow fast, about 20% of new US cases. Roche's US business sold $1,702mn of it in 2025.

but Roche is moving patients on. Phesgo, Perjeta and Herceptin in 1 injection under the skin, is in Roche's words the treatment preferred over Perjeta and Herceptin, and its US sales rose 70% to $1.1bn in 2025. Pebrilzo copies only Perjeta, a drip. by 2028 part of the market Biocon is waiting for may have moved.

so the first money comes from elsewhere. the settlement allows launches in the EU and UK from January to March 2027, the same quarter that supplies start to Brazil's public health system under a 10-year contract worth about $400mn in all. Biocon gets milestone payments and a share of revenue, not the whole sum.

so the 16 November approval will not bring Biocon any US sales before 2028. Its first sales of this drug can start in Europe and Brazil in early 2027. and by the time Biocon can sell in the US, more patients may have moved to Phesgo, the injection Roche now prefers over the Perjeta drip.

Supriya Lifescience | ₹1,000 Cr Sales, But Where Will Profit Come From?

One more thing about Supriya after going little deeper into Q2 concall.

Some answers were quite interesting, specially when management talked about next 3–4 years.

Company still maintaining ₹1,000 Cr revenue guidance.

But H1 sales only ₹396 Cr. Means ₹604 Cr required in H2, almost ₹302 Cr every quarter against Q2 sales of ₹206 Cr.

Analyst asked where this much sales will come from.

Management said newer products doing well in semi regulated markets and orders are there.

But clear breakup not given.

And these products coming at lower margins than earlier business.

So sales may come back, but will profit also come in same proportion?

Now Ambernath. This part was more surprising.

Company spending around ₹60 Cr annually, but FY27 revenue expected almost zero.

CFO said ₹160–200 Cr annual sales needed just to break even.

Even after positive EU audit, meaningful scale may take another 1–1.5 years.

So plant getting approval and plant making profit are two different things.

Now big liquid anaesthetic contract.

Management said discussions going on, but deal not signed yet.

Initially API supply for first couple of years. Formulations later after approvals.

Even large customer may take 4–5 years to reach full volumes.

Big opportunity, but profit may take much longer.

What about other products?

Contrast media expected to start commercial production.

Whey samples accepted, waiting for first commercial orders.

Statin intermediate production started, bigger contracts under discussion.

ADHD intermediate with US customer, approvals expected in 3–4 months.

All these looks interesting. But most still waiting to become regular paying business.

Management expecting 20%+ revenue growth for next 3–4 years.

Ambernath itself having eventual ₹450–500 Cr revenue potential.

But when analyst asked FY28 margins, CFO declined giving guidance.

Now valuation is also important.

At around ₹620 share price, market cap nearly ₹5,000 Cr.

Trailing PE around 28 and price to sales 5.7 times.

Not exactly cheap considering H1 PAT fallen 37%.

Suppose company achieve ₹300 Cr sustainable PAT in next 3–4 years. Even at 25 PE, market cap becomes ₹7,500 Cr.

Around 50% upside from present valuation. Good, but not extraordinary considering risks and time involved.

And ₹300 Cr PAT itself need significant improvement from present earnings.

This is where things becoming complicated.

Old high margin business facing regulatory problems.

New products giving lower margins.

Ambernath expenses already coming, but revenue not coming.

All three happening together.

One question which is bothering.

Will Supriya's future ₹1,000 Cr sales business earn same profit as its earlier ₹700–800 Cr business?

Because sales increasing 25% with margins falling 10 percentage points doesnt necessarily create more value.

Management have good chemistry capabilities and many products under development.

But older concalls shows timelines are not always reliable.

Next few quarters should tell lot.

LATAM shipments restarting, inventory converting into cash and new products getting repeat commercial orders.

Supriya may become much bigger company in next 4–5 years. But bigger sales doesnt always means bigger profits.

And if Ambernath needs ₹200 Cr sales just to break even, how much more required to earn decent ROCE?

For me opportunity is there, but at 28 PE, market is not giving future growth free also.

  ▸ Standalone revenue grew 27.2% YoY to ₹32.70 Cr.
  ▸ EBITDA increased 50.8% to ₹11.47 Cr, with margins expanding to 35.1%.
  ▸ PAT grew 120.8% to ₹3.63 Cr.

𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗼𝗹𝗶𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗳𝗼𝗿𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲:

- 𝗤2 𝗙𝗬27: Consolidated revenue grew 17.6% to ₹31.53 Cr. EBITDA increased 14.4% to ₹7.99 Cr. PAT was ₹0.21 Cr.

𝗢𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸 & 𝗣𝗶𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲:

- 𝗢𝗿𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗼𝗼𝗸: ₹300 Cr. Expected to execute ₹100-125 Cr in the next 12 months.
- 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗣𝗶𝗽𝗲𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗲: ₹625 Cr. Targeting a 40% win rate, with 50-75% of the pipeline expected to be delivered in the next 12 months.

𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗤&𝗔 𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘀:

So people are now outraged about  love? About a couple being in love? About a son talking about the love between his parents?

Give me a break!

To love and be loved, for partners to stay madly in love through the mundane chaos of everyday life, to demonstrate their love and reach for each other without shame, for children to grow up watching parents who still look at each other like the world stopped the day they met - is not just beautiful. It is revolutionary. Love is a blessing, a privilege. It is a gift some people never get, and those who do should never hide it.

Yet when Rahul Gandhi spoke of his parents - head over heels, unapologetically affectionate, still in love after decades - some people were outraged and shocked. 

These are the same people who are so used to abandoning their wives and families, the cold distance between married couples that they can’t wrap their heads around the idea of a man who still wants to hold his wife. They cannot accept the sight of real love. 

They would have found it perhaps perfectly normal if the story had been of Sonia ji rushing between the kitchen and the dining table, serving hot phulkas, clearing Rajiv ji’s plate, and eating only after he had finished. That is their version of marriage, their version of a woman, their idea of a wife - useful, silent, secondary. Anything equal, anything tender, anything alive and romantic feels alien and outrageous.

Well, welcome to a world where partners are equals. Where love is not just a duty. Where a husband and wife in love don’t need a nod to be human, where they are not afraid of showing their love. 

Love is magical - It is the bravest thing two people can do in a world so full of uncertainty and hatred. Love is never weakness, love is strength. 

I wish more wives are kissed at home, I wish  more husbands are hugged without apology. I wish physical display of affection isn’t scorned over and I truly wish more children are brought up in households full of love, laughter and romance between their parents. Love is not weakness. And love can never be vulgar.

So folks take a deep breath and sit down. Stop policing affection. Celebrate this love story, one of the greatest of our times. Celebrate your own love story. Be unapologetic about the one person who still makes your heart skip a beat.

Because in the end, when the noise dies down it is only and only love that matters. Love that keeps us warm in the bones and love that carries us through. 

Thank you Rahul Gandhi for speaking of your parents’ love without hesitation and shattering the silence around affection in public life. And thank you Sonia ji for falling in love so deeply, so insanely, and for keeping it alive so unapologetically.

It’s the season of love folks. Be in love ❤️
