👉 Sammaan Capital's consolidated revenue fell 26.6% year on year to ₹1,652 Cr in Q2 FY27, from ₹2,251 Cr, and 10.7% quarter on quarter from ₹1,850 Cr. Net profit dropped 21.1% to ₹243.3 Cr from ₹308.5 Cr, and 22.1% from ₹312.3 Cr in Q1. Profit before tax fell 23.3% to ₹326 Cr.

👉 Operating margin improved to 19.4% from 18.8% a year earlier, though it fell 357 bps from 22.9% in Q1 FY27. Other income rose to ₹30.9 Cr from ₹9.9 Cr a year earlier and ₹0.9 Cr in Q1, but total income still fell 25.6% year on year to ₹1,683 Cr.

👉 On 30 October 2026 the company allotted 8,68,92,966 equity shares at ₹139 each to promoter Avenir Investment on conversion of Tranche I warrants. Avenir paid a balance of ₹905.86 Cr, taking its stake to 33.32%, with the conversion worth about ₹1,207.81 Cr in total. The allotment came after the quarter ended, so it does not appear in Q2 numbers.

👉 Debt payments in October and early November were all reported as timely, with ₹26.11 Cr of principal and interest across 16 ISINs and ₹22.75 Cr of principal redeemed on 7 November. No filing reported a delay or default, and one filing describes servicing of existing debt rather than new borrowing.

👉 Growth catalyst: Promoter Avenir's ₹905.86 Cr payment on Tranche I warrants, which lifted its stake to 33.32%, is the largest capital infusion in the company record.

👉 Road blocker: Revenue fell 26.6% year on year and net profit fell 21.1% to ₹243.3 Cr, with the quarterly decline of 22.1% from Q1 FY27 showing no recovery.

👉 The company is counting on recent credit rating upgrades to AA+ to bring down its borrowing costs. However, auditors noted that the company breached certain financial terms on its bank borrowings at the end of September, showing that bank credit lines are still catching up with the new ratings.

👉 The stock trades at 0.82 times book value, which may already reflect the slow pace of recovery. Management has targeted ₹20,000 Cr of fresh loan disbursements in the second half of the year, which is crucial for rebuilding the lending book.

👉 The result looks neutral because core operating profit fell -68.21% from a year ago and reported profit was sustained by ₹216.66 Cr of provision write-backs; the next result must show core earnings growing from fresh lending to confirm a real recovery.

Sammaan Capital board meets today to approve Q2 FY27 results.

The Q2 business update already showed growth is back. Today is about whether that growth starts showing up in earnings.

The context going in:

Q1 FY27:

AUM ₹56,239 cr
Disbursals ₹3,875 cr
PAT ₹243 cr
Cost of funds 10.0% (vs 10.9% a year ago, ~90 bps lower)
Net NPA 0.15%, CRAR 20.1%
97% of AUM secured

Q2 business update:

Disbursals ~₹6,000 cr (+55% QoQ); H1 ~₹9,900 cr against the ₹10,000 cr plan
AUM ₹59,000 cr+ (+11% in two quarters)
30,700+ new customers (vs 11,867 in Q1)
245 branches

Q2 FY26 base: PAT ₹308 cr

The nuance:

Volumes are moving. The next step is the P&L.

Cost of funds is guided to ~9.3% for FY27, with incremental borrowing already at ~9%. Every bps of that flows straight into earnings as the new book grows.

Q1 profit was helped by recoveries (₹240 cr net) and fair-value gains. A cleaner earnings mix matters as much as the headline number.

The YoY comparison is against ₹308 cr, which included more one-offs. QoQ growth and the quality of earnings tell you more.

Key things to watch:
→ PAT vs Q1’s ₹243 cr, and how much comes from core interest vs recoveries and fair-value gains
→ Cost of funds: below 10%, heading toward ~9.3%?
→ NII and spreads as the new book builds
→ Asset quality on the new book (net NPA 0.15% in Q1)
→ Product mix: LAP, loans against securities, unsecured, and the secured share
→ IHC integration: ratings, bank lines, board and the warrant conversion

The first checkpoint has been passed on growth. Now it’s about earnings.

Watching today’s numbers closely.

Not a recommendation. DYOR.

• Significant tax disputes and historical governance/record-keeping concerns.

My Take:

A strong business with a dominant market position, but declining financial performance and long-term coal transition risks deserve attention.

The key question: At what valuation is MCL being offered?

Good company ≠ Good IPO at any price.

WHAT ARE PROMOTERS, GLOBAL INVESTORS AND MUTUAL FUNDS DOING?

Here are the deals that caught my attention — and what retail investors should make of them.

1. HAVELLS: PROMOTER BUYING AS THE SHARE PRICE MOVES UP

QRG Investments & Holdings, a promoter entity of Havells India, purchased shares across three trading sessions.

• 6 November: 14 lakh shares at ₹1,091.50
• 9 November: 7 lakh shares at ₹1,148.50
• 11 November: 6.05 lakh shares at ₹1,159.90

Total acquired: 27.05 lakh shares.

What makes this transaction interesting?
The promoter entity continued buying even as the share price moved higher across the three sessions.

This is more meaningful than a token purchase made at a single price.

What should investors investigate?

• Is this an isolated purchase or the beginning of sustained accumulation?
• How does the promoter's holding change in the next shareholding disclosure?
• Are earnings growth, margins and capital efficiency supporting the investment case?
• Does the current valuation leave room for future returns?

Promoter buying is an important research signal. But it does not automatically mean the stock is undervalued.

2. MEESHO: SOFTBANK CONTINUES ITS EXIT

SoftBank's SVF II Meerkat sold 7.64 crore shares of Meesho at ₹246.75.
The interesting part is not just the seller. It is the identity of the buyers.

The disclosed buyer composition included:

• Fidelity/FIAM
• Domestic mutual funds and an insurer
• Sovereign and pension investors
• Broker/ODI-routed investors
• A hedge fund

The stock closed the week at ₹257.07, above the block transaction price.

There are two ways to interpret this.

The positive: A large shareholder was able to sell a substantial stake, and the market absorbed the supply without the stock closing below the block price.

The caution: Not every buyer can be classified as a long-term institutional investor. The ultimate beneficial investors behind broker/ODI-routed transactions are not fully identifiable from the disclosure.

The bigger question is whether Meesho can translate its scale into sustainable profitability.

Track contribution margins, repeat purchases, customer acquisition costs, cash burn and the path to positive cash flows.

Institutional absorption is interesting. Business economics will determine the investment outcome.

3. ADITYA INFOTECH: DIXON SELLS, MUTUAL FUNDS STEP IN
Dixon Technologies sold approximately 14.05 lakh shares of Aditya Infotech (CP Plus).

The shares were acquired by:

• Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund
• Kotak Mutual Fund

The entire disclosed sale was absorbed by these two domestic mutual funds.

The transaction took place at ₹4,140, while the stock closed the week at ₹4,148.

This is an interesting change in the shareholder base.

Dixon is reducing its exposure, while domestic institutional investors are taking the other side.

For investors, three things deserve attention:

Dixon's remaining stake and whether it continues to sell.

Whether Motilal Oswal and Kotak increase their holdings in subsequent disclosures.

Whether Aditya Infotech's earnings growth, margins and cash conversion justify its valuation.

A strategic shareholder's exit need not be negative if the business fundamentals remain intact and a new set of investors is willing to own the stock.

But don't mistake a change in ownership for an improvement in the business.

4. INDO TECH TRANSFORMERS: A SIGNIFICANT PLEDGE RELEASE
Promoter Shirdi Sai Electricals revoked the pledge on 13.30 lakh shares of Indo Tech Transformers.

This represents approximately 12.5% of the company's equity.

The release is a constructive development because pledged promoter shares carry collateral and potential forced-selling risks.

However, there is a question investors should not overlook:

How was the borrowing against these shares settled?

Was it repaid using promoter funds? Was there an asset sale? Was the loan refinanced against other collateral?

A pledge release is positive, but it does not necessarily mean the promoter's overall leverage has declined.

Watch for fresh pledge creation in subsequent disclosures.

5. HORIZON INDUSTRIAL PARKS: DAMANI AND SBI ON THE SHAREHOLDER REGISTER

Two names stand out in the latest shareholding disclosures:

• Radhakishan Damani
• SBI Group

Their holdings crossed the 1% disclosure threshold.

This makes Horizon Industrial Parks an interesting company to investigate.

But an important distinction:

These are post-listing shareholding disclosures, not confirmation that both investors purchased shares during this particular week.

For a business operating in the industrial and logistics infrastructure space, I would focus on:

• Occupancy and tenant additions
• Lease rentals and rental escalations
• Development pipeline
• Capital expenditure requirements
• Debt and interest costs
• Cash flow generation

A reputed investor appearing on the register should prompt research, not replace it.

6. IIFL CAPITAL: FINANCIAL INVESTORS TRIM THEIR HOLDINGS

Three financial investors sold shares of IIFL Capital on 13 November.

The transactions were executed in a relatively narrow price range.

Unlike the Meesho and Aditya Infotech transactions, the disclosures did not identify corresponding institutional buyers.

This is worth monitoring.

Possible explanations include portfolio rebalancing, fund redemptions, a change in investment mandate or a change in the investors' view of the company.

The transaction alone cannot establish which explanation is correct.
What I would track:

• Whether the same investors continue selling.
• Whether new institutional investors emerge as buyers.
• Whether the selling is accompanied by changes in fundamentals.
• Whether the next shareholding disclosure shows a meaningful ownership shift.

One week's selling is a signal to investigate, not a reason to jump to conclusions.

7. EMBASSY DEVELOPMENTS: A PLEDGE RELEASE THAT DIDN'T REALLY REDUCE THE RISK

This is one of the more instructive transactions of the week.

First, shares were released from pledge.
A few days later, the same quantity of shares was pledged again.
The transactions involved Embassy Property Developments and OMR Investments LLP.
This appears to be a pledge roll or refinancing-related transaction rather than a genuine reduction in pledged shares.

Why does this matter?
Investors often interpret a pledge-revocation filing as a positive development.

But the subsequent pledge-creation filing can completely change the interpretation.

Always reconcile the quantity of shares released with the quantity subsequently pledged.

Check the dates, entities and lenders.

A pledge release should be considered a genuine improvement only after the full sequence of transactions is understood.

8. MASTER TRUST AND CAMLIN FINE SCIENCES: FRESH PLEDGE CREATION

Two other transactions deserve attention.

Master Trust

Two promoters pledged shares in separate filings. Together, these pledges represent approximately 10.8% of the company's equity.

Camlin Fine Sciences

Promoter-director Ashish Dandekar created three pledges covering 14.5 lakh shares.

Neither transaction should automatically be interpreted as evidence of financial distress.
But fresh promoter pledges warrant questions:
• What is the purpose of the borrowing?
• Who is the lender?
• What is the repayment schedule?
• Are the shares pledged for promoter-level or company-level obligations?
• Is there sufficient collateral headroom if the share price falls?
• Is the promoter's overall leverage increasing?
For retail investors, promoter pledges are not merely a disclosure to note. They are a balance-sheet and governance risk to understand.

9. OTHER SHAREHOLDING MOVEMENTS WORTH TRACKING

A few additional developments from the shareholding disclosures:

Concord Enviro Systems: Kotak Group reduced its holding, although it continues to remain a meaningful shareholder.

Generic Engineering: Arihant Capital appeared above the 1% threshold. Given its role as a broker and its presence in trading activity, I would not automatically treat this as a high-conviction investment.

Midwest: Axis Group made a marginal addition to its holding.

GHCL: Vanguard marginally reduced its position. This could reflect passive portfolio or index-related activity rather than a fundamental negative view.

The important lesson: institutional ownership changes need context.

A long-only fund, an index-tracking fund, a proprietary trading desk and a broker are not interchangeable categories of investors.

10. MY TAKEAWAY: WHICH DEALS DESERVE A DEEPER LOOK?

If I were using this week's disclosures to build a research pipeline, my priorities would be:

Havells — Promoter accumulation across multiple sessions. Investigate valuation and earnings trajectory.

Aditya Infotech — Dixon's exit and mutual fund absorption. Track the change in shareholder composition.

Meesho — SoftBank's continuing sell-down. Understand the buyer base and the company's path to profitability.

Indo Tech Transformers — Pledge release. Verify the source of repayment and monitor subsequent filings.

Horizon Industrial Parks — New post-listing shareholder disclosures. Investigate operating performance and asset economics.

On the risk-monitoring side:

• IIFL Capital — financial-investor selling.
• Embassy Developments — pledge refinancing.
• Master Trust — fresh promoter pledges.
• Camlin Fine Sciences — additional pledge creation.

The larger lesson:

Don't simply track who bought or sold a stock.

Understand:

Who is buying?

Who is selling?

At what price did the transaction happen?

Is it an open-market purchase, a strategic exit, a portfolio transfer or a pledge-related transaction?

What does the transaction mean for the company's ownership, financial risk and future prospects?

A bulk deal is a disclosure.

A well-understood transaction can become an investment insight.

In last week’s elections Democrats won historic victories in places where their party has long been in the political wilderness. Dimming the optimism this week are reminders of the continuing dysfunction in areas where Democrats have long exercised control.

In the Windy City, Democratic mayors have been in charge for nearly a century. Now Fran Spielman reports for the Chicago Sun-Times:

The abrupt resignation on Friday of Mayor Brandon Johnson’s third chief financial officer in a year could trigger another drop in Chicago’s already shaky bond rating and scare investors away from the city’s bonds.

Ashlee Gabrysch’s departure sent shock waves through City Hall and beyond — her resignation comes in the middle of a budget stalemate, after just three months as CFO. Even more damaging than Gabrysch’s sudden exit is what she said on her way out the door…

“As the City of Chicago’s Chief Financial Officer, there is nothing more important than my fiduciary duty to the City and its taxpayers. The Chief Financial Officer’s statements about city finances are not idle chatter: they are relied upon by investors, ratings agencies, City Council, and taxpayers. The CFO must act scrupulously to ensure they are always accurate and complete,” Gabrysch said in a statement released to the media.

“Throughout my career, I have remained committed to upholding the highest standards of financial integrity and transparency, and in my short time as Chief Financial Officer, I have faithfully discharged this duty. Ms. Gabrysch hasn’t detailed the particulars that made the job incompatible with her integrity. 10 Key Takeaways

FY27 Guidance: Management maintained ~15% comparable consolidated revenue growth guidance, excluding the impact of closing AWUKO and Foskor Zirconia.

Ceramics – Biggest Growth Driver: FY27 sales growth guidance upgraded to 25–28%, with segment margin guidance raised to 22.5–23.5%.

Why Ceramics Is Growing: Strong demand for engineered ceramics, including products supplied to Bloom Energy, and metallized cylinders. These are key growth drivers.

Abrasives – Margin Pressure: FY27 margin guidance cut from 9.5–10% to 8–8.5% (excluding AWUKO), driven by higher raw-material and fuel costs, with limited pricing power.

Electrominerals: FY27 comparable revenue growth guidance maintained at 9–10%, with margins expected at 9–9.5%.

Semiconductor Opportunity: Semiconductor equipment components could generate ₹300–350 Cr annual revenue around FY30–31. This represents a new high-value growth opportunity.

Electronics & Defence: AMB/DBC electronic substrates and armour programmes are progressing with anchor-customer support. Management expects these high-tech businesses to deliver superior margins at maturity.

AWUKO Restructuring: German subsidiary closure progressing. ₹18.3 Cr exceptional charge recognised in Q2; no further major write-offs anticipated. Foskor Zirconia closure is also progressing.

CapEx: FY27 consolidated capex guidance maintained at ₹400 Cr, supporting existing operations and new high-tech growth initiatives.

Overall View: CUMI is increasingly benefiting from high-margin ceramics and emerging semiconductor/electronics opportunities. However, abrasives profitability, overseas restructuring and commercialisation of new businesses remain key monitorables.

AXISCADES... Q2 results . At first look PAT doubled, but inside numbers story is little different.

Revenue ₹359 Cr, up 20%. PAT ₹47 Cr.

But this profit mainly came because of selling old engineering business. The business company is keeping actually reported ₹48 Cr loss, including ₹38 Cr impairment.

Normalised PBT only ₹3.7 Cr.

Now interesting part is what AXISCADES is becoming.

Retained business revenue ₹196 Cr, up 30%. H1 growth 55%.

Defence Q2 revenue ₹128 Cr, EBITDA ₹22.5 Cr, margin 17.6%.

Within this DRDO/PSU business earning almost 24% margin.

XIDA, earlier ESAI, revenue ₹48 Cr, up 47%, EBITDA margin 22%.

This business is moving into semiconductor equipment, AI infrastructure and advanced electronics. New global customers coming also.

I find XIDA equally interesting as defence, may be even more in future.

Then Aerospace. Cloud Wave acquired, contributed ₹16.5 Cr revenue with 20% EBITDA margin.

Company is trying to move from engineering design to actually manufacturing components.

This is important. Designing something for customer and then supplying same product for years, can change whole economics.

16 new defence orders worth ₹80 Cr. Management talking about ₹730 Cr potential future production from these programmes. But not confirmed order yet.

Now one thing bothering me.

Defence, XIDA, Cloud Wave individually making good margins. But at total group level EBITDA only ₹11.4 Cr.

Why?

Parent company carrying heavy expenses, ESOP ₹12 Cr, and old loss making businesses also eating profits.

Even before ESOP, group EBITDA only ₹23.4 Cr.

So profitable divisions are there, but their earnings not fully reaching shareholders.

H1 operating cash flow negative ₹58 Cr. Gross debt increased from ₹276 Cr to ₹624 Cr.

Company selling old profitable engineering business to fund this new journey. First phase completed, second expected February 2027.

Also old acquisitions getting written off. Cleaning balance sheet is good, but capital allocation mistakes of past cant be ignored.

And valuation around ₹8,200 Cr market cap.

Even if company achieve ₹135 Cr PAT discussed in earlier call for FY27, PE still around 61.

Management has very ambitious ₹9,000 Cr revenue and ₹960 Cr PAT target by FY30. But lot of distance between ambition and actual earnings.

What I like is defence electronics and XIDA already have customers and margins. Aerospace manufacturing is developing. Space is much early.

Now need to see whether selling old business really reduces debt, parent expenses comes down, and new facilities start generating cash.

Because having 3-4 good divisions is not enough, if at group level profit keeps getting absorbed.

AXISCADES is definitely changing into different kind of company.

But at ₹8,200 Cr valuation, market already expecting quite big success.

Business opportunity is real. Investment opportunity at this price, still not so clear to me.

The judges appreciated the participants for their composure, technical precision and preparedness in handling simulated emergency situations.

The programme was successfully coordinated under the guidance and leadership of Shri Harshad Datar, AGM, Nagpur Area; Shri Raj Kapoor Prasad, GM (Rescue); and Shri Avinash Prasad, GM (S&C).

Operating profit grew 23% YoY as IPO proceeds cut total debt to ₹941 Cr.

👉 Headline profit doubled to ₹215.19 Cr, but the comparison is distorted by a ₹92.66 Cr exceptional charge in the same period last year. Stripping out that base effect, underlying core operating profit grew 22.89% YoY to ₹379.85 Cr on revenue of ₹1,271.84 Cr. The fresh issue from the July 2026 listing allowed the company to pay off ₹400.00 Cr of debt, cutting quarterly interest costs by 38.8% YoY to ₹26.98 Cr.

👉 Raw material cost intensity fell 409 bps YoY to 17.4% of sales, lifting the operating margin by 209 bps YoY to 29.87%. However, other expenses rose 21.3% YoY to ₹424.56 Cr, causing operating margin to pull back from the 33.36% recorded in the June quarter. Capital expenditure reached ₹257.35 Cr for the first half, keeping capital work-in-progress elevated at ₹202.43 Cr as new lines are readied.

👉 The main friction in the numbers is working capital absorption. Operating cash flow fell 17.8% YoY to ₹470.37 Cr during the first half as receivables climbed to ₹994.79 Cr and inventory reached ₹999.94 Cr, absorbing ₹250.41 Cr in cash. While cash flow still covered the ₹257.35 Cr half-year capex and ₹329.22 Cr in interim dividends, cash conversion has slowed compared to last year.

👉 The stock has risen about 53% over the past three months and trades at roughly 90 times earnings, suggesting that the current pace of growth is largely anticipated by the market. Additional production from the Bangalore Titanium facility and the Chennai aerospace plant represent the next stage of volume additions.

👉 Growth catalyst: Ramping production at the newly built Chennai aerospace plant and Bangalore Titanium Additive Manufacturing unit, supported by ₹202.43 Cr in capacity under construction, is targeted to add new volumes over the next twelve months

👉 Road blocker: Working capital absorbed ₹250.41 Cr in the first half as inventory reached ₹999.94 Cr and receivables rose to ₹994.79 Cr, which could weigh on cash conversion if collection periods lengthen

Q2 Results Live: Axiscades Tech Q2 Net Profit Doubles To Rs 47 Crore
Axiscades Tech Q2 Results Highlights (Cons, YoY)

• Net Profit Up 104.3% at Rs 47 crore vs Rs 23 crore YoY
• Revenue Up 30.7% at Rs 196 crore vs Rs 150 crore YoY
• EBITDA Down 64.9% at Rs 6.8 crore vs Rs 19.4 crore YoY
• EBITDA Margin at 3.5% vs 12.9% YoY

US Opportunity: Better Customers, Better Returns

Tata Chemicals paid $22 million for Searles Valley customer contracts covering 0.5 mt over 2 years. Nearby California and Mexico customers mean lower transport costs. Management says pricing is better than its export alternative.

Expansion: Where Growth Could Come From

Tata Chemicals is adding:
• 82.5 KTPA salt at Mithapur
• 210 KTPA salt at Valinokkam
• 50 KTPA silica at Cuddalore
• 40 KTPA bicarbonate at Singapore
More capacity creates growth potential, but returns depend on demand and execution.

The Macros

HEADWIND. High natural gas and energy prices raise production costs. Middle East disruptions increase freight, logistics and CO₂ costs. At the same time, cheap Chinese supply pushes selling prices down. Tata Chemicals is being squeezed from both sides.

Business :

Tata Chemicals makes ingredients used in glass, detergents, food, medicines and agriculture. Think of it as a chemical supplier powering everyday life. Q2 revenue: ₹4,177 Cr (+8%). But EBITDA fell 29% to ₹381 Cr, and the company reported a ₹50 Cr loss.

👉 Management expects supply shortages to ease in the second half of the year, while new lines in Spokane start commercial runs. The next result will show whether nuclear medicine margins begin recovering or whether plant fixes take longer than planned.

ALPEX SOLAR – THE BIGGER QUESTIONS ARE NOW ABOUT EXECUTION, TRANSPARENCY AND MANAGEMENT CREDIBILITY!

The latest results are disappointing. But beyond the numbers, I have some serious questions for management:

🔴 1. MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY, REVENUE COLLAPSE & TRUST

I understand that a significant portion of your business comes from schemes like PM Surya Ghar. However, management should have had visibility into the business situation well before announcing the results.

My concern is not margins. I was already expecting margin pressure and a possible margin collapse. But what I wasn't expecting was such a sharp collapse in revenue.

How come revenue collapsed so significantly?

If you had visibility of these challenges during your August/September concall, investors should have been made aware of them. You make extremely bullish statements during concalls, but when it comes to execution, the actual performance tells a different story.

You should have communicated the potential challenges and risks to investors instead of leaving them surprised by the results.

Honestly, this is now becoming a TRUST ISSUE. Investors are finding it difficult to trust management commentary.

🔴 2. SOLAR CELL MANUFACTURING

Has Alpex actually started solar cell manufacturing? Does the company genuinely have its own solar cell manufacturing capability, or is it still dependent on external suppliers?

This is an important question because having its own cell manufacturing capability could make a significant difference to its competitive positioning.

🔴 3. ALMM APPROVAL

₹3,000 crore revenue may still be achievable, but investors need clarity on the execution roadmap and the assumptions behind this target.

The concern is no longer just about one disappointing quarter. It is also about management credibility, transparency and the trust investors place in the company's commentary.

I am not making any allegations, but these are serious questions that deserve clear and convincing answers from management.

If you remember one month ago I posted about the Growth Catalysts report covering 100 companies where I divided the opportunities into three categories:

- where growth may already be visible and rerating may be harder
- where expectations based rerating may be possible
- where the spending opportunity looks Strong but the business case is still developing

This analysis was based on the report published by @stockscansin by SOIC.

Around 10 days ago, StockScans by SOIC published another Growth Catalysts report, this time covering 250 companies.

This report looked at what businesses are planning, what management has committed to and where the next phase of growth could come from through capex, order books, new products and other opportunities.

Now, if you look at both reports together, you will see that they look at growth from two different angles.

The first helps us understand where growth may already be visible.

The second helps us understand where businesses are preparing to grow next.

So I picked up the latest report and decided to look at it differently this time.

Instead of looking at companies one by one, I started looking at the spending pools and supply chains.

why?

Because when money starts moving across different industries, the opportunity is not always limited to the companies directly working in those industries.

The companies supplying the products, equipment and systems behind them can also benefit.

So I wanted to understand where this money would go, which companies would receive that spending and whether some of the same products and systems were needed across different industries.

Then I connected both reports and this is where things started getting interesting.

Let's start with power and grid infra.

In the 100-company report, #AparIndustries reported overseas utility conductor orders exceeding ₹2,800 crore, with deliveries spread over four years. #DiamondPower reported ₹435.71 crore of hyperscale campus orders from L&T, Sterling & Wilson and Blue Star, along with another ₹52.86 crore from Aurionpro.

Now look at the latest report.

#CGPower's Power Systems order intake reached ₹6,258 crore in Q2 FY27, up 137% YoY. Its unexecuted order book reached ₹18,964 crore, up 81%, while its switchgear facilities were already operating at peak utilisation.

If you put these developments together, what do you see?

Demand is growing across transmission equipment, transformers, switchgear and other electrical products.

But is this demand coming only from the power and grid sector?

Let's look at data centres.

In the earlier report, #TDPower Systems had signed a 10-year generator manufacturing framework agreement with Siemens Energy, along with repeat orders for gas turbine and gas engine applications linked to US data centres.

#HFCL reported an approximately US$1.1 billion optical fibre cable supply contract and an order book of over ₹850 crore for data-centre connectivity.

And in the latest report, CG Power received a ₹900 crore order from Tallgrass for 330 kV transformers serving a US hyperscale data centre.

Now, if you connect this with what we just saw in the power sector, something becomes clear.

The spending is coming from different areas but we are again seeing orders reaching companies supplying generators, transformers, cables and electrical equipment.

So the opportunity may not be limited to one industry, the same companies and products could be linked to more than one spending pool.

Now let's move to aerospace and defence.

The earlier report included companies such as #PTC, #MTAR, #RossellTechsys, #CyientDLM and #Avalon, which are connected to specialised components, aerospace manufacturing and electronics.

In the latest report, #Aequs has a single-source A320 wheel assembly agreement with Safran running through 2042.

#Unimech has more than 250 qualified aerospace parts with another 340-plus in the pipeline.

#ApolloMicro has sole-supplier positions for selected electronic processing systems and sensors in defence programmes.

Now, if you look beyond the company names and orders, what do you notice?

We are again seeing demand for specialised components, precision manufacturing, electronics, sensors and control systems.

The products are different but some of the same capabilities are needed here as well.

And then there is another connection: semiconductors and power electronics.

#CGPower has started commercial production at its OSAT semiconductor facility.

#SterlingTools has started commercial supplies of domestically manufactured HVDC contactors and relays, with seven customers receiving products.

#RIRPower Electronics has received its first overseas order for 120 press-pack SCR thyristors.

Now, why am I connecting all these developments?

Because if you look at the grid, data centres, aerospace and defence together, you will start seeing some common requirements.

Power electronics. Sensors. Electronic systems. Communication. Protection. Monitoring and control.

Electronics, Sensing and Intelligent Control.

This is the common layer I started seeing when I connected both reports.

Think about it, we are not looking at just one industry or one spending pool, we are looking at a layer that is needed across several different areas where money is being spent.

So what if, instead of looking at these industries separately, we start looking at the companies supplying this common layer?

So, how did I reach this conclusion? 

This report is all about answering these questions.

जयंत विस्तार परियोजना से जुड़े विभिन्न पहलुओं पर की चर्चा

शुक्रवार को मध्य प्रदेश शासन के खनिज संसाधन विभाग के प्रमुख सचिव श्री विवेक कुमार पोरवाल, (आईएएस), ने नॉर्दर्न कोलफील्ड्स लिमिटेड मुख्यालय में जयंत विस्तार परियोजना से जुड़े विभिन्न महत्वपूर्ण पहलुओं पर  चर्चा की ।

बैठक में एनसीएल सीएमडी श्री एन. फ्रैंकलिन जयकुमार, सिंगरौली कलेक्टर श्री अंकित अस्थाना,  निदेशक (मानव संसाधन) श्री मनीष कुमार, निदेशक (तकनीकी/संचालन) श्री आशुतोष द्विवेदी, निदेशक (तकनीकी/परियोजना एवं नियोजन) श्री संजय कुमार मिश्रा, अपर कलेक्टर श्री पी एस त्रिपाठी, एसडीएम श्री सुरेश जादव, तहसीलदार श्री अभिषेक यादव, जिला खनन अधिकारी सुश्री आकांक्षा पटेल तथा महाप्रबंधक (एसपीसी) श्री निरंजन रुकमांगड़ व श्री आर आर सिंह  एवं अन्य अधिकारी उपस्थित रहे।

बैठक के शुभारंभ में एनसीएल सीएमडी श्री एन. फ्रैंकलिन जयकुमार ने मध्य प्रदेश शासन के खनिज संसाधन विभाग के प्रमुख सचिव श्री विवेक कुमार पोरवाल, (आईएएस) सहित आगंतुक अधिकारियों का स्वागत करते हुए एनसीएल का देश की ऊर्जा सुरक्षा एवं राजस्व में योगदान तथा जयंत विस्तार परियोजना की रूपरेखा, इसकी जरूरत व इससे जुड़े विभिन्न पहलुओं की जानकारी दी।

प्रमुख सचिव श्री पोरवाल ने अपने अनुभवों को साझा करते हुए निरंतर परामर्श और संवाद को विस्थापन प्रक्रिया का अभिन्न अंग बताया। उन्होंने पूरी प्रक्रिया में पारस्परिक समझ एवं संवेदनशीलता पर बल दिया ।
इस अवसर पर निदेशक (मानव संसाधन) श्री मनीष कुमार ने मोरवा विस्थापन की प्रगति की जानकारी देते हुए इससे जुड़े विभिन्न पहलुओं जैसे पुनर्वास स्थल की व्यवस्था, परियोजना प्रभावित परिवारों की विभिन्न श्रेणियों, पात्रताओं एवं अधिकारों तथा आजीविका के अवसरों पर सभा को अवगत कराया । 

गौरतलब है कि एनसीएल मोरवा पुनर्स्थापन की प्रक्रिया को सहभागिता, पारदर्शिता एवं मानवीय दृष्टिकोण के साथ समयबद्ध तरीके से पूर्ण करने के लिए सदैव प्रतिबद्ध है।

RBI से हाथ जोड़कर अनुरोध है कि समय रहते कड़ी कार्रवाई करें और आर्थिक संकट से जूझ रहे कर्जदारों को न्याय दिलाएँ।

👉 Edelweiss Financial Services posted consolidated net profit of ₹207.3 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 18.2% from ₹175.4 Cr a year earlier and 54.2% above Q1's ₹134.4 Cr. Profit before tax was ₹241.4 Cr, against a loss of ₹46.3 Cr last year. The Capital business earned a segment profit of ₹20.4 Cr, against a loss of ₹59.0 Cr in Q1 and ₹211.4 Cr a year earlier. Alternatives profit rose to ₹112.3 Cr.

👉 Employee benefit expenses rose to ₹524 Cr from ₹394 Cr in Q1, including a ₹220 Cr variable incentive provision. Finance costs eased to ₹563 Cr from ₹655 Cr a year ago. The insurance business still posted a segment loss of ₹17.1 Cr, narrower than ₹33.7 Cr in Q1 and ₹67.4 Cr last year.

👉 Cash and cash equivalents fell to ₹1,752 Cr at 30 September 2026 from ₹2,720 Cr in March, while loans dropped to ₹8,484 Cr from ₹10,986 Cr. Non-controlling interest fell to ₹521 Cr from ₹1,321 Cr over the same period. Debt securities stood at ₹14,251 Cr, and total equity at ₹5,615 Cr. Half-year net profit was ₹341.7 Cr, up from ₹278.1 Cr.

👉 Growth catalyst: EAAA Alternatives was listed on BSE and NSE on 2 November 2026 after its ₹1,200 Cr IPO, which the filing says has no impact on these results.

👉 Road blocker: Revenue from operations fell 5.6% QoQ, and the ₹453 Cr Nido gain is larger than the quarter's ₹241 Cr pre-tax profit.

IP protection for India engineering teams in 2026: if a non-compete won’t hold, what actually protects you?

The paperwork behind your code, and how you run the exit.

Rarely when an engineer leaves. It surfaces in due diligence, when an investor or acquirer traces who owns every line of code. The Delhi High Court applied India’s assignment defaults against a software buyer in Pine Labs v. Gemalto.
 🗣️ What should you check this quarter?
Every engineer’s contract assigns all IP types, not just copyright
If you hire through an EOR, a second written assignment moves IP from the EOR to your company
Both assignments state the duration and territory
Contractors have signed assignments too, since they own their work by default

Production access steps down in stages across the notice period
Repos, credentials and documentation move to named owners
A written handover plan, signed off before exit
None of this restricts where a good engineer works next. It makes sure the work they did for you stays yours.

EBITDA fell 32.81% as ₹403.40 Cr of other income saved reported profit

👉 Selling assets, not core business operations, drove this quarter's headline profit. Operating profit before other income dropped sharply because costs rose faster than revenue, leaving the reported profit dependent on the one-time gain from transferring control of the home finance business to Carlyle.

👉 Underneath the headline, the business is shifting away from wholesale loans toward fee-earning asset management and insurance. The capital business returned to an operating profit after losing money a year ago, while the alternatives division and asset reconstruction arms continued earning steady fees. Insurance losses narrowed as well, but total operating expenses still grew faster than revenue due to variable staff incentives.

👉 Cash generation improved as wholesale loan recoveries brought in fresh funds, which were used to pay down borrowings of ₹17,309.33 Cr. However, co-founder Venkatachalam Ramaswamy resigned from the board just before these results were approved, asking to be reclassified as a public shareholder rather than a promoter, creating leadership uncertainty at the parent level.

👉 The result looks neutral because EBITDA fell 32.81% from a year ago to ₹404.21 Cr, while PAT was supported by ₹403.40 Cr of other income.

👉 Road blocker: Total borrowings of ₹17,309.33 Cr take ₹562.53 Cr in quarterly finance costs out of operating profit, until corporate net debt is reduced to the targeted ₹3,000 Cr by FY27

Economists expect the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to increase key policy rates following the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting in early December to counter rising inflation.

Key details reported:
- Projected Increases: Economists project the MPC will raise the repo rate by 25 to 50 basis points during the 2026-27 financial year.
- Driving Factors: Upward pressure stems from food inflation, adverse base effects, and elevated commodity prices, with CPI inflation projected to stay above 6%.

உலகம் முழுக்க இருக்கிற பெரிய இன்வெஸ்டர்கள் ஃபாலோ பண்ற ஒரு லிஸ்ட்ல நம்ம ஊர் கம்பெனிங்க ஏறுனா யாருக்கு லாபம், யாருக்கு நஷ்டம் தெரியுமா?

இந்த நவம்பர் 30 நடக்கப்போற MSCI Index ரீஜிக் மூலமா இந்தியாவுக்கு 2 பில்லியன் டாலர் வரைக்கும் மியூச்சுவல் ஃபண்ட் மற்றும் பாசிவ் இன்வெஸ்ட்மெண்ட் உள்ள வரப்போகுது.

இதுல பெரிய வின்னர் Coforge தான். அவங்க Standard Index உள்ள வர்றதால 630 மில்லியன் டாலர் மேல புதுசா பணம் உள்ள வரும். ஆனா இதுல ஒரு சின்ன ட்விஸ்ட் இருக்கு. இவங்க Smallcap லிஸ்ட்ல இருந்து வெளிய போறதால 97 மில்லியன் டாலர் வெளியவும் போகும். மீதி இருக்கிற 533 மில்லியன் டாலர் தான் நெட் லாபம்.

அடுத்ததா LIC மேல 468 மில்லியன் டாலர் பந்தயம் கட்டப்படுது. Adani Green மற்றும் Meesho பின்னாடியே வர்றாங்க.

🔹 Oswal Pumps announced its Q2 FY27 financial results, reporting a Total Income of ₹5,118 million, marking a 6.2% increase quarter-on-quarter but a 6.4% decrease year-on-year.

🔹 Total Income was ₹5,118 million, up 6.2% quarter-on-quarter and down 6.4% year-on-year.

🔹 EBITDA was ₹628 million, down 23.8% quarter-on-quarter and down 53.4% year-on-year.

🔹 EBITDA Margin was 12.3%, down 484 bps quarter-on-quarter and down 1,239 bps year-on-year.

🔹 Profit After Tax was ₹396 million, down 26.4% quarter-on-quarter and down 59.4% year-on-year.

🔹 Profit After Tax Margin was 7.7%, down 343 bps quarter-on-quarter and down 1,010 bps year-on-year.

🔹 Diluted EPS was ₹3.34, down 31.3% quarter-on-quarter and down 60.4% year-on-year.

🔹 Sequential income growth was supported by a 6.9% quarter-on-quarter increase in Revenue from Operations to ₹5,063 million, driven by solar pump order book execution.

🔹 Profitability faced pressure during the quarter.

🔹 EBITDA margin decreased to 12.3% and Profit After Tax margin to 7.7%.

🔹 The margin decline was attributed to higher raw material costs with around 210 bps impact, due to increased prices of aluminium, glass, copper, zinc and steel.

🔹 The company plans to establish a 1.2 GW TOPCon solar cell manufacturing facility in Karnal, Haryana, with an estimated project cost of ₹4,558.5 million.

Jewellers’ Gain Masks Gold Volume Dip: Organised Retailers Post Strong Q2 Revenue Growth, but Gold Jewellery Demand by Volume Falls 20% While Value Rises 16%; Crisil Sees 21-23% Revenue Growth in FY27 Despite 4-6% Volume Decline

Core Theme 
Higher gold prices are lifting jewellers’ revenues even as the weight of gold sold falls about 20%, pushing retailers to lean on lighter, lower-karat and studded designs and on gold exchange programmes to sustain sales and protect margins.

The Divergence: Value Up, Volume Down
Organised jewellery retailers reported strong revenue growth in the September quarter (Q2 FY27), but higher gold prices continued to mask weakness in the volume of gold consumers are buying

India’s gold jewellery demand by volume fell 20% year-on-year in the quarter, even as the value of jewellery demand increased 16%, according to the World Gold Council

Consumers are spending more on jewellery but buying less gold by weight

The trend is expected to continue through the current fiscal year

Crisil Outlook and Gold Prices
Crisil Ratings expects revenue of organised jewellery retailers to grow 21-23% in FY27, even as sales volumes decline 4-6%

Gold prices are expected to average 25-27% higher than the previous fiscal year, supporting revenue growth despite weaker demand by volume

The price of 24K gold fell from ₹1,63,437 per 10 grams on 24 August to ₹1,38,192 on 12 November

The pullback was driven by hotter US inflation and strong jobs data, which fuelled expectations that the Federal Reserve would hold or raise interest rates

Higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar made non-yielding bullion less attractive compared with interest-bearing assets, while profit-booking, ETF outflows and broader equity-market selling added to the pressure

Company Results
Titan reported 24% year-on-year growth in its jewellery business to ₹17,495 crore in Q2 FY27, excluding bullion and digital gold

Kalyan Jewellers reported a 32% increase in consolidated revenue to ₹10,323 crore; same-store sales growth of about 20% in India, while Titan did not disclose same-store sales growth

BlueStone’s Ebitda more than doubled in Q2 FY27, its fourth consecutive profitable quarter on a standalone basis; revenue from operations rose 43% to ₹738 crore

Shift Toward Affordability
With gold prices elevated, retailers see consumers prioritising design, variety and affordability, driving a shift toward lighter pieces, studded jewellery and products across price points

Ajoy Chawla, MD of Titan: “We have seen fantastic growth at a consolidated level across most of our brands and businesses... driven by a lot of focus on innovation and prioritising growth over everything else, given the opportunity that India offers”

Consumers are increasingly moving from 22-karat to lower-karat options; Mangesh Chauhan, Sky Gold managing director: the karatage shift is from 22-karat to 18, 14 and 9-karat, with youngsters wanting lower karatage at a very decent budget

Titan also sees the gold exchange as an important tool to sustain purchases; Arun Narayan, CEO of Titan’s jewellery division, said it is a long-term strategic decision

Kalyan is using cash-for-gold programmes alongside exchange to protect margins; gold-for-cash transactions accounted for 7-8% of the business, taking the overall exchange share to 42%, which helped keep margins stable in Q2

BlueStone’s Gaurav Singh Kushwaha: “today’s customer wants to feel elegant and aspirational, and wants her jewellery to do that for her”

Texmaco Rail: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Revenue improved over Q1 but is still well below last year because Indian Railways is ordering fewer wagons. The order book has shifted toward exports and private buyers.

Q2 FY27 (Standalone)
Revenue: ₹860 Cr, up 15% QoQ (Quarter-on-Quarter), down about 31% YoY
EBITDA: ₹88 Cr, margin 10.2%
PBT (Profit Before Tax): ₹51 Cr vs ₹44 Cr in Q1
Wagons delivered: 1,106
Foundry output: 6,468 tonnes

1.  Less dependent on Indian Railways-
Revenue fell from about ₹1,250 Cr last year mainly because Railways ordered fewer wagons. Private and export orders now make up 80-85% of the wagon order book. Exports are 54% of the order book, up from 9% a year ago.

2.  Order book gives visibility-
Wagon orders of about ₹8,000 Cr will be delivered over the next 10 quarters. Another ₹3,000-3,500 Cr of infra and component orders are due this year and next. The South Africa order (₹4,000 Cr of wagons plus ₹1,300 Cr of locomotives) starts adding revenue only from FY28.

3.  Other businesses are growing-
Businesses other than wagons now bring about 37% of revenue, up from 25%. The electrical infra business did about ₹250 Cr this quarter and has ₹1,600 Cr of orders pending.

4.  Balance sheet is improving-
CRISIL upgraded its rating from A to A+, and debt is falling every quarter. Management says capex will be funded from internal cash. About ₹200 Cr has been set aside for new businesses.

5.  Investors pushed back on credibility-
One investor asked for clarity on the ₹700 Cr provision made earlier, and management pointed to its past disclosure. Another said the company keeps promising better quarters without delivering. Exports of components to the US were also hurt by changing tariffs.

Key Guidance
- Vision 2030 target: ₹9,000-10,000 Cr revenue
- Foundry output of 35,000-40,000 tonnes in FY27, with 25-30% exported

🔹 Kotak is betting on India’s faster-growing IT challengers, with Persistent, Coforge and Tech Mahindra emerging as preferred picks over several large-cap peers.

🔹 Tech Mahindra, Persistent Systems, Coforge, Mphasis and Tata Consultancy Services are among the key Indian IT stocks in focus on Friday, November 13, after a mixed September-quarter performance and fresh volatility in US technology shares.

🔹 Kotak Institutional Equities stated that they favoured mid-tier IT companies with stronger revenue growth, naming Tech Mahindra, Coforge, Persistent, Indegene and Sagility among its top Buy-rated picks.

🔹 The latest Nasdaq decline, led by weakness in Nvidia $NVDA, adds to near-term market concerns, although gains in AMD $ AMD and Broadcom $AVGO suggest that selling has not spread across all AI-related stocks.

🔹 Kotak prefers companies that can grow through market-share gains and new client additions rather than relying on valuation gains.

🔹 In its November 11 report, the brokerage said it retains its preference for challengers and hybrids over incumbents.

🔹 Persistent Systems reported 20% year-on-year constant-currency revenue growth in the September quarter, while Coforge recorded 43% growth.

🔹 Tech Mahindra delivered 7.2% growth, making it a strong performer among larger IT companies.

🔹 Kotak expects Persistent to lead the sector with 19.9% organic revenue growth in FY27, followed by Coforge at 13.8%.

🔹 Tech Mahindra is expected to grow 6% in FY27.

🔹 The brokerage has also retained Mphasis among its preferred companies, expecting organic revenue growth of 8% in FY27.

🔹 Its preference among large-cap IT companies remains Tata Consultancy Services, with a fair value of Rs 2,500.

🔹 US technology stocks ended lower on Thursday, November 12, after a volatile trading session.

🔹 The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.40% to 25,363.75, while the S&P 500 declined 0.34% and the Dow Jones fell 0.36%.

🔹 Nvidia $NVDA shares closed 4.34% lower after falling as much as 14% during the session following reports of chief executive Jensen Huang’s departure.

🔹 AMD $ AMD gained 5.86%, while Broadcom $AVGO also advanced more than 5%.

🔹 The contrasting performance suggests that the pressure was concentrated in specific companies rather than being a uniform sell-off across AI-related stocks.

🔹 For Indian IT companies, the key question is whether weakness in US technology shares affects enterprise technology budgets.

🔹 A sustained reduction in spending could affect demand for outsourcing, cloud services and software development.

🔹 Continued AI adoption could support demand for implementation, integration and managed services.

🔹 Indian IT services companies depend heavily on overseas clients, particularly in North America.

🔹 Kotak’s assessment of the September quarter points to some improvement in deal activity.

🔹 Financial services demand remained relatively strong, while hiring resumed selectively across companies.

🔹 The brokerage noted that deal wins were strong across companies with the exception of Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro.

🔹 It also cautioned that AI automation could put pressure on traditional services revenue.

🔹 Companies will need to generate fresh business from AI implementation and other technology services to offset this pressure.

🔹 Kotak said accelerating AI revenue growth on an increasing base has not increased overall revenue growth outlook for these companies.

🔹 Tata Consultancy Services recorded 2.8% year-on-year growth in the September quarter, while Infosys and HCLTech reported 1.5% and 2.6%, respectively.

🔹 Wipro’s growth stood at 0.6% in the September quarter.

🔹 Kotak expects organic revenue to decline 0.5% at Infosys and 3.6% at Wipro in FY27.

🔹 It expects Tata Consultancy Services to grow 2.6%, while HCLTech is projected to grow 2.5% in FY27.

🔹 Kotak expects Persistent and Coforge to lead sequential revenue growth among mid-tier companies in the December quarter, followed by Mphasis.

🔹 Tech Mahindra is also expected to deliver modest growth in the December quarter.

🔹 The brokerage expects a sequential revenue decline at Infosys, Wipro and Hexaware, while Tata Consultancy Services and LTIMindtree are expected to report modest growth.

🔹 Deal conversion, client spending and employee furloughs will be important factors to track.

🔹 Margins also need attention as companies face higher competition, AI-related investment costs and pressure on traditional services pricing.

ARC Recovery From Stressed Mortgage Loans May Rise 10%, Says Crisil: Recoveries Seen Improving to 110-120% From 93-100%, Driven by Small-Ticket Accounts From NBFCs and Stronger Enforcement Rights

Core Theme 
ARCs are on course for better recoveries on stressed mortgage loans, with ratios rising to 110-120%, as small-ticket NBFC accounts, stronger enforcement rights and better collateral lift performance, and retail recoveries (up 25%) outpace corporate ones (up 18%).

The Forecast: Recoveries Set to Improve
Asset reconstruction companies (ARCs) are expected to show an over 10% improvement in recoveries from stressed mortgage loans (110-120% from 93-100%), Crisil Ratings said on Thursday

The assessment is based on its rated, mortgage-backed retail security receipts (SR) portfolio, comprising about ₹1,100 crore of SRs issued both in FY26 and FY25, and about ₹800 crore in FY24, the agency said

What Is Driving the Improvement
A higher share of small-ticket accounts acquired from NBFCs, where ARCs benefit from stronger enforcement rights

Improved collateral coverage

A growing proportion of acquisitions from regions where there is stronger servicing and recovery capabilities

Industry View
Hari Hara Mishra, chief executive, Association of ARCs in India, told FE there has been an overall improvement in the recovery climate in the real estate sector across the housing, commercial and logistics segments

Year-on-year growth in recovery in retail portfolios of ARCs was higher at 25%, against 18% for the corporate book in FY26

The retail recovery was ₹8,000 crore, of which ₹6,000 crore was from secured credit

Uflex profit up 683% YoY to ₹210.6 Cr, but down 50% from Q1

👉 Uflex reported consolidated net profit of ₹210.6 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 682.9% from ₹26.9 Cr a year earlier but down 50.2% from ₹423.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. Revenue from operations was ₹4,821 Cr, up 25.8% year on year and down 10.2% sequentially from ₹5,366 Cr. Profit before tax came in at ₹258.5 Cr against ₹490.5 Cr in the June quarter.

👉 The steeper fall came in operating margins. OPM slipped to 5.3% from 9.1% in Q1 and from 1.1% a year earlier, a 378 bps sequential decline. Profit before other income was ₹210 Cr against ₹459.4 Cr in Q1. Other income of ₹48.5 Cr, up 67.8% YoY, was a small support and did not offset the drop.

👉 Consolidated cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹1,365 Cr at September 30, 2026 from ₹984 Cr at March 31, 2026. Consolidated borrowings, current and non-current, totalled about ₹10,722 Cr against ₹9,853 Cr in March. Trade receivables increased to ₹4,398 Cr from ₹3,861 Cr, and inventories to ₹3,165 Cr from ₹2,408 Cr. Receivables and stock rose even as quarterly revenue fell 10.2%.

👉 Growth is slowing against management's plan. Half-year revenue from operations was ₹10,187 Cr, up about 32% from ₹7,733 Cr in H1 FY26. Management has guided roughly 35% revenue and EBITDA growth for FY27, and the company record shows Q1 revenue growth of 37.6% YoY, so Q2's 25.8% is a clear step down.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management guided about 35% revenue and EBITDA growth for FY27 and expects ₹1,900-2,000 Cr of capex to be capitalised in the year.

👉 Road blocker: OPM compressed to 5.3% from 9.1% in Q1 while finance costs rose to ₹232.7 Cr from ₹188.1 Cr a year earlier, and CRISIL revised the outlook to Negative in August.

"De cultuur van de klacht leidt het Westen naar de decadentie"

06/09/2011 – 00:23

"Een goede vrouw maakt je gelukkig: de slechte maakt je filosoof", ironiseert de swami (meester) Parthasarathy, en de ondernemer Luis Daswani knikt instemmend. Daswani is pionier van de vedanta in Catalonië en heeft een loge in het Camp Nou, waar hij goed karma geeft aan Barça. De vedanta is geen religie, geen sekte, vraagt geen geld en geen gelovigen. Het is een millennia-oude discipline van rede, waaruit tradities als de socratische, de aristotelische, de christelijke en de islamitische hebben geput. Van haar leer ik neutralisatie: om meer van de drank te genieten, drink minder (dit geldt voor elk plezier). En hij leert me hoe problemen te lokaliseren: zoek het probleem in jezelf – corrigeer je houding – en stop met de schuld bij anderen te leggen. In jou ligt elk probleem en elke oplossing.Een cultuur die alleen op individuele rechten is gebaseerd, leidt noch tot persoonlijke noch tot collectieve harmonie, want wie is opgevoed in de overtuiging dat hij recht heeft op alles, vindt altijd redenen tot klagen.

En is dat niet zo?

Integendeel: als je leeft in de overtuiging dat je alle rechten hebt, geloof je dat de enige reden van je ontevredenheid is dat iemand ze je niet heeft gegeven. Op die manier verlies je de kans om verantwoordelijkheden te hebben. En daardoor ben je ongelukkig, want je verliest de controle over je eigen bestaan.

Waarom?

Omdat, als je alleen gelooft rechten te hebben, de oorzaak van je ontevredenheid niet in jezelf ligt, maar in de anderen, in iets wat anderen je niet geven. En door zo te denken word je een verwend en afhankelijk kind, aan wie, hoeveel men ook geeft, altijd iets ontbreekt.

Is de cultuur van de rechten ook die van de klacht en de ontevredenheid?

Precies. Daarom klaagt het Westen altijd en daarom zijn jullie altijd ontevreden, hoeveel jullie ook hebben.

Nu hebben we misschien wel redenen.

Alles hangt samen. De cultuur van de klacht is de reden van de decadentie van het Westen. Want behalve ontevreden maakt die cultuur van individuele rechten zonder enige sociale verantwoordelijkheid jullie ook egoïstisch en improductief.

Diezelfde cultuur maakte ons – tot nu toe – welvarender dan wie ook.

De tijd heeft de dingen op hun plaats gezet, en toen India en Azië eindelijk bevrijd waren van jullie kolonialisme, heeft ons gevoel van verantwoordelijkheid ons in staat gesteld opnieuw welvarend te worden.Hoe?

India en heel Azië en hun collectivistische samenlevingen zijn gebaseerd op het gevoel van plicht tegenover de anderen: het volk, de familie, de samenleving. Daarom concurreren we nu al met jullie op economisch terrein.

Ik zie het verband niet helemaal…

Een samenleving zoals de westerse, gebaseerd op het voortdurend opeisen van rechten, veroordeelt hen tot de klacht. En de schuldigen zijn altijd de anderen: de Staat, de ondernemer, je familie, de politici, de gemeente… Maar het ergste is dat je op die manier de verantwoordelijkheid voor je leven overlaat aan iemand die jij niet bent. Jij zou juist degene moeten zijn die beslist over je eigen voldoening.

Hoe herwin je het initiatief?

Door te geven. Door je leven te baseren op verplichtingen en verantwoordelijkheden. Dat zou jullie westerlingen opnieuw productiever maken. Want om iets te krijgen waarvan je denkt dat je het verdient, hoef je alleen maar voldoende aan te dringen en zelfs te klagen, en misschien krijg je het uiteindelijk. Maar om iets aan anderen te kunnen geven, moet je het eerst hebben geproduceerd en gecreëerd, en daarna gul zijn.

Geven is hier niet de heersende cultuur.

Als je je bestaan fundeert op verantwoordelijkheid en de gulheid van geven, herwin je de controle over je eigen bestaan. Want geven hangt alleen van jou af; ontvangen stelt je bloot aan de willekeur van anderen. Als je je gezin alleen sticht om liefde en rechten te ontvangen, zul je nooit genoeg krijgen en eindig je met het te verlaten.

Waarom?

Omdat de enige manier om een duurzaam gezin te hebben is te leven om het alles te geven. Mijn enige vrouw en ik zijn 58 jaar getrouwd… en gelukkig. Omdat we nooit dachten aan wat de ander ons verschuldigd is, maar aan wat we hem en onze kinderen kunnen geven. De dag dat je meer denkt aan wat je ontvangt dan aan wat je geeft, verliest het gezin elke zin. Het zal je nooit genoeg geven.

Vereist die houding religie?

Ze is universeel en eeuwig in de mens die zichzelf kent. De beschavingen die vooruitgaan, zijn gefundeerd op gulheid, op mensen die werken, scheppen en aan anderen geven.Adam Smith geloofde dat individuele egoïsmen, bemiddeld in efficiënte markten, collectieve welvaart scheppen.

Dat soort activiteit kan je welvaart geven, maar geen innerlijke vrede. Het is niet dat welvaart op zich slecht is, maar als ze niet gepaard gaat met innerlijke groei, voldoet ze niemand. Integendeel, die hyperactiviteit stress je en maakt je verwaand en onhandelbaar.

Waarom?

Omdat het enige echte plezier dat iets winnen geeft, is het te kunnen delen. Dat ontdekt de vedanta al millennia. En daaruit putten Plato, Socrates, Jezus Christus en Mohammed. En duizenden meesters van alle culturen.

Waaruit bestaat het?

Er is geen blinde geloof nodig, noch ascese, noch grote openbaringen. Je zult tot die waarheid komen door je eigen gezond verstand. Het gaat er niet om heilig te zijn, maar eenvoudig verstandig.

Mentale discipline?

Volwassenheid. En ik bedoel niet de opeenhoping van kennis, maar levenswijsheid. Het plezier bijvoorbeeld brengt ongenoegen met zich mee. Als je drinkt om plezier, zul je uiteindelijk lijden onder de drank, tenzij je leert je begeerte te beheersen – dat is de neutralisatie – en volwassen wordt tot je ontdekt dat minder drinken de beste manier is om er meer van te genieten.

Het hangt ook af van met wie je drinkt.

De oorzaak van een slechte relatie ligt niet in de ander, maar in je eigen houding. Het gebrek zit niet in de vriend, de auto, het huis, de echtgenote… maar in jezelf, in je houding tegenover hen. Elk conflict in een relatie is een gelegenheid om jezelf te bestuderen en te corrigeren. Voordat je over anderen klaagt, bestudeer jezelf en je zult zien dat het probleem in jou ligt.

Na středečním zastupitelstvu Prahy 8 jsem byl zvolen předsedou finančního výboru. Budu tak mít možnost přímo dohlížet na to, jak naše městská část hospodaří se svým téměř jeden a půl miliardovým rozpočtem. Je to velká odpovědnost a výzva. Nebudu lhát, že není.

Bylo mi vyčítáno, že nejsem bankéř a nepracuji ve finančním sektoru. Ano, nejsem bankéř. Zato jsem ale řídil a sestavoval milionové rozpočty, studoval ekonomiku a účetnictví a umím číst čísla. Rozpočet Prahy 8 jsem navíc v posledních letech bedlivě sledoval a komentoval. 

Je to prostě výzva a ty já mám rád. Přistupuju k tomu s pokorou. Chci funkci předsedy finančního výboru vykonávat minimálně se stejným nasazením, s jakým jsem poslední čtyři roky vedl kontrolní výbor. Ten patřil k nejaktivnějším v historii Prahy 8. A rád bych na tuhle práci navázal i ve finančním výboru.

Středeční zastupitelstvo ale nebylo jen o výborech. Bylo hlavně o složení nového vedení Prahy 8.

Musím říct, že pětičlenná rada pro městskou část se sto tisíci obyvateli, která je větší než většina krajských měst, mi přijde opravdu malá. Uvidíme, jestli se její složení v příštích měsících změní. Mám za to, že takový model je dlouhodobě neudržitelný.

Novým starostou se stal Tomáš Hřebík ze Starostů. S Piráty jsme ho při volbě podpořili a ještě jednou mu gratuluju ke zvolení. Stejně tak jsme podpořili dva nové místostarosty Martina Jedličku a Tomáše Slabihoudka z TOP 09.

A to z jednoduchého důvodu. Celou dobu jsme usilovali o to, abychom společně se STAN, TOP 09 a 8žije složili městotvornou koalici. Bylo by od nás velmi pokrytecké, kdybychom teď pro ty stejné lidi nehlasovali.

Naopak jsme nepodpořili zástupce ODS, tedy Vladimíru Ludkovou a Davida Straku. Důvod je stále stejný a říkáme ho dlouhodobě. ODS a Praha 8 by si od sebe měly na nějaký čas odpočinout.

Do čela kontrolního výboru jsme podpořili kandidáta 8žije, Prahy sobě a Zelených Václava Stránského. Bohužel mu ke zvolení chyběly čtyři hlasy. Proto jsme následně podpořili opozičního kolegu z Patriotů Jiřího Vítka. Zkrátka proto, že kontrolní výbor má podle nás vést opozice. 

S Piráty jsme šli do voleb s heslem Ať to tu žije. A je pravda, že na středečním zastupitelstvu to žilo, ale trochu jinak, než jsme si představovali. Mrzí mě především to, že petice občanů nebyla projednána hned na začátku jednání. Hlas lidí a našich sousedů, kterým záleží na budoucnosti Prahy 8, by měl dostat prostor.

Po volbách máme sice jen tříčlenný zastupitelský klub, ale budeme pracovat minimálně za šest. Dobré nápady podpoříme, ty špatné budeme kritizovat. Budeme konstruktivní, ale důslednou opozicí. Stejně jako doposud.

Protože nám na Osmičce záleží. A chceme, aby to tu opravdu žilo. 🏴‍☠️

Oswal Pumps | Q2 FY27 results

Oswal Pumps' Q2 net profit falls 61% to ₹38 Cr; operating margin drops to 9.3%

👉 Oswal Pumps reported consolidated revenue of ₹506.3 Cr for Q2 FY27, down 6.2% from ₹539.6 Cr a year earlier and up 6.9% from ₹473.6 Cr in Q1. Net profit for the period was ₹38.2 Cr, against ₹97.5 Cr in Q2 FY26 and ₹54.1 Cr in Q1, a 60.8% fall year on year. Profit before tax was ₹47.4 Cr. No exceptional items were booked in the quarter. Other income fell to ₹5.5 Cr from ₹6.9 Cr a year earlier.

👉 Operating margin contracted to 9.3%, from 23.1% a year ago and 14.2% in Q1. Cost of materials consumed rose to ₹394.5 Cr from ₹287.0 Cr in Q1, while the change in inventories showed a ₹107 Cr build-up. Employee costs rose to ₹29.1 Cr and other expenses to ₹69.7 Cr. Finance costs were ₹11.2 Cr, up from ₹4.5 Cr a year earlier, as current borrowings increased.

👉 Trade receivables climbed to ₹1,319 Cr at September 30, 2026, from ₹1,128 Cr at March 31, 2026, while inventories rose to ₹376 Cr from ₹221 Cr. Cash and cash equivalents fell to ₹4.9 Cr from ₹90.7 Cr, and current borrowings rose to ₹507 Cr from ₹214 Cr. Net cash used in operating activities for the half year was ₹275 Cr, against ₹92 Cr a year earlier. Purchases of property, plant and equipment were ₹65 Cr.

👉 Against FY27 guidance given on earnings calls of 20-25% revenue growth and a 22-23% EBITDA margin, the half-year shows revenue down 7.0% and Q2 operating margin at 9.3%. ICRA reaffirmed the A+ long-term rating on September 23 but revised the outlook from stable to negative. It cited substantial receivable build-up and moderating profitability amid competitive intensity.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans a 1.2 GW solar cell manufacturing facility in Karnal through subsidiary OSEPL, with a total investment of ₹456 Cr, per the October 10 filing.

👉 Road blocker: ICRA revised the outlook to negative on September 23, 2026, citing substantial receivable build-up and moderating profitability, with trade receivables at ₹1,319 Cr.

Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers | Q2 FY27 results

RCF Q2 profit rises 24% to ₹130.9 Cr as margins widen to 3.5%

👉 Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilizers reported consolidated net profit of ₹130.9 Cr for Q2 FY27, up 24.3% from ₹105.3 Cr a year earlier and up 78.1% from ₹73.5 Cr in Q1. Revenue from operations was ₹5,063 Cr, down 4.3% year on year but up 41.2% sequentially. Profit before tax was ₹177.1 Cr. Earnings per share were ₹2.37, against ₹1.91 a year ago.

👉 Operating profit before other income rose 72.6% to ₹154.5 Cr, with operating margin at 3.5% against 2.6% a year earlier and 2.8% in Q1. Other income dropped to ₹22.6 Cr from ₹51.1 Cr, so it added less to the bottom line than last year. Finance costs rose to ₹65.5 Cr from ₹54.8 Cr. No exceptional items were booked in the quarter.

👉 Fertiliser revenue rose 33.9% year on year to ₹3,945 Cr, but its segment result of ₹84.9 Cr was below ₹108.5 Cr a year ago. Industrial chemicals revenue climbed to ₹506 Cr from ₹327 Cr, and its result rose to ₹144.9 Cr from ₹41.8 Cr. Trading revenue fell 70% to ₹608 Cr from ₹2,013 Cr, and trading result dropped to ₹10.6 Cr from ₹47.5 Cr.

👉 Half-year net profit rose to ₹204.5 Cr from ₹159.8 Cr, while revenue of ₹8,649 Cr was almost unchanged. The filing also records a Thal unit energy norm revision, notified by the Department of Fertilizers on July 30, 2026, with a cumulative financial impact of ₹231.71 Cr through September 30, 2026, of which ₹60.17 Cr was recognised in Q2. Separately, ₹217.50 Cr of differential subsidy remains pending with DoF.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management approved a ₹797 Cr order to L&T on September 25, 2026, to revamp the Thal ammonia plant to improve efficiency and cut energy consumption.

👉 Road blocker: Management flagged the revised Thal unit energy norms, which carry a ₹231.71 Cr cumulative financial impact through September 30, 2026, and ₹217.50 Cr of differential subsidy is still pending settlement by DoF.

V sobotu na Pasonetce, konferenci kolegů a kolegyň ze Sekce mladých lékařů ČLK. 

Má role byla dvojí. Prvně jsem vedl workshop na téma Záda z pohledu neurochirurga. A to z toho důvodu, že na problémy s páteří u nás i ve světě trpí hrozně moc lidí. Přitom většina potíží časem, za pomoci léků na bolest, změny zátěže v práci, zlepšení životosprávy (zhubnutí, jídelníček…), rehabilitace a aktivního pravidelného cvičení vymizí. Jen velká menšina si nakonec vyžádá operační sál. Což je dobře! A měli by o tom vědět jak samotní pacienti, tak lékařky a lékaři různých odborností, nejvíc asi praktici a neurologové. Věřím, že právě takovýmto mezioborovým sdílením zkušeností tomuto napomůžeme.

V druhém kole jsem se účastnil jako předseda spolku Mladí lékaři panelové debaty s ministrem zdravotnictví o reformě specializačního vzdělávání lékařů, a to směrem k tzv. kompetenčnímu modelu. Ten jako Mladí lékaři podporujeme a podílíme se v rámci pracovní skupiny na ministerstvu od samého začátku na jeho tvorbě. Nicméně i tak jsem měl v prvé řadě dotaz na to, jak budou (v případě, že budou, na čemž trváme) financováni školitelé. Protože papír snese všechno, a na naprosté většině se koneckonců v obecné rovině shodneme. Jakmile ale přijde na peníze, mohou nastat znenadání závažné komplikace, známe to. Ministr Vojtěch se nechal slyšet, že s odměňováním školitelů se počítá. A jednou cestou, jak toto zprocesovat (i s přihlédnutím k roztříštěnosti poskytovatelů zdravotní péče), je skrz bonifikace, úhrady zdravotními pojišťovnami.

Opravdu si přeji, aby se tato reforma vzdělávání uskutečnila, protože k tomu máme nyní jedinečnou příležitost, která se dlouho nemusí opakovat. Na naší straně pro to uděláme maximum!

EAAA India Alternatives: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

This was the first earnings call since listing. Fundraising was strong in the first half, and profit grew 35%.

H1 FY27
Total income: ₹616 Cr, up 35% YoY (Year-on-Year)
Management fees: ₹333 Cr, up 24%
PAT (Profit After Tax): ₹169 Cr, up 35%
Q2 PAT: ₹88 Cr, up 28% YoY

Fee-paying AUM (Assets Under Management): ₹49,164 Cr, up 28%
ROE (Return on Equity): 29.5%
Dividend: ₹7 per share

1.  What the company does-
EAAA (formerly Edelweiss Alternatives) runs private funds that own roads, solar plants and office parks, and that lend to companies. Investors get regular income from tolls, rent and interest. The company earns a fee on fee-paying AUM, which is the money already invested.

2.  About ₹20,000 Cr raised in six months-
It raised ₹8,250 Cr in its funds and ₹12,000 Cr in InvITs (Infrastructure Investment Trusts) during H1. Total AUM is ₹95,000 Cr. About ₹20,000-25,000 Cr of that is raised but not yet invested, and it will start earning fees once it is deployed.

3.  Money is being invested-
It won the TOT-19 road bundle for ₹2,259 Cr, covering about 600 lane km in Tamil Nadu. It also bought a 1 million sq ft office park in Pune. Its first infrastructure fund fully exited with about a 19% gross return.

4.  Performance fee is more predictable-
On top of regular fees, the company earns a share of profits once investors get a minimum return. Because its income funds pay investors every year, that minimum return is easier to meet. Management expects this to be 25-30% of profit.

5.  Clients keep coming back-
77% of AUM comes from repeat clients. Institutions bring 49% and wealthy families bring 51%. Management fees grew slower than AUM because new money takes a few quarters to start earning.

Key Guidance
- Fee-paying AUM and PAT to grow 20-25% a year (stated range 20-30%) over the medium term
- ROE around 30%, with about 50% of profit paid as dividend

Motoristé dlouhodobě a cíleně destruují ministerstvo životního prostředí a spolu s ním i Krkonošský národní park.

V posledních týdnech sílí kritika nového ředitele Správy Krkonošského národní parku Petra Moravce. Vymezují se vůči němu jak zaměstnanci parku a odborná veřejnost, tak i místní senátor a starosta Vrchlabí Jan Sobotka nebo tisíce občanů. Abychom porozuměli tomu, co se v Krkonoších děje, musíme se vrátit na začátek letošního roku.

1️⃣ V březnu – zčistajasna – odvolal ministr životního prostředí Igor Červený z pozice ředitele Krkonošského národního parku Robina Bönische, který jej vedl od roku 2018. Ten byl opakovaně terčem výpadů sponzorky Motoristů a provozovatelky Labské a Luční boudy Kláry Sovové, jež za stranu nakonec kandidovala v letošních komunálních volbách na pražskou primátorku.

🗨️ „Odvolat úspěšného ředitele jakékoliv státní instituce, natož národního parku bez udání důvodu, bez jediné výtky, je ve slušném demokratickém státě a mezi slušnými lidmi nepřijatelné. Potvrzuje se, že Motoristé uvolňují překážky v byznysu svým blízkým a jdou při tom přes mrtvoly. Tou překážkou je pro ně naše příroda,” shrnul Jaromír Bláha z hnutí DUHA.

2️⃣ Červený následně vypsal na uvolněné místo výběrové řízení, z něhož coby nový ředitel v červnu vzešel učitel České lesnické akademie Trutnov Petr Moravec. Proti jeho jmenování se obratem vymezil například Svazek obcí Východní Krkonoše, který zpochybnil jeho odborné schopnosti. Současně upozornil na skutečnost, že Moravec v minulosti, kdy měl malý úvazek ve Bönischově kanceláři, zneužíval služební auto a „fixloval” docházku. 

3️⃣ V říjnu Moravec – bez vědomí ředitelů ostatních tří národních parků – svévolně založil Asociaci národní parků České republiky, přestože instituci stejného názvu parky mají již od roku 2024. Od zaměstnanců Správy Krkonošského národního parku zaznívaly hlasy o podrazu na všechny národní parky, včetně toho krkonošského. 

4️⃣ Nový ředitel současně začal připravovat škrty v oblasti pracovních úvazků a nenadále odvolal dva své náměstky – vedoucího odboru vnějších vztahů Jakuba Kašpara a vedoucího odboru vnitřních věcí Luďka Khola, kteří v národním parku pracovali osmnáct, respektive 32 let. Reakcí na Moravcovy kroky byly protesty před ministerstvem životního prostředí i sídlem správy parku a vyhlášení stávkové pohotovost odborů Krkonošského národního parku.

‼️ „Současný ministr životního prostředí chce v záležitostech národního parku dosáhnout stejného cíle, jaký měl po ruské okupaci Československa v srpnu 1968 ustanovený totalitní režim — zlikvidovat dobře fungující pracovní tým a výsledky jeho práce v oblasti ochrany přírody, vědy a výzkumu,” shrnul zakladatel Krkonošského národního parku a žijící legenda české ochrany přírody Josef Fanta.

➡️ Současně pak vznesl požadavek, aby byl Moravec ze své funkce okamžitě odvolán.

The Hinduism Religion 

Hinduism does not have a single holy book like the Quran or the Bible; instead, it has a vast, diverse body of sacred texts divided into two main categories: Shruti ("that which is heard") and Smriti ("that which is remembered"). 

https://t.co/r8uTsIShS6

1. Shruti (Revealed Scriptures)

Shruti texts are considered eternal, authorless (apaurusheya), and divinely heard by ancient sages in deep states of meditation. 

https://t.co/9ltSk7RycO

•The Four Vedas: The oldest and most foundational sacred texts of Hinduism, comprising:

◦Rigveda: The oldest text, containing hymns and verses dedicated to various deities.

◦Samaveda: Musical chants and melodies adapted from the Rigveda.

◦Yajurveda: Formulas and instructions for sacred rituals and sacrifices (yajna).

◦Atharvaveda: Practical spells, charms, and philosophical prose. 

https://t.co/eRuBil4018

•Upanishads: Philosophical and mystical texts located at the end of the Vedas (Vedanta) that explore the nature of reality, the soul (Atman), and the universal spirit (Brahman). 

https://t.co/o20AIGikOI

2. Smriti (Derived and Remembered Texts)

Smriti texts are composed by human sages to explain, expand upon, and translate the deep wisdom of Shruti through stories, epics, and laws. 

https://t.co/u6pyBTAjoD

•Itihasas (Epics):

◦Mahabharata: A massive epic narrating a great dynastic war, which famously embeds the Bhagavad Gita—a 700-verse spiritual dialogue on duty (dharma), action (karma), and devotion between Prince Arjuna and Lord Krishna.

◦Ramayana: The epic poem by Valmiki detailing the life of Prince Rama, his rescue of Sita, and the ideal principles of righteousness. 

https://t.co/izw5m6aGnN

•Puranas: Extensive mythological and historical texts detailing creation, cosmology, royal genealogies, and devotion to major deities like Vishnu, Shiva, and Devi. 

https://t.co/appfwTAp1F

•Dharmashastras & Sutras: Guides on ethics, law, daily conduct, and spiritual practices like Yoga. 

https://t.co/dMpYFrgwYr

Two Deals in One Week: Why Global Investors Are Betting Big on India’s NBFCs

This week, two global investors wrote big cheques to Indian lenders. On Tuesday, Blackstone agreed to buy about 16% of IIFL Finance for 50 billion rupees, about $535 million. The same week, Singapore’s Temasek said it will invest roughly $265 million in Godrej Capital.

That is about $800 million in one week. It is also the latest in a year full of such deals.

First, what’s an NBFC?

A non-banking financial company lends like a bank, with vehicle loans, home loans, gold loans and small-business credit. It is not a bank, and it follows a different set of rules.

The 2026 deal list
MUFG and Shriram Finance: Japan’s MUFG agreed in December 2025 to invest ₹39,618 crore for a 20% stake, which Business Standard described as the largest foreign direct investment ever in an Indian financial services company. The investment was completed in April 2026 at ₹840.93 per share.

IHC and Sammaan Capital: Abu Dhabi’s IHC announced in October 2025 that it would buy a controlling stake for ₹8,850 crore. On 31 March 2026, IHC said it had received all required regulatory approvals to acquire about 41.5%.

Carlyle and Nido Home Finance: Carlyle agreed to take a strategic majority stake for ₹2,100 crore. That includes buying 45% from Edelweiss and putting ₹1,500 crore of fresh equity into the company.

Advent International and Aditya Birla Housing Finance: On 3 February, Advent said it would acquire a 14.3% stake for ₹2,750 crore.

The bigger picture

Reuters cites Grant Thornton data showing that about $5.4 billion of private equity money flowed into India’s financial sector in 2025, up 6% from 2024. Another $3.6 billion came in through the end of September this year. That data covers the whole financial sector, not NBFCs alone.

Why the interest?

Reuters says foreign investors have been drawn by strong demand for credit in the economy and low loan delinquencies.

The IIFL deal shows how these investments work. The company says the money is meant to strengthen its capital adequacy, improve its cost of funds and accelerate growth in its gold finance business. Capital adequacy is the cushion of capital a lender holds against the risks it takes. For IIFL, the company says it will rise to about 30% from 17%.

Two kinds of foreign money
Foreign money in India now moves in two different ways. Foreign portfolio investors, who trade listed shares, have been selling. NSDL data show they withdrew a record ₹3.08 trillion from Indian equities in the first nine months of 2026, against ₹1.66 trillion in all of 2025.

Meanwhile, the investors in the deals above are buying large stakes directly from the companies or their promoters. These are different activities with different goals. Selling shares on an exchange says little about stake deals like these.

Now, the rulebook
There is a regulatory development today. Reuters reports, citing two people with knowledge of the plans, that the RBI is working on proposals that would stop private equity firms from holding a controlling stake in more than one non-bank lender. The worry is that financial stress at a global private equity firm could spread across several lenders it has invested in.

The report adds that holdings of 15% or less would be treated as a financial investment and face less scrutiny. There is precedent. Bain Capital agreed in March 2025 to invest ₹4,385 crore in Manappuram Finance. The RBI approved Bain’s purchase of 41.7% on the condition that it divest its stake in another non-bank lender. The RBI did not respond to Reuters’ request for comment. A draft of the rules would be finalised after public consultation and could be issued early next year, the person said.
