KRAKOVSKÝ STŘELEZ
JINÝ POHLED
Co vidím, když se dívám na Krakov
 (odhad situace z veřejně dostupných zdrojů)
 Vidím mladého muže, který byl v úzkém kontaktu s rodiči. Jeho sestra s nimi nežila, ale občas přicházela. Mladý muž si dokázal vraždu naplánovat... počkal, až všichni doma usnou, a pak je postupně s tlumičem na zbrani zastřelil. Je to tedy lstivý člen rodiny... je to nepřítel, schopný do poslední chvíle předstírat neutralitu.
 
Považuji za důležité, že si na vraždu vybral právě ten čas, kdy byla sestra doma. Kdyby ji nechtěl zavraždit, počkal by na další noc, až by sestra odešla.
 
Z toho mi vyplývá, že sestra souvisí s motivem vraždy jeho rodiny.
 
Sestra byla otevřená, přátelská, se srdcem na dlani, umělecká duše, na kterou byli rodiče i veřejně hrdí.
 
Právě to mohlo v mladém muži, který celé roky nosil kapuci a nepozdravoval sousedy, vyvolat pocity žárlivosti na sestru, jejíž socializace a vztahy s lidmi šly tak snadno.
 
Mladý muž se celé roky izoloval od svého okolí. Schovával se před přímým pohledem. Přímý pohled nemají rádi například lidé s Aspergerovým syndromem, autisté nebo paranoidní jedinci.
 
V tomto případě trvalo jeho podivné chování k okolí roky, takže se nejednalo o náhlé propuknutí duševní choroby, ale jeho izolace od lidí a zvláštní záliby byly trvalé. Spíše bych to přisoudil Aspergerovu syndromu, protože jako autista by byl na střelnici příliš nápadný a pravděpodobně by neprošel ani psychologickými testy pro získání zbraně.
 
Jako člověk s Aspergerovým syndromem nemá vytvořeny hluboké citové vazby ke svému okolí, a proto myšlenky typu "Co by bylo, kdybych někoho zabil", mohly jeho hlavu zaplňovat bez větší překážky v podobě citové vazby na rodinu nebo v podobě výčitek svědomí.
 
Jeho spolužáci si vzpomínají, že kreslil bizarní násilné kresby, hákové kříže a on sám, ani oni, nezastírali, že tušili, že jednou někoho zabije. Ale když to přišlo, "nemohli uvěřit", že to udělal.
 
Prosím vás... vím, že ve svém klidném životě se s vrahy téměř nesetkáváte... ale když vám někdo řekne, že někoho zavraždí, tak mu věřte a jednejte.
 
Mnoho vrahů mluví mezi řádky o svých činech... občas žertují o vraždách... občas popíší, jak to udělali, nebo udělali... stačí jim jen naslouchat.
 
Nerada to píšu, protože nerada píšu o negativních aspektech obětí, ale mám pocit, že v tomto případě selhal otec útočníka. Selhal, protože měl netypického syna a i tak ho každou neděli vedl k lásce ke zbraním. Tento mladý muž se k zbraním vůbec neměl dostat.
 
Co jsem vnímala z popisů jeho útoků:
 
Že je to člověk trénovaný ve střelbě. Střílet za jízdy z jedoucího auta tak, že 30 procent obětí to nepřežije, to je silné číslo a ukazuje to na to, že takové něco v minulosti trénoval. Netrénovaný člověk nemá představu ani o tom, jak manipulovat s dlouhou puškou v autě, aby dostal hlaveň ven z okna... natož aby někoho za jízdy vůbec trefil.
 
Další moment, kdy se prozradily jeho speciální tréninky, které ale údajně nezískal na střelnici, kam chodí s otcem, bylo, když vystoupil z auta a ve vysokém stresu trefil každého, koho chtěl:
Řidiče auta, které jelo před ním, do čelisti.
Do jednoho policisty vystřelil tři náboje. Do druhého policisty jeden.
 
Potom se vycvičeným, taktickým krokem posouval kolem auta... i to se ho někdo naučil... civilisté takto nechodí, protože netuší, že takový typ pohybu se zbraní existuje... a pak udělal několik chyb najednou, které naštěstí vedly k jeho eliminaci.
 
Kdyby se nešel nesmyslně dívat na ležící policisty, mohl pokračovat dál ve vraždění civilistů... ale naštěstí něco v něm chtělo ještě něco dokázat policistům... a to ho spolu s nesprávným postupem při vykukování spoza překážky (kapota auta) stálo život.
 
Když policista na konci vytáhl turniket, aby si zastavil krvácení z postřelené ruky, věděla jsem, že tohle není běžný policista, ale také někdo velmi dobře vytrénovaný. Dnes bude mít asi velmi těžký den i noc.
 
Zabral život.
 
Zemřel člověk, i když terorista.
 
Doufám, že tento hrdinský zásah bude mít pro oba mladé policisty:
 
pro Jakuba Kulika a
 
Artura Moranského
 
co nejmenší negativní následky.

Finished reading @SoniaGandhi ji’s memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, last night.

Couldn’t stop once I had started.  It is riveting, deeply moving, and quietly shattering.

I am overwhelmed not only by her remarkable life, but by her candour, her nerves of steel, her sensitivity, and her ability to hold her head high in the face of cruel adversities. 

But above all, I am moved by her faith in love - the love that made her cross continents, love that nurtured her, the love she feels for India, the love that makes her belong. 

The love that was crushed before her eyes, yet the same love that has sustained her, and kept her going - again and again - and is the bedrock of everything she has done and continues to do.

What left me truly spellbound, though, is her sense of duty and responsibility.

I have admired her my entire life, but reading this book has deepened that respect into something I can’t explain in words. 

Despite unimaginable violence and irreparable losses, she never allowed herself to become bitter. Her capacity to forgive even those who destroyed her world - left me in awe. 

She is fully aware of the vicious lies her opponents have spread about her for decades. And she addresses each one with her trademark simplicity and dignity.

An intensely private person has finally chosen to tell her story on her own terms. For the first time, she speaks of battling cancer not once but twice. For the first time one gets to know that before her two children, she bore the pain of losing her firstborn. 

I wept as I read - a lot actually. It is almost unbearable to imagine the pain inflicted upon her, yet not once did she ever play victim.

She is deeply admired - for her courage, her grace, and the quiet strength with which she has carried so much. But the book will make many people understand her and love her - even more.

‘Belonging’ is not merely a memoir. It is a testament to a life lived with love as both compass and anchor, and to a woman who refused to let grief harden her heart. Some stories do not just move you, they stay with you, reminding you what true resilience looks like. This is one of them. 

At its heart, ‘Belonging’ is one of the greatest love stories of our time!

Pritika Auto Industries Ltd Concall Summary (Q2 FY27, 11 November 2026) #PRITIKAUTO

🟡 Management Guidance:
 Management targets revenue growth of approximately 15% to 20% YoY and an EBITDA margin of 14% to 15%. Margins could improve slightly once the Lost Foam Casting (LFC) facility is streamlined and reaches 50% to 60% utilisation and beyond. The company aims to increase installed capacity from the current 72,000 metric tonnes to approximately 80,000 metric tonnes by the end of November 2026, followed by another 24,000 metric tonnes by March 2028, taking total capacity to 1 lakh metric tonnes by the end of calendar year 2028. Management expects exports to contribute at least 10% to 15% of sales over the next three to five years. The Italian export order of approximately ₹12 crore annually has potential to increase to ₹40 crore to ₹50 crore over the next three years. The KION USA product has received customer approval, with regular production expected to commence in FY28. Pritika Engineering Components is expected to increase its contribution to approximately 30% to 35% of the business over the next 1 to 1.5 years. Management expects railway component supplies to begin around September or October 2027, following RDSO trials and testing. The company is also expanding its product portfolio in large castings, construction equipment and heavy commercial vehicles.

🟢 Green Alert: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue increased 31.55% YoY to ₹153.19 crore, compared with ₹116.45 crore. EBITDA grew 13.97% to ₹21.21 crore, while PAT increased 12.41% to ₹7.43 crore. Production volumes increased approximately 22% YoY to 15,665 metric tonnes. H1 FY27 production reached 30,000 metric tonnes, up nearly 19% from 25,267 metric tonnes. H1 consolidated revenue grew 29.04% to ₹298.16 crore, EBITDA increased 12.93% to ₹40.72 crore and PAT rose 14.52% to ₹14.55 crore. The company continues to receive repeat and incremental orders from established OEMs including Mahindra & Mahindra, Mahindra Swaraj, TAFE, CNH Industrial and Escorts Kubota. The Italian export order of approximately ₹12 crore per annum represents an important entry into the European precision engineering supply chain. KION USA has approved the product developed by Pritika Engineering Components, bringing it closer to commercial production. The company has a competitive advantage through integrated casting and machining capabilities, supported by Indian and Japanese machinery, advanced CNC and HMC machining, radiography and 3D precision scanning. Its Lost Foam Casting technology provides the ability to manufacture complex and critical large castings at lower capital expenditure than conventional green sand technology. The group has also signed a long-term solar power arrangement expected to generate approximately ₹110 crore in savings over 25 years.

🔴 Red Alert: Despite 31.55% revenue growth, EBITDA increased only 13.97%, resulting in EBITDA margin declining to 13.85% from 15.99% YoY. Management attributed the pressure primarily to higher raw material prices, particularly scrap and oil, which are passed on to customers with an approximately one-quarter lag. Margins improved sequentially from 13.45% in Q1 FY27 to 13.85% in Q2, and management expects improvement as cost pass-through takes effect. However, Q3 is normally a seasonally weaker quarter for the tractor and automotive industries because of post-Diwali demand moderation and planned maintenance. The company's expansion will require additional funding through a combination of debt and equity, and management explicitly indicated that net debt-to-equity could increase. The consolidated net debt-to-equity ratio was cited at approximately 0.67 for FY26. The next 24,000-tonne capacity expansion also requires land acquisition and greenfield construction, creating execution and capital-allocation risks. The Italian export order and KION USA opportunity are promising, but the latter will only enter regular production in FY28, and the larger potential contribution is not yet realised. Railway components are also dependent on RDSO approval, trials and testing, with commercial supplies targeted only from H2 FY28. Investors should distinguish between confirmed orders, customer approvals, enquiries and future opportunities.

🔵 Blue Alert: Pritika Auto is gradually moving beyond its traditional tractor-component business into commercial vehicles, construction equipment, railway components and international markets. Approximately 77% of its current business comes from the commercial vehicle segment, according to management's opening remarks, while tractor components remain a key part of its established manufacturing portfolio. The company is developing larger and more technically complex castings such as differential housings, transmission cases, crankcases and cylinder blocks, where competition is relatively lower and product realisations are better. Lost Foam Casting is a key differentiator, with Pritika stating that it is among the very few foundries in India operating this technology at scale. Its subsidiary Pritika Engineering Components has an Italian export order with potential to grow from ₹12 crore to ₹40 crore to ₹50 crore annually. KION USA approval could provide an entry point into the large US machine-castings market. The company is also developing two to three railway components, with RDSO trials targeted around January or February 2027. In commercial vehicles, it is increasing its product range and volumes with Ashok Leyland. The solar power agreement with SparkGrid is expected to provide long-term energy-cost visibility, with approximately ₹70 crore of the projected ₹110 crore savings benefiting Pritika Engineering Components and Mehta Casting, while Pritika Auto Industries receives the balance. The capacity expansion, including a future greenfield plant, is intended to support these new opportunities.

🧠 Deep Insight: Pritika Auto is transitioning from a relatively conventional casting manufacturer into a higher-value engineering and machining supplier. The most important growth drivers are not simply additional casting volumes, but the movement towards larger, complex components, integrated casting and machining, and international OEM relationships. Its Lost Foam Casting technology could be particularly valuable because it allows the company to manufacture critical large castings with lower capital expenditure than conventional green sand methods. However, the financial performance shows an important gap between revenue growth and profit growth. Q2 revenue increased 31.55%, but EBITDA grew only 13.97%, indicating that higher volumes have not yet translated into proportional operating leverage. The one-quarter raw material pass-through mechanism provides a possible explanation for temporary margin pressure, but the next few quarters will need to demonstrate actual recovery. The expansion from 72,000 to 1 lakh metric tonnes creates substantial growth capacity, although utilisation and returns on this additional investment will matter more than installed capacity alone. Exports are another major opportunity, but the ₹12 crore Italian order and KION USA approval should not be valued as though their full potential has already converted into revenue. The central investment thesis is that Pritika Auto is building a larger, technologically differentiated casting and machining platform, with exports, large castings and customer diversification providing the next phase of growth. Investors should monitor EBITDA margin recovery, capacity utilisation, debt-to-equity, the conversion of export opportunities into repeat orders, and the timely commissioning of the expanded capacity.

Texmaco Rail and Engineering Ltd Concall Summary (Q2 FY27, 11 November 2026) #TEXRAIL

🟡 Management Guidance: 
Management expects the company to deliver better results in the coming quarters, with a stronger rebound in the second half of FY27. The approximately ₹10,000 crore order book is expected to be executed over the coming periods, with freight rolling stock orders scheduled for execution over the next 10 quarters. Around ₹8,000 crore of freight rolling stock orders and ₹3,000 crore to ₹3,500 crore of infrastructure and component orders are expected to be executable during the current and next financial years. The South African turnkey order, covering wagons and locomotives, is scheduled for delivery during FY28 and one additional quarter, followed by a 15-year maintenance commitment. Revenue from this order is expected to begin from FY28, not H2 FY27. Foundry production is expected to reach at least 35,000 to 40,000 metric tonnes, with 25% to 30% coming from exports. Management has earmarked approximately ₹200 crore of capex for different purposes and has completed around 40% of its planned capex for the current year. It expects to fund growth and maintenance capex through internal operational surpluses, without requiring additional debt in the short term. The longer-term Vision 2030 ambition is to build a ₹9,000 crore to ₹10,000 crore revenue business, with ₹4,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore from core businesses and the balance from diversification.

🟢 Green Alert: Standalone revenue from operations increased 15% QoQ to approximately ₹863 crore, compared with ₹753 crore in Q1 FY27. EBITDA stood at ₹88 crore, with a margin of 10.2%, while profit was ₹36 crore. The company delivered 1,106 wagons during the quarter and produced 6,468 metric tonnes from its foundry. All three divisions recorded sequential revenue growth. Rail infrastructure grew approximately 41% to 42% QoQ, while electrical infrastructure grew 38% QoQ. Freight cars contributed 62.3% of standalone turnover, down from 68.8% in Q1 and 74.7% in the corresponding quarter last year, showing improving diversification. Infrastructure and other businesses now contribute approximately 37% of turnover compared with 25% last year. Export orders have increased to 54% of the order book from 9% YoY, while private and export customers together account for approximately 80% to 85% of the core freight rolling stock order book. The electrical business reached approximately ₹250 crore of revenue in one quarter, with an order backlog of around ₹1,600 crore executable over the current financial year and the next four quarters. Foundry capacity has expanded to 60,000 metric tonnes, with management expecting significant export growth. CRISIL upgraded the company's long-term rating from A to A+, and the company continues to reduce debt.

🔴 Red Alert: Revenue remained approximately 31% lower YoY, with Q2 FY26 revenue of around ₹1,250 crore compared with approximately ₹860 crore in Q2 FY27. The decline was primarily due to significantly lower Indian Railways wagon orders. EBITDA margin also declined sequentially from 10.8% to 10.2%, although management stated that the previous quarter benefited from non-recurring other income and that adjusted EBITDA margin was approximately 70 basis points higher in Q2. The company has made a substantial provision of approximately ₹700 crore, which management described as a risk-mitigation measure arising from geopolitical uncertainties. However, management did not explain the detailed composition during the call and referred investors to the earlier published clarification. This remains an important point to independently examine. Private and export orders involve different wagon designs, supply chains and execution requirements, so their production volumes may not match the historical volumes of standard Indian Railways commodity wagons. The South African opportunity also requires setting up a facility in South Africa for maintenance and further business development, creating additional execution and capital requirements. The proposed wheel JV, RVNL JV and NYMWAG-related opportunities are still at different stages of development, with timelines and commercial contributions not yet clearly established. Management also did not provide a detailed multi-year capex and debt forecast.

🔵 Blue Alert: Texmaco 2.0 is focused on strengthening its core freight rolling stock and foundry businesses, expanding into railway adjacencies and increasing exports. The South African opportunity is a major international growth driver, involving approximately ₹4,000 crore of earlier orders and a subsequent ₹1,300 crore locomotive order. The turnkey contract includes wagons, locomotives and long-term maintenance, with locomotive manufacturing participation from India and a planned South African facility. The company is also developing its wheel business through a proposed JV, targeting a broader product range aligned with heavy-haul and high-speed rail requirements. Its NYMWAG JV plant is almost production-ready and has received initial RDSO G-105 certification, with prototype manufacturing dependent on receiving an initial order from Indian Railways. The RVNL JV is waiting for suitable tenders, with management expecting a potential opportunity within FY27. The electrical infrastructure business is another major diversification opportunity, with participation in various tenders linked to power transmission and grid expansion. The company has also entered the defence business, while EPC has turned profitable and electrical contracting is performing well. Management intends to evaluate acquisitions and new opportunities based on commercial readiness, technology, capital requirements and expected returns, with a stated preference for businesses that generate earnings from day one.

🧠 Deep Insight: The most important change at Texmaco is the transformation of its order book from heavy dependence on Indian Railways towards private customers and exports. Earlier, railway contracts accounted for approximately 90% to 95% of orders, whereas management now indicates that private and export business represents around 80% to 85% of the core freight rolling stock order book. This reduces customer concentration risk and creates access to potentially higher-margin international business. However, the transition also means that investors should not judge performance only by wagon delivery volumes, because specialised private and export orders have different production requirements and execution cycles. The current quarter shows improving sequential momentum, particularly in electrical infrastructure and rail infrastructure, but the YoY revenue decline highlights that the recovery is not yet fully established. Another important distinction is that the ₹10,000 crore revenue ambition is not simply an expansion of the existing wagon business. Management wants the core business to contribute ₹4,000 crore to ₹5,000 crore, with the remaining ₹5,000 crore to ₹6,000 crore coming from adjacencies and newer businesses such as passenger mobility, defence and renewables. This is a significant diversification ambition, but several initiatives are still at the development or tender stage. The ₹700 crore provision also deserves careful scrutiny before assuming that future export profitability will translate directly into reported earnings. The central investment thesis is that Texmaco is attempting to evolve from a railway wagon manufacturer into a diversified railway engineering and infrastructure company, with exports, electrical infrastructure and new technology partnerships driving its next growth phase. Investors should monitor quarterly revenue recovery, EBITDA margins, conversion of the ₹10,000 crore order book, South African order execution, the ₹700 crore provision, working capital and the commercial progress of its new JVs.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

  ▸ Revenue from operations: ₹4,177 Cr (up 8% YoY)
  ▸ EBITDA: ₹381 Cr (lower than ₹537 Cr in Q2 FY26)
  ▸ Loss After Tax: ₹50 Cr (compared to profit in Q2 FY26)

  ▸ Profit After Tax (before NCI): ₹10 Cr (compared to ₹535 Cr in H1 FY26)

𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁 & 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗜𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗚𝗹𝗼𝗯𝗮𝗹 𝗦𝗼𝗱𝗮 𝗔𝘀𝗵 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁: Continues to be challenging due to persistent oversupply from China, subdued industrial demand, & intense competition. High Chinese capacity additions & exports are key market drivers. 🇨🇳
- 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮 𝗠𝗮𝗿𝗸𝗲𝘁: Outperforming global markets with healthy demand growth, supported by solar glass & infrastructure investments. However, domestic pricing is under pressure due to import availability & increased domestic supply.
- 𝗟𝗶𝘃𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗘𝘀𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹𝘀 (𝗕𝗶𝗰𝗮𝗿𝗯𝗼𝗻𝗮𝘁𝗲, 𝗦𝗮𝗹𝘁, 𝗙𝗢𝗦): Demand outlook remains stable, driven by premiumization & increasing consumption. Prebiotics offer long-term growth opportunities. 🍎
- 𝗙𝗮𝗿𝗺 𝗘𝘀𝘀𝗲𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗮𝗹𝘀: Demand affected by uneven rainfall & delayed sowing, though Kharif acreage recovered. Agriculture outlook remains cautious due to weather volatility & input costs. 🌾
- 𝗨𝗦 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 (𝗧𝗖𝗡𝗔): Acquired customer contracts from Searles Valley Minerals (Chapter 11), representing 0.5 million tonnes over two years. This acquisition offers logistical advantages & is expected to provide better netbacks than export options. The accounting treatment involves amortizing the $22 million payment over five years as an intangible asset.
- 𝗨𝗞 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀: Performance impacted by higher gas & energy costs, affecting both salt & bicarbonate segments. Feedstock costs for bicarbonate also increased. 🇬🇧
- 𝗞𝗲𝗻𝘆𝗮 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀: Remained suspended during the quarter due to a notice from the Ministry of Mining. The company is pursuing administrative & legal remedies, asserting its lease rights until 2053 & has submitted proposals to the technical committee. The UK-Kenya Bilateral Investment Treaty may offer protection. 🇰🇪
- 𝗥𝗮𝗹𝗹𝗶𝘀 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝗶𝗮: Delivered a resilient performance aided by crop care & soil health, despite input cost inflation & unfavorable operating conditions impacting profitability.

𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗢𝘂𝘁𝗹𝗼𝗼𝗸 & 𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝘆:

- Near-term market conditions are expected to remain range-bound, particularly for soda ash, due to capacity additions & sustained exports.
- Focus on strengthening cost competitiveness, enhancing supply chain resilience, operational excellence, & disciplined capital allocation. 💪
- Advancing strategy to increase the contribution of non-cyclical specialty & value-added businesses to reduce earnings volatility. 📈
- Capex budget for the current year is around ₹1,000 Cr, including growth projects, with a similar level expected for the next year.
- Proceeds of ₹796 Cr from the sale of non-current investments in group companies were used to pay down debt in the US & UK.

🤝 Strategic Updates — 2026-11-11

🤝 Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar Limited — Strategic Update

Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar Limited's board approved the divestment of its entire 100% stake in wholly owned subsidiary Bajaj Hindusthan (Singapore) Private Limited (BH(S)PL) to Altaqat Management Consultancies Co LLC (lead member) in consortium with Dejavu FZ LLC, both registered at Business Bay, Dubai, UAE. The buyers are unrelated to the company's promoter group and the transaction does not constitute a related-party transaction.

Total consideration is USD 62,61,887 (approximately Rs 52 Crores), against BH(S)PL's net worth of Rs 81.11 Crores (2.13% of Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar's net worth) as of March 31, 2026; the subsidiary reported nil revenue and nil total income in that year. Two Indonesian step-down subsidiaries — PT Jangkar Prima and PT Batu Bumi Persada — will simultaneously cease to be subsidiaries of the listed entity. The transaction is expected to close within 180 days of the Share Purchase Agreement being executed.

The divestment exits a non-revenue-generating overseas holding structure at a discount to book value; the proceeds provide a modest cash inflow while removing the carrying obligation on the Singapore and Indonesian entities from the consolidated balance sheet.

🤝 Protean eGov Technologies Limited — Strategic Update

Protean eGov Technologies Limited and Yubi announced a collaboration to embed Protean's identity verification, KYC, consent and eSign capabilities into Yubi's AI-powered lending platform, targeting faster borrower onboarding, digital underwriting and paperless loan closure for lenders and borrowers across India.

No deal value is disclosed. Yubi has facilitated over ₹3.2 lakh crore in credit and serves 17,000+ enterprises and 6,200+ investors and lenders. The arrangement will operate within India's regulatory and consent-based frameworks, including data protection laws.

The collaboration gives Protean a commercial channel to monetize its public digital rails — identity, KYC, eSign, bank statement pull and ITR access — through Yubi's lending infrastructure, opening exposure to India's private credit market beyond its predominantly government-facing revenue base.

🎯 Management Guidance & Outlook

• Q3 has started strongly, with excellent Navratri and Dhanteras sales.

When a company starts conducting earnings concalls for the first time, or resumes them after a long gap, pay attention.

Don't just listen to what management says. Start tracking what's changing in the business.

Look for:
1. New capacity coming online.
2. Large order books and fresh customer additions.
3. Entry into new business segments.
4. Export opportunities.
5. Margin expansion triggers.
6. Debt reduction and improving cash flows.
7. New products that could become meaningful revenue contributors.

Sometimes, the most interesting part isn't what the company is earning today, but what management is building for the next 2-3 years.

Fee-paying AUM hit ₹49,164 Cr while operating margin expanded to 38.43%

👉 This asset manager is building a larger foundation of steady income as institutional allocators commit money to private credit and infrastructure funds. Fee-paying assets under management reached ₹49,164 Cr, rising 28% from a year ago. That growth matters because contractual management fees from locked-in vehicles provide predictable earnings regardless of public market swings.

👉 Profitability improved because employee expenses grew slower than sales, taking a noticeably smaller share of operational income. While administrative and fund distribution expenses rose compared to last year, the overall cost base stayed disciplined, allowing operating margins to widen comfortably.

👉 The business also holds substantial committed dry powder awaiting deployment into performing credit and yield assets. As this institutional capital gets drawn down into active investments, it automatically turns uncalled capital into additional recurring fees. With cash and liquid balances comfortably exceeding all outstanding borrowings, the company can easily fund coinvestments in new fund vintages without taking on debt.

👉 The result looks neutral because revenue from operations of ₹251.49 Cr dipped from the previous quarter even as operating margin reached 38.43%, showing quarter-to-quarter top-line lumpiness from fund performance timing.

👉 Growth catalyst: Deploying ~₹46,700 Cr of committed dry powder over the next 12 to 18 months will expand fee-paying assets and add steady contractual management fee income

The company said Q1's other expenses were higher because of higher amortisation of selling and distribution costs tied to a Variable Additional Return realised in that quarter.

Yubi and Protean eGov Technologies Ltd are collaborating to integrate India's trusted digital infrastructure into the credit lifecycle, enhancing the lending ecosystem. 

This partnership leverages Protean's public rails—identity, KYC, consent, and e-signature—alongside Yubi's advanced lending stack to streamline the loan approval process, significantly reducing onboarding time and improving risk assessment for borrowers, particularly MSMEs.

Company Snapshot: 
Protean eGov Technologies Ltd specializes in digital public infrastructure solutions, focusing on identity verification and KYC processes to facilitate lending. 

Key Highlights:
Key Highlights:
- Partnership with Yubi aims to transform India's lending ecosystem through digital public infrastructure. 
- Integration of identity, KYC, consent, and e-signature processes to reduce loan onboarding time from days to minutes. 
- Enhanced risk assessment for borrowers, especially MSMEs, through automated analysis of consented bank statements and income tax returns. 
- Online signing of agreements, sanction letters, and security documents to streamline the lending process. 
- Collaboration will adhere to India's regulatory frameworks, prioritizing data privacy and security.

Core Growth Triggers: 
Core Growth Triggers: 
- Digital Infrastructure Integration 
- Collaboration with Yubi to embed digital public rails into the lending process. 
- Expected to enhance loan approval rates and reduce onboarding time. 
- Regulatory Compliance 
- Partnership will operate within India's regulatory and consent-based frameworks, ensuring adherence to data protection laws.

Key Risks to Trigger Thesis:

- Potential challenges in data privacy and security compliance amidst increasing scrutiny.

Executive quote:

The partnership positions Protean to play a pivotal role in modernizing India's lending landscape, leveraging technology to enhance borrower experiences and lender efficiencies.

Concord Control Systems Ltd : 1HFY27 Conference Call : At inflection point of great transformation!

Key Catalysts for Investors over the Next Six Months

Execution of the Unexecuted Order Book and H2 Seasonality: 
o Concord entered H1 FY27 with an unexecuted order book of INR 846 crores (roughly four times its FY26 full-year revenue).

o Company performance has historically followed a 60:40 seasonal split, with H2 typically delivering substantially higher execution and revenue than H1.

Assuming this seasonality, the company has the potential to post a PAT of 80cr in FY27.

Main Board Migration: 
o The company is completing its eligibility requirements and plans to file applications to migrate to the main board as soon as approvals are in place.

Hydrogen & Battery Locomotive Deployments: 

o Following the deployment of India’s first battery locomotive propulsion system (which has operated for over 12 months), Concord is developing a 3,100 HP green hydrogen locomotive propulsion system scheduled for deployment early next year.

Fusion Electronics Commercialisation & Orders: 
o The Fusion plant is production-ready for both flexible and rigid PCBs as well as SMT/PCBA assembly.
oManagement expects the initial revenue tranche and order book conversion to begin showing up in FY27 and scale significantly into FY28, supported by client discussions and participation in international fairs like Electronica Germany.

Safety Approvals (Kavach & MSDAC): 
o Kavach: Ongoing track, loco, station, and section trials to transition from developmental status to an approved vendor.
o MSDAC (Multi-Section Digital Axle Counter): Management stated they are waiting for final approval.

Tenders & Commercialisation in Diagnostics & Subsystems: 
o Order conversion for Distributed Power Wireless Control Systems (DPWCS) is ramping into revenue.
o New bids for Wheel Impact Load Detectors (WILD) are anticipated in the current financial year.
 
Management Quotes & Guidance on Future Growth Potential

1. Long-Term Growth Rate (40% to 50% Revenue CAGR)
•Targeting 40–50% CAGR over 3–5 years: 
"Based on our current order book, our technology pipeline, and our planned commercialization, we are targeting a revenue CAGR of approximately 40 to 50 percent over the next three to five years. All four pillars will contribute significantly to this growth."

"The targeted growth of 40 to 50 percent CAGR is ambitious, and it is forward looking. But given our confidence in the opportunity ahead, we believe all these engines, put together, can deliver this kind of growth."

•Growth trajectory even excluding Kavach: 
"We are contemplating a target of 40% to 50% CAGR year on year. We would be growing with similar numbers, ex-Kavach also in the next year."

•Milestone toward FY30 (reaching ~INR 1,000 crores): 

When asked whether a 40–50% CAGR implies reaching ~INR 1,000 crore revenue by FY30, Managing Director Gaurav Lath responded:

"So, we also, if you talk about a mathematical calculation, definitely we should be reaching somewhere there. And that is where we are aiming at in terms of a CAGR positioning."
 
2. Inflection Point and Business Model

•Entering a transformative phase: 
"We have reached that inflection point where the next 5, 6 years are completely going to be a game-changing financial performance by us."

•Self-funded growth philosophy: 
"We take profitability seriously, and our policy is clear: profits fund growth, and growth funds the technologies that will shape the future of railways."
 
3. International Revenue Contribution

•Global market expansion: 
"As a company, we are very bullish on global railways. Over the next three to five years, we expect somewhere between one-fourth and one-half of our revenue to come from international markets. Personally, I am very optimistic about this."
 
4. Fusion Acquisition Potential
•Full-scale capacity potential: 
"At full scale we expect around INR 400 crores of revenue once the entire fusion capabilities are up and running... this opportunity will become a large growth lever for us."
 
5. Margin Sustainability (~29% to 30% EBITDA Margin)
•In-house R&D protecting margins: 
"Focus on margins and the bottom line is part of our DNA, and we will keep working to improve them... business is expanding, and economies of scale are beginning to show. We expect this to continue, and we are confident we can sustain it."

"That’s what we believe in because a lot of technologies is in-house developed. So, the cost of technology will significantly go down for us in future."

No buy/sell recommendation.

Bright Outdoor Media Makes Main Board Debut on BSE and NSE; Dr. Yogesh Lakhani Celebrates Milestone at NSE Bell-Ringing Ceremony

Ashish Shelar, Bhagyashree, Padmini Kolhapure, Poonam Dhillon, Adv Amit Mehta, Shekhar Suman and other personalities attended the celebration marking the company's next phase of growth.

Bright Outdoor Media Limited marked a significant milestone in its corporate journey by transitioning from the BSE SME Platform to the Main Boards of BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE). The development was commemorated with a special bell-ringing ceremony at the NSE, attended by political representatives, film personalities, business associates and other distinguished guests.

The occasion saw the presence of Ashish Shelar, along with actors Bhagyashree, Padmini Kolhapure, Poonam Dhillon, Shekhar Suman, Rajat Bedi and Manoj Joshi, among others. The gathering brought together personalities from the entertainment, business and public spheres to mark the company's new chapter.

Led by Chairman and Managing Director Dr. Yogesh Lakhani, Bright Outdoor Media became the first company from India's Out-of-Home (OOH) advertising industry to list on the BSE SME Platform on March 24, 2023. Its transition to the Main Boards of BSE and NSE represents a further step in its corporate growth and provides the company with a wider platform to engage with investors and market participants.

Founded in 1980 and headquartered in Andheri, Mumbai, the company has over four decades of experience in the outdoor advertising sector. Its operations include a network of more than 1,350 hoardings across strategic locations and over 50 large-format Digital LED Billboards in Mumbai. Its portfolio also includes advertising opportunities connected with public infrastructure, railway networks and government-led projects.

The company has been expanding its presence across traditional and digital outdoor advertising formats. Its Bright 360 initiative is aimed at developing integrated branding and advertising solutions, while its future focus includes digital advertising, infrastructure-led opportunities, new markets and sustainability initiatives such as solar-powered advertising infrastructure.

In its reported financial performance, Bright Outdoor Media recorded total revenue of ₹155.43 crore, EBITDA of ₹35.23 crore and net profit of ₹24.05 crore for FY26. For H2 FY26, the company reported revenue of ₹92.12 crore, EBITDA of ₹20.25 crore and net profit of ₹13.97 crore.

Speaking at the occasion, Dr. Yogesh Lakhani, CMD of Bright Outdoor Media Limited, said, “This is an extremely proud and emotional moment for me and the entire Bright Outdoor Media family. Our journey from the BSE SME Platform to the NSE Main Board has been built on years of hard work, perseverance, trust and the unwavering support of our clients, partners, employees and investors. This milestone is not just an achievement for the company but a reflection of the belief that people have placed in us. I am grateful to everyone who has been part of this journey. The NSE listing opens up a new chapter for Bright Outdoor Media, and we look forward to scaling greater heights, exploring new opportunities and creating long-term value for our shareholders.”

The Main Board transition marks another milestone for the Mumbai-based company as it looks to expand its advertising network, strengthen its digital capabilities and explore new opportunities in India's evolving outdoor advertising industry.

•Consolidated Q2 PAT ₹427 cr (vs ₹261 cr YoY); adjusted PAT ₹333 cr
•India Q2 revenue ₹9,007 cr (vs ₹6,843 cr YoY); EBITDA ₹549 cr (vs ₹432 cr); adjusted EBITDA ₹496 cr; PAT ₹424 cr (+62% YoY); adjusted PAT ₹330 cr
•Middle East Q2 revenue ₹960 cr (vs ₹860 cr); EBITDA ₹71 cr (vs ₹61 cr); PAT ₹12 cr
•H1 consolidated revenue ₹20,912 cr (+38% YoY); PAT ₹776 cr (+48% YoY); adjusted PAT ₹651 cr
•SSG >20% in Q2 with single-digit gold price inflation indicating volume growth

Growth Visibility Drivers
•Festive demand strong (Navratri, Dhanteras and post-Navratri weekend excellent); Q3 momentum continuing with volume growth; confident of meeting full-year targets
•APM (regional brand) launched in T. Nagar, Chennai in August — strong early traction especially during festive; 4 more stores planned this FY (2 in Q3, 2 in Q4)
•Store additions weighted toward H2/Q4 to support growth against high base; minimum ~25% revenue growth targeted for the year (with ~10% SSSG guidance)
•Exchange program ~42% (was ~30%); gold-for-cash (70–80%) supporting margin stability; PBT margins stable in Q2 after adjustments and expected higher in H2
•Market share gains continuing (post-COVID trend); organic shift from unorganized/semi-organized driven by younger consumers seeking choice, service and transparency; studded share improving on design preference
•Cash utilization focus on strengthening inventory in existing stores and select flagship openings; non-GML debt free; partial land sale completed (₹86–87 cr sold, further proceeds expected)

Outlook
•Q3 tracking well despite high base; wedding season upbeat; Q4 store openings to help offset high base
•PBT margins expected stable-to-better in H2 vs H1; exchange and gold-for-cash mix managed for accretion
•APM expansion focused only on Tamil Nadu for next couple of years before considering other states

OD CHARTY 77 K DĚKOVNÉMU DOPISU ORBÁNOVI 

Oldřich Kaiser vystoupil na demonstraci proti televizním poplatkům před Českou televizí. Recitoval oslavnou báseň o Leninovi a mnozí, já také, v tom viděli geniální satiru. On sám to pak v rozhovoru pro Deník N popřel.

Mě ale zaujalo něco jiného.

Oldřich Kaiser a jeho žena Dáša Vokatá jsou čestnými členy Společenství PRAK – Proti represi a kriminalizaci.

Když jsem se podíval, kdo za touto iniciativou stojí, zarazil jsem se.

Jindřich Rajchl. Josef Skála. Lenka Procházková. Jan Schneider.

Bývalí disidenti a signatáři Charty 77 vedle bývalého místopředsedy KSČM Josefa Skály a dnešního poslance za SPD Jindřicha Rajchla. Všichni spojeni jednou iniciativou.

Dáša Vokatá podepsala Chartu 77 ve třiadvaceti letech. Policie ji šikanovala, ničila jí bydlení a v roce 1980 jí v rámci akce Asanace vzali občanství a vyhnali ji i s rodinou ze země.

Ve stejných letech vedl Josef Skála čtyři roky Mezinárodní svaz studentstva a v ústředním výboru KSČ odpovídal za to, jak se Československo prezentuje v zahraničí. V srpnu 1968 podle svého vlastního životopisu pro StB vítal sovětské vojáky.

Jedna byla vyhnána. Druhý tentýž režim reprezentoval ve světě. Dnes stojí pod jednou hlavičkou.

To samo o sobě neznamená, že Vokatá sdílí Skálovy názory. Bylo by nespravedlivé jí je přisuzovat. Její odvaha si zaslouží úctu.

U dalších bývalých chartistů však máme konkrétnější doklady.

Lenka Procházková a Jan Schneider PRAK založili. V říjnu 2024 poslali otevřený děkovný dopis Viktoru Orbánovi za jeho vystoupení v Evropském parlamentu. Podepsali se jako signatáři Charty 77.

Lidé, kteří kdysi vzdorovali komunistické moci, veřejně děkovali politikovi, jehož vláda podle kritiků ovládla média a oslabila právní stát. A použili k tomu autoritu Charty 77.

To mě zaráží.

Procházková jde ještě dál. V jednom otevřeném dopise napsala, že v dobách jejího mládí to byl VONS, Výbor na obranu nespravedlivě stíhaných, a dnes je to PRAK.

Jenže VONS hájil lidi, které režim zavíral za samizdat a za to, že chtěli dodržování zákonů. PRAK vyhlásil sbírku pro učitelku Martinu Bednářovou, kterou soud pravomocně odsoudil za ospravedlňování ruských válečných zločinů při výuce na základní škole. Jejím advokátem byl Jindřich Rajchl.

Nikomu neupírám právo na obhajobu. To patří k demokracii. Ale právo na obhajobu není totéž jako pravdivost obhajovaných výroků.

Svoboda slova neznamená, že každá lež je pravda. A kritika demokracie ještě nedělá z člověka disidenta.

Před listopadem 1989 lidé z Charty 77 čelili režimu, který nešlo vyměnit ve volbách. Stát kontroloval média, potlačoval opozici a trestal občany za názory.

Dnes může člověk veřejně kritizovat vládu, založit stranu, kandidovat, organizovat demonstrace a požadovat změnu zákonů.

To není normalizace. To je demokracie.

I demokratický stát může postupovat nespravedlivě. Proto existují nezávislé soudy, odvolání a veřejná kontrola. Ale srovnávat každé trestní stíhání kontroverzního výroku s komunistickým pronásledováním je nebezpečné zjednodušení.

Charta 77 nebyla jednotné politické hnutí. Byli v ní demokraté, křesťané, socialisté i bývalí komunisté. Spojoval je požadavek dodržování lidských práv. Proto netvrdím, že bývalý chartista musí dnes smýšlet jako já.

Tvrdím něco jiného.

Odvaha postavit se jedné totalitě není doživotní zárukou správného úsudku o každé další moci.

Dáše Vokaté její odvahu nikdo nevezme. Lenka Procházková ani Jan Schneider nepřestávají být bývalými disidenty jen proto, že s nimi dnes nesouhlasím. Ale jejich minulost nemůže stavět dnešní postoje mimo kritiku.

Proto se ptám:

Kde končí obrana svobody projevu a začíná politická podpora lidí, kteří sami zpochybňují demokratické instituce?

A co dnes znamená odkaz Charty 77, když se jím zaštiťují lidé s tak rozdílným vztahem k demokracii, Rusku a evropské svobodě?

Nechci nikomu upírat jeho minulost.

Jen odmítám, aby slavná minulost nahrazovala odpovědnost za přítomnost.

🚩 Jubilant Pharmova Limited — Milestone

Jubilant Therapeutics Inc., a clinical-stage subsidiary of Jubilant Pharmova Limited, announced that Phase 1 data from its ongoing Phase 1/2 study of JBI-802 — a first-in-class oral dual inhibitor of LSD1 and HDAC6 (CoREST complex) — was selected for oral presentation at the 68th American Society of Hematology Annual Meeting, scheduled for December 12–15, 2026, in New Orleans.

Data as of June 30, 2026 from the Phase 1 cohort showed all 8 patients who initiated treatment at the 15 mg dose achieved greater than 50% platelet reduction or platelet normalization by Week 3 (median time to response: 15 days), with normalization maintained through 33–46 weeks in patients with more than 12 weeks of follow-up; 7 of 11 patients with leukocytosis achieved a complete hematologic response; and no dose-limiting toxicities were observed at the 5, 7 or 15 mg dose levels. No deal value or rupee figure was disclosed.

The results establish early clinical proof-of-concept for a mechanism with no currently approved oral agent in essential thrombocythemia and related myeloproliferative neoplasms; commercial impact is not yet quantifiable at this stage of development, but the data support progression into the Phase 2 portion of the study.

Why is Supriya Lifescience falling? 📉
The stock fell from ₹870 to ₹631 in three sessions, a 27% drop. It's now 40% below its June peak of ₹1,052.
The trigger wasn't revenue, it was margins.
Q2 FY27:
• Revenue ₹206 cr, up 3% YoY
• EBITDA ₹45 cr, down 38%
• Margin 22%, compared with 35%+ last year
• Profit ₹29 cr, down 42%
"The big hit: margin guidance cut"

FY27 EBITDA margin guidance was cut from 33–35% to 23–25%. In August, management had kept 33–35%, even though Q1 margin had already fallen to 25%.

Three reasons, roughly 10–12 points of margin lost:
1️⃣ Ambernath plant: about ₹60 cr of FY27 costs with almost no revenue. The EU audit has moved to November.
2️⃣ LATAM: high-margin products were reclassified as controlled substances in Colombia, Peru and Uruguay. Customers now need import permits, which take 4–5 months. Orders aren't lost, but they're delayed.
3️⃣ Raw materials and solvents: costs are up. Price increases have been passed on, but they'll take 2–3 quarters to show.

What's still intact:
• FY27 revenue target of ₹1,000 cr is maintained. That needs about ₹604 cr in H2.
• Pipeline: anaesthetic CMO deal close to signing, ADHD intermediates, contrast media launch next quarter, a cardiovascular intermediate, and whey protein.
• Ambernath could eventually do ₹450–500 cr of revenue. Breakeven is about ₹160–200 cr.
What's missing: no FY28 margin guidance. Ambernath needs 1–1.5 years after approval to scale, so don't assume margins snap back to 33–35%.

Q2:

H1:

EBITDA ₹294 Cr (+35.5% YoY) | 
Margin 30.9% (+127 bps) | 
PAT ₹189 Cr (+35.8% YoY) | 
Volume +24% |

Gross margin 60.8% (+161 bps)

Company converts raw steel into precision-engineered, safety-critical forged and machined components for trucks, cars, tractors, industrial engines, power generation, wind and mining equipment. Process involves forging (shaping heated steel on powerful presses) followed by machining into finished OEM-ready parts. High entry barriers from capital-intensive machinery, strict quality standards and long OEM approval cycles. Vertically integrated across forging, machining, heat treatment, testing and die design. Transitioning from forging-led to higher-value precision component supplier via increased machining and heavier/more complex parts.

Margin drivers / pressures: H1 EBITDA margin expanded 127 bps to 30.9% and gross margin 161 bps to 60.8%, driven by higher value addition (machined products rose to 90% of H1 sales from 88%), better realisations (+4.8% to ₹260/kg on raw-material pass-through, conversion-cost price hikes and mix), improved capacity utilisation, operating leverage and efficiency. EBITDA/kg rose 9.3% to ₹80. Q2 EBITDA margin broadly flat at 30.6%. ~80% of cost increases passed through; domestic OEMs largely compensated. Export freight costs had nearly doubled earlier but are softening. 33.5 MW renewable energy project ~90% complete (generation expected Q4, meaningful contribution from Q1 next year) with estimated ~₹30 Cr annual power savings.

Capacity expansions: Existing H1 capacity – Forging 1.58 lakh MT (60% utilisation), Machining 82,000 MT (77% utilisation). ₹650 Cr heavy-component project at Dugri, Ludhiana (primarily internal accruals; operations from FY28): advanced heavy-forging for complex components weighing 300–3,000 kg. Target applications include power generation (including data-centre backup), marine, mining, high-horsepower farm equipment, wind energy and oil & gas. Includes ~₹300 Cr heavy hammer line (2,000 tonnes/month capacity), ~₹200 Cr dedicated machining lines for heavy-engine applications and ~₹150 Cr vertical upsetter for North American high-HP tractors and wind. Additional ₹500 Cr expansion (funded via debt + internal accruals; commissioning in phases FY28–FY29; 70% machining / 30% forging/small press lines). Focus on passenger vehicles, industrials and CV exports. Combined expansions add ~59,000 MT forging and 34,000 MT machining capacity over 2–2.5 years, taking planned capacity to approximately 2.17 lakh MT forging and 1.16 lakh MT machining. Heavy hammer line is fungible across multiple end uses.

Product / new segment progress & diversification: Machined products now 90% of H1 revenue. Segment mix – CV 33% (strong domestic growth, exports subdued), Farm equipment 31% (growth >20%, market share rose from 42% to 46%; new programme ramp-up began 2–3 months ago), Industrials 16% (growth >50%), Off-highway 12% (growth >50%), PV 9% (revenue almost doubled YoY).

Order visibility, pipeline & international opportunities: ~₹300 Cr annual secured business for a dedicated machining programme with visibility till 2033. ~₹1,000 Cr additional under discussion; management aims to close nearly ₹500 Cr of orders by FY-end. Cold trials expected Jan–Feb, hot trials around March; sample submissions in FY28; revenue contribution expected from Q3/Q4 FY28. North American PV: 4,000-tonne line commissioned with 80–100 Cr projected revenue (shipments in transit, contribution from Q3). North American CV: ~₹80 Cr secured business in trials/testing with a global engine manufacturer. European CV: potential supply-chain opportunity following a customer’s acquisition (discussions ongoing, likely 2–3 year horizon). Industrials opportunities in gensets, gas engines, oil & gas, wind, mining, marine and railways. Exports form a meaningful share of the order book.

Guidance: FY27 volume growth guidance (high teens) expected to be met. FY27 margins expected broadly around FY26 levels despite stronger H1. Absolute EBITDA/kg to be maintained or improve in H2; gross margin and EBITDA/kg expected to trend upwards on product mix, value addition and efficiencies. Combined growth initiatives could add revenue equivalent to the current business over 3–4 years. Heavy-forging capacity should be adequate for 4–5 years; machining is likely to become the next constraint. Strong demand visibility across key verticals with recent customer wins/programmes ramping up.

Balance sheet & cash: H1 operating cash flow ₹124 Cr; capex ₹78 Cr. Cash/liquid reserves ~₹350 Cr. Net debt/equity 0.08. Working capital impacted by higher receivables and ₹35 Cr supplier advances; normalisation expected over the full year. New ₹500 Cr capex may involve up to ₹300 Cr debt; actual utilisation could be lower depending on internal liquidity.

Timely commissioning of heavy-forging and additional capacity, conversion of discussed orders into confirmed programmes, utilisation ramp-up, margin resilience amid cost and freight volatility, and working-capital discipline.

Outlook: Strong volume momentum with improving product mix and diversification across end markets. Company is moving deeper into higher-value machined and heavier components while expanding capacity for data centres, power, wind, marine, mining and other industrial applications. Execution on capex, order conversion and utilisation remains critical to translating investments into sustainable growth and profitability.

The incident occurred around midnight on Thursday at their residence in Naroda Smart City-2. According to Naroda Police Inspector B. M. Katariya, the couple had reportedly experienced frequent disagreements over domestic and financial issues for nearly a year.

Police said the latest argument started when Dilip questioned his wife about the vegetable she had prepared for dinner. The disagreement allegedly developed into a heated exchange, during which both exchanged insults. Nirmala reportedly picked up a kitchen knife and stabbed him on the left side of his chest.

Investigators said Nirmala later contacted her brother-in-law, Mukesh, and allegedly admitted that she had stabbed her husband. She also reportedly told him that Dilip had lost consciousness and that she was taking him to the hospital.

On Friday afternoon, Mukesh informed his father, Somaji Kharadi, 73, about the incident. Somaji, a retired assistant sub-inspector of the Rajkot city police, rushed to the hospital with other relatives but was informed that his son had died.

According to his complaint, he noticed a stab wound on Dilip’s chest, alongside other injuries to his cheek, upper arm and hands.

Police subsequently reviewed CCTV footage and gathered local intelligence before arresting Nirmala within hours. The murder investigation is ongoing, with officers questioning her to establish the circumstances surrounding the killing.

Kalyan Jewellers' Q2 net profit rises 64% to ₹427 Cr on revenue of ₹10,323 Cr

👉 Kalyan Jewellers India reported consolidated net profit of ₹427.1 Cr for Q2 FY27, up 64.0% from ₹260.5 Cr a year earlier and 22.5% above the ₹348.7 Cr of Q1. Revenue from operations was ₹10,323 Cr, up 31.4% YoY but down 2.5% QoQ from ₹10,589 Cr. Total income was ₹10,401 Cr. The profit includes a ₹73.5 Cr exceptional item, which the cash flow statement ties to the profit on sale of an investment property.

👉 Operating profit, excluding other income and the exceptional item, was ₹408.6 Cr, flat against ₹409.1 Cr in Q1 and up 36.7% from ₹298.9 Cr a year earlier. The operating margin rose to 5.4% from 4.4% in both Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY26, even as revenue fell 2.5% sequentially. Cost of materials consumed fell to ₹8,428 Cr from ₹9,100 Cr in Q1.

👉 Operating cash flow for the half-year was ₹1,075 Cr, up from ₹741 Cr a year earlier, but trade receivables rose by ₹480 Cr in the same period. Current borrowings fell to ₹177 Cr at 30 September from ₹524 Cr at 31 March, after net repayments of ₹346 Cr. Cash and cash equivalents closed at ₹384 Cr after dividend payments of ₹258 Cr to equity shareholders.

👉 Revenue growth has slowed each quarter, from 66.2% YoY in Q4 FY26 to 45.7% in Q1 FY27 and 31.4% in Q2. For the half-year, revenue rose 38.3% to ₹20,912 Cr and net profit rose 47.9% to ₹776 Cr. Management's August 2026 call targeted 80 new Kalyan and 50 Candere showrooms in FY27. A South store launch was reported delayed, citing elections.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management targeted 80 new Kalyan and 50 Candere showrooms in FY27 and a new regional brand, ATM, launching in Chennai in August 2026.

👉 Road blocker: Trade receivables rose to ₹1,346 Cr from ₹866 Cr in March, absorbing ₹480 Cr of cash, and management flagged margin dilution from old-gold recycling and rising employee costs.

👉 Underneath the headline numbers, profit was helped by selling property. A one-time gain of ₹73.46 Cr from selling investment land boosted pre-tax profit, masking the fact that operating margins remained under mild pressure from high gold prices.

👉 Cash generation was solid, with cash from operations reaching ₹1,074.55 Cr for the first half of the fiscal year. That cash helped the company eliminate all of its general bank borrowings by September, leaving the balance sheet funded primarily by low-cost gold metal loans and store leases.

👉 Showroom expansion is heavily tilted toward the second half of the year, where festive demand will test store productivity. The result looks neutral because OPM of 6.24% fell slightly from a year ago as promotional recycling discounts offset revenue gains.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management is expanding its retail reach by opening 80 Kalyan showrooms and 50 Candere stores across India during FY2027, with store openings heavily tilted toward the second half

Sansera Engineering Q2 FY27: Precision beyond auto, with a bigger investment cycle ahead

Sansera's diversification is becoming visible in the factory and the numbers. The same engineering base that supplies connecting rods and crankshafts is expanding into aircraft components and precision parts for semiconductor-manufacturing equipment.

The interesting development is that these newer businesses are growing while the automotive business is also expanding. Sansera is broadening what it can manufacture, increasing the complexity of its parts and investing ahead of customer programmes.

Q2 consolidated performance:
• Revenue: ₹1,091.45cr, up 32.3% YoY.
• EBITDA excluding other income: ₹211.23cr, up 47.6%.
• EBITDA margin: 19.4%, versus 17.3% a year ago.
• Group PAT: ₹108.65cr, up 52.2%.

1. The mix is changing without the core shrinking

Auto ICE product sales grew 18.2%, even as their share of product sales fell from 72.9% to 65.7% YoY. Non-auto's share increased from 13.2% to 20.9%.

These mix figures exclude scrap and other operating income. They describe the composition of product sales, rather than percentages calculated from consolidated revenue.

Passenger-vehicle product sales grew 42.4%. Tech-agnostic and xEV product sales together grew 27%. Premium vehicles, more engineered content per vehicle and OEMs buying more components from specialist suppliers are expanding Sansera's opportunities beyond simply following vehicle volumes.

One concrete development: management reported a pilot order linked to a two-wheeler OEM's move from in-house production to outsourcing. Successful execution must come before a much larger programme can be assumed.

Geography also needs care. Some new orders from global vehicle manufacturers relate to engine programmes being built in India. An international customer relationship can therefore generate domestic business.

2. Two order books, with very different meanings

At September-end, Sansera reported:

• ADS: ₹5,869.7cr of cumulative unexecuted backlog across approximately five years. ADS covers aerospace, defence and semiconductor equipment.
• Non-ADS: ₹2,241cr of estimated peak annual revenue from new business, expected to reach that peak within roughly three years.

The second number is a future annual sales level from awarded programmes, not a cumulative amount waiting to be shipped. Adding the two would produce a misleading order-book headline.

There is another important comparison. In the August call, management had already disclosed an ADS backlog of roughly ₹5,750cr after a large semiconductor-equipment order received after June-end. Much of the increase from June to September was therefore already known.

The more useful development is how that work moves through equipment installation, customer validation and production ramp-up.

In the previous call, ADS head Hari Krishnan explained the constraint:
“the significant or the defining lead time is the arrival of the mother machine.”

The specialised production equipment has to arrive before meaningful volumes can follow. In August, management expected significant revenue from that large semiconductor order in calendar 2027, with a peak in calendar 2029. A five-year order does not become next year's revenue simply because it is booked.

3. Semiconductor capability is advancing, but concentration remains

Q2 ADS revenue was ₹164.3cr, taking H1 to ₹309.7cr. These figures include the business's scrap and tooling income.

Management described validations for more complex semiconductor-equipment components and efforts to move further into assemblies. These are valuable steps: supplying a larger, more complicated package can increase the work captured from each customer.

Demand is linked to semiconductor-equipment investment, which in turn benefits from AI infrastructure and chip-capacity spending. Customer investment cycles and equipment-delivery schedules remain relevant risks.

The current semiconductor business still depends on one customer. Management hopes to add a second during Q3; it has not announced that conversion as completed.

On exclusivity, management was explicit:
“I don’t think we’ll be single source.”

Customers are developing multiple suppliers, including in India. Precision capability and successful validation help Sansera compete for more work, but they do not create an assured monopoly over those parts.

Aerospace progress also has different stages. The company reported its first Safran business in the quarter. Separately, the engine-blisk development remains under validation. The latter is not yet a proven commercial revenue stream, and potential investment for that opportunity is excluded from the current capex plan.

4. The larger capex plan changes the scale of execution

FY27 planned capex has increased from approximately ₹500cr to ₹800cr, with about half directed towards ADS. Management says some newer programmes are moving faster than typical automotive projects, requiring investment sooner.

The presentation indicates incremental asset turns of 2.0–2.2 times for ADS versus 1.25–1.3 times for automotive. That suggests more annual revenue per rupee of assets once production matures. It does not remove the time needed for commissioning, approvals and utilisation to build.

Near-term milestones include:
• The expanded ADS bay becoming fully operational during Q3 FY27.
• The dedicated defence facility starting around late Q3 or early Q4.
• Sansera–Nichidai beginning production or sample production towards the end of Q4, with customer conversion still to follow.

The defence facility initially relocates existing machines and gives the business dedicated attention. Proposed sheet-metal capabilities and larger orders are still developing.

The Nichidai venture targets steering, driveline and related precision components. Discussions around humanoid components are interesting, but the company has not provided a firm commercial revenue forecast for them.

5. Better margins do not make the investment cash-free

H1 statutory operating cash flow was ₹222.31cr, ahead of reported group PAT of ₹196.01cr.

However, cash paid for property, plant, equipment and intangibles was ₹356.86cr, with another ₹30.01cr invested in the Nichidai joint venture. Growth investment exceeded operating cash generation.

Inventory absorbed about ₹226cr, partly offset by higher supplier payables. Company-reported net debt increased from about ₹60cr in March to ₹261cr in September. Interest costs are already rising, and management expects some further increase as the business expands.

Margin quality also needs a careful reading. Q2 included a ₹16.7cr minimum-wage provision, with a catch-up from around mid-May. The higher wage base is recurring even though part of this quarter's expense relates to earlier months. Adding back the entire amount permanently would overstate sustainable profitability.

Richer business mix and operating leverage have absorbed some input, freight and labour pressure. Customer compensation for certain cost increases is still being pursued, so it should not be counted before it is secured.

6. The outlook is stronger, but avoid extrapolating the first half

The closing Q&A put FY27 revenue at ₹4,250–4,300cr. Against FY26 revenue of about ₹3,498cr, that implies roughly 21.5–22.9% growth, above the earlier high-teens-to-20% discussion.

After H1 revenue of ₹2,112.7cr, the range implies H2 revenue of approximately ₹2,137–2,187cr. That is only about 1–4% above H1, rather than another dramatic sequential step-up. Management made the outlook conditional on post-festive demand and geopolitical developments.

The presentation retains ADS revenue guidance of ₹550–600cr for FY27. Despite a stronger current run rate, a higher formal annual target has not been published.

Longer term, management aspires to ADS contributing 35–40% of revenue around the end of the decade. A refreshed strategy and firmer targets are expected towards the financial year-end. Capacity potential, aspirational mix and contracted revenue should remain separate in any forecast.

Kyro Read

Sansera is demonstrating that its precision-engineering skills can serve larger markets while its automotive foundation continues to grow.

The investment case now depends on converting qualified components and customer programmes into sustained production, while spreading semiconductor exposure across more customers and earning adequate returns on the higher capital deployed.

Customer approvals, commissioning progress, inventory requirements and the distinction between awarded work and early development will explain the next phase better than one large combined “order book” number.

Morning. Indian markets are shut today for Diwali-Balipratipada and reopen Wednesday, which means a fair bit is piling up while we are away.

The one thing that matters is crude. Brent is around $92 this morning, down about 6% in the last session and roughly six dollars off Friday's level, having settled Monday at its lowest since 31 August. The trigger was Trump saying US military action against Iran is not needed "at this point". The Hormuz blockade stays in place though, and an Iranian official has already denied reports of talks, so this is de-escalation rather than resolution. Take the peace-deal framing with a pinch of salt.

For India the level is close to everything. Citi's arithmetic: a $10 fall in crude narrows the current account deficit by 30 to 40bps, takes about 50bps off inflation, and adds roughly 2% to Nifty earnings. That is why foreigners have put over $4.1bn into Indian equities this month, their best month since September 2024. HSBC moved India to overweight and cut China to neutral. Citi lifted its December 2027 Nifty target to 28,000.

Monday reflected it. Nifty closed 25,044.65 and Sensex 81,106.65, both the highest since 27 February, with Nifty PSU Bank up 3.7%. One thing to keep in view: breadth was negative, 2,316 decliners against 1,922 advancers. Seven sessions of roughly 10.5% gains have been narrow ones.

Three names actually moved. Divi's Labs posted PAT of Rs 1,127 crore, up 64%, with an EBITDA margin of 42.6% against 32.7% a year ago, hit a record and crossed Rs 3 trillion in market cap, pulling Nifty Pharma to an all-time high. Tata Steel grew profit 16% and still fell 2.8%, the worst Nifty name of the day. Tata Chemicals swung to a Rs 50 crore loss on weaker realisations and higher energy costs.

Gold is about $4,113 and silver $52.76, which looks fine until you notice silver is down roughly 11% from a month ago.

Three things to watch. US October CPI tonight at 6pm IST, printing without year-on-year rates for most series because of last year's shutdown gap, so the monthly number carries all the weight. December Fed odds sit near 80% for a hike, not a cut. India CPI on Thursday, with forecasts near 5.9% against the RBI's own 4.9% projection for this quarter and a 6% tolerance ceiling, three weeks before an MPC that has already called cuts off the table. And 14 November is the filing deadline, so over 1,600 companies report between now and Saturday.

More after the close on Wednesday.

SANSERA ENGINEERING | Q2 & H1 Concall Updates: 

The story is Sansera’s transition from an automotive-focused precision engineering company towards a larger Aerospace & Defence (ADS) business.

1.
Q2 revenue 1,091.5 Cr (+32% YoY)
EBITDA 211.2 Cr (+48%); margin 19.4%, up ~200 bps.
PAT 108.6 Cr (+52%).
H1 revenue ₹2,112.7 Cr (+33%); EBITDA 407.3 Cr (+48%).
H1 reported PAT 196 Cr; 208.7 Cr excluding the Q1 litigation settlement impact.
Gross margin expanded 180 bps to 43%. However, employee costs, other expenses and depreciation also increased. Mgmt expects a steady margin profile.

2. Automotive: strong core business
Q2 automotive revenue was 669.7 Cr (+18%), around 65% of revenue. PV, two-wheelers, tech-agnostic automotive and XCV delivered their best-ever qtrs.

Automotive new-business order book reached 2,241 Cr of peak annual revenue potential, broadly equally split between domestic and exports. New wins include a tractor customer, PV engine programmes and a pilot outsourcing order from a two-wheeler OEM.

3. ADS: the key strategic growth engine

Q2 ADS revenue: 164.3 Cr; H1: 309.7 Cr.

ADS order backlog: 5,870 Cr versus 4,440 Cr in the previous quarter, executable over five years.💡

Mgmt 👉this is a rolling order book, with fresh wins adding to future execution.
ADS currently contributes ~15% of revenue. Mgmt’s ambition is to take this to 35–40% by decade-end.

4. Aerospace, semiconductors and defence

Aerospace: Two new customers added; first Safran engine-component business won in Q2. Rolls-Royce development has achieved agreed milestones, but validation is awaited; possible conclusion in Q3 FY27.

Semiconductors: Most of the top 10 complex parts for the existing customer have been validated. Mgmt hopes to add a second customer in Q3 FY27 and move towards assembly. Customers use multiple suppliers; exclusivity should not be assumed.
Defence: Dedicated facility expected by end-Q3/early-Q4 FY27. A couple of sizeable opportunities are in final stages. Additional 15–20 Cr capex may be needed if these wins materialise.

5. Capex: 
FY27 capex increased from 500 Cr to 800 Cr, with ~400 Cr earmarked for ADS.
Potential revenue capacities indicated :

Expanded ADS facility: ~1,500 Cr.
New facility: ~1,000–1,500 Cr.

Defence facility: ~400–500 Cr.

( Overall 👉Almost 2X kind of FY26 rev.)

The expanded bay is expected to be operational in Q3; the defence facility by end-Q3/early-Q4; the new facility towards the end of next calendar year.

6. New opportunities
Nichidai JV: Three forging press lines planned initially. Sample/commercial production expected towards end-Q4 FY27; customer discussions are underway.

Humanoid robotics: Developing complex aluminium forged and machined components for a North American customer. Still at development stage; no confirmed order or revenue potential disclosed.

Sheet-metal forming is being considered to address larger defence and aerospace packages.

7. Other updates:
Sweden operates at ~80–85% efficiency. Focus is on automation and engineering improvements, with a 10–12% return target; no major expansion planned.
US plant plans are being reconsidered amid customer delays and tariff uncertainty. Mgmt currently prefers sourcing from India.

MMRFIC is an associate, not a subsidiary. Sansera’s holding is ~47% after full CCPS conversion. Its activities include anti-drone and electronic-warfare radars; it is excluded from Sansera’s capex and revenue projections.

Acquisitions/JVs remain under evaluation, subject to strategic fit.

8. Guidance 🎯
FY27 revenue indication: 4,250–4,300 Cr. Healthy H2, subject to industry demand and geopolitical developments.

FY30 revenue aspiration is 8,000 Cr 💡

A new five-year vision statement is expected by end-FY27.

Overall : Strong call with clear growth focus and future growth oriented, now execution will be key, the order book and investments must reflect in stongvbottom line and cash flows.

• Cold Plates – Transfer heat directly from chips.

• Heat Exchangers – Transfer heat between cooling circuits.
• Chillers – Maintain required coolant temperatures.
• Valves, Hoses & Sensors – Control flow, pressure and leakage.

This creates opportunities across specialised engineering, piping, thermal components and cooling infrastructure.

🔵 Management expects domestic steel price increases may be passed on to customers.

3/4 – Debt, Railway JV & Returns

🔵 Debt reduced by ₹126 Cr during H1. Management targets ₹500 Cr debt reduction in FY27 and another ₹300–400 Cr in FY28.

🔵 Net debt target is around ₹1,500 Cr by FY27-end. A ₹500 Cr reduction could generate approximately ₹40 Cr annual interest savings.

🔵 Railway wheels JV: 300 wheels are ready and awaiting railway inspection. Initial supplies are expected after approval, with partial production targeted from December.

🔵 Management expects the JV to reach 4,000–5,000 wheels per month in Q4 and supply 20,000–25,000 wheels during FY27.

🔵 Railway JV's optimum EBITDA margin is expected at 18–20%. Phase 1 capacity is 1.4 lakh wheels, with Phase 2 adding another 1.4 lakh machining capacity.

🔵 ROCE target is 12–15% for FY27, with 20% in FY28 an aspiration.

4/4 – Future Growth Opportunities & Risks

🔵 Passenger vehicles are a key growth opportunity. Management expects this segment to contribute meaningfully, with a 10%+ growth contribution discussed for CY28/FY29.

🔵 Aerospace opportunity: direct discussions with OEMs for engine-side forgings and frame components. Advanced materials such as aluminium, titanium, Inconel and niobium are being explored. This remains a long-term opportunity; no confirmed revenue or orders were disclosed.

🔵 Working capital increased by approximately ₹140 Cr due to higher volumes and shipping delays. Management expects efficiency to improve.

🔵 Existing casting capacity is sufficient for current orders; further capacity decisions may be considered next year.

🔵 Management expects strong domestic and international markets in FY28. It also indicated that FY27 could surpass previous growth peaks, but did not provide detailed FY28 numerical guidance.

#Sejal Glass is taking a strategic step to expand beyond its existing manufacturing base.

Its board has approved a Business Transfer Agreement with Magnumtuff India Pvt. Ltd. to acquire its architectural and automotive glass business at Nangal Village, Belgaum, Karnataka, through a slump sale.

The strategic rationale is clear: instead of building a new operation from the ground up, Sejal gets access to an existing manufacturing facility, land and buildings, intellectual property, brand-related assets, customer relationships, goodwill and employees.

Why this matters: The acquisition could broaden Sejal's product portfolio, strengthen its presence in architectural and automotive glass, and give it an operating platform in Karnataka. Existing customer relationships and manufacturing infrastructure may also shorten the time needed to build scale.

The important details still to emerge are the transaction value, funding structure, business revenue and profitability, and how quickly Sejal can integrate the acquired operations.

The real opportunity is not just acquiring a factory—it is converting an existing business platform into incremental customers, capacity and growth.
