Tata Chemicals Ltd Concall Summary (Q2 FY27, 7 November 2026) #TATACHEM

🟡 Management Guidance: 
Management expects global soda ash prices to remain range-bound in the near term because of persistent oversupply, elevated Chinese exports and subdued industrial demand. Any sustained pricing recovery will depend on supply rationalisation and stronger demand. India continues to show relatively healthy demand, supported by solar glass capacity additions and infrastructure activity. In the US, Tata Chemicals will focus on North and South America and markets that generate positive netbacks rather than pursuing unremunerative Southeast Asian exports. The Searles Valley customer contracts acquired through bankruptcy proceedings cover approximately 5 lakh tonnes over two years, after which contract renewals will be required. Management expects UK salt and bicarbonate profitability to recover as energy and logistics costs moderate, but did not provide a specific timeline. The standalone business continues to focus on operational efficiency, while the broader strategy is to increase the contribution of non-cyclical specialty and value-added products. Annual CapEx is approximately ₹1,000 crore for FY27, with a similar amount indicated for the following year.

🟢 Green Alert: Standalone Q2 revenue increased 8% YoY to ₹1,300 crore, while EBITDA grew 22% to ₹292 crore. Standalone H1 revenue increased 9% to ₹2,584 crore and EBITDA rose 29% to ₹656 crore. India's business performed relatively well, supported by higher volumes in salt, FOS and silica. The US business secured customer contracts representing approximately 5 lakh tonnes through the Searles Valley Minerals bankruptcy proceedings. These contracts provide geographical advantages by allowing Tata Chemicals to serve customers in California and Mexico through more efficient overland logistics instead of relying entirely on exports. Management also highlighted the long-term potential of bicarbonate, salt and prebiotics, supported by demand from food, feed, pharmaceutical and wellness applications. India remains a relatively stronger soda ash market compared with several global regions. The company is also working towards improving its balance sheet through the sale of selected listed group-company investments, with approximately ₹796 crore of proceeds used towards debt reduction in the US and UK.

🔴 Red Alert: Consolidated Q2 EBITDA declined to ₹381 crore from ₹537 crore in the previous year, while the company reported a loss after tax of ₹50 crore compared with a profit in Q2 FY26. Consolidated H1 EBITDA declined to ₹936 crore from ₹1,186 crore, and profit after tax before exceptional items and non-controlling interests fell sharply to ₹10 crore from ₹535 crore. The main pressure is coming from lower soda ash realisations in overseas subsidiaries, higher UK natural gas and energy costs, increased freight and logistics expenses, and the suspension of Kenya operations. Global soda ash remains structurally oversupplied, particularly due to Chinese capacity additions and elevated producer inventories. Chinese soda ash inventories reached approximately 1.89 million tonnes by the end of September. Indian domestic prices also softened following improved import availability and increased domestic supply. Kenya remains a significant uncertainty. Operations are suspended following a notice from the Ministry of Mining, and management is pursuing administrative and legal remedies. Although management believes its lease rights extend until 2053, there is no confirmed restart timeline. Rallis India also faced pressure from delayed sowing, uneven rainfall, input cost inflation and unfavourable operating conditions. Consolidated net debt, excluding leases, stood at ₹6,127 crore.

🔵 Blue Alert: Tata Chemicals is repositioning its portfolio towards higher-value and relatively non-cyclical businesses under its LIFE framework. Living Essentials includes salt, bicarbonate and FOS, while the company is also developing opportunities in prebiotics, supported by growing interest in gut health and wellness. In the US, the Searles Valley customer contracts strengthen its geographical presence in California and Mexico and could improve logistics economics and customer relationships. The company is deliberately reducing exposure to Southeast Asian soda ash exports because of poor netbacks, while focusing on North and South America and other profitable markets. Management also highlighted potential demand growth from solar glass, lithium-related applications, food and pharmaceuticals. In Kenya, the company had planned to double capacity, add a bicarbonate unit and explore a container-glass partnership before operations were suspended. The company is pursuing its legal rights through the Kenyan courts and has also highlighted protection under the UK-Kenya bilateral investment treaty. The sale of selected group-company investments is part of a broader strategy to monetise assets and reduce debt.

🧠 Deep Insight: Tata Chemicals is facing a difficult combination of a global soda ash downturn and operational problems in overseas subsidiaries. The difference between standalone and consolidated performance is particularly important. Standalone EBITDA grew 22%, but consolidated EBITDA declined because overseas operations, especially the UK and US, are facing lower realisations and higher operating costs. This shows that the problem is not uniform across the business. India remains relatively resilient, while international operations are under pressure. The most important near-term issue is global soda ash pricing. Chinese oversupply is preventing meaningful price recovery, and even demand growth in India may not be sufficient to offset excess international supply. The company is responding by exiting unremunerative export markets and focusing on customers that offer better post-logistics contribution. The Searles Valley contracts are strategically useful because they improve customer proximity and reduce dependence on expensive shipping, but they are secured for only two years and renewals are not guaranteed. Kenya is another major uncertainty. Management is confident about its legal position, but investors should not assume a quick resolution or restart of operations. The ₹6,127 crore net debt position also makes cash generation and capital discipline important. Investors should monitor global soda ash prices, Chinese supply rationalisation, UK energy costs, Kenya's legal proceedings, US contract profitability, Rallis' recovery and debt reduction. The central investment question is whether Tata Chemicals can protect cash flows through the soda ash downturn while improving the profitability and resilience of its international operations.

FOLLOWING THE SMART MONEY: 5 BUYING SIGNALS THAT DESERVE INVESTORS’ ATTENTION

1. JUBILANT INGREVIA: MULTIPLE MUTUAL FUNDS INCREASE EXPOSURE

One of the strongest institutional accumulation signals this week.

• Franklin MF: +0.56 percentage points to 2.38%
• Axis MF: +0.30 pp to 2.11%
• Kotak MF: +0.12 pp to 3.19%
• HDFC MF: +0.05 pp to 2.16%

Combined increase: approximately 1.03 percentage points.
Multiple fund houses increasing exposure makes this worth investigating.
What are they seeing in the company's growth outlook, margins, capacity utilisation and earnings visibility?
Investor watch: Examine segment growth, margin trajectory, return ratios, cash-flow conversion and valuation.

2. JINDAL STAINLESS: REPEAT PROMOTER BUYING

JSL Overseas purchased shares worth approximately ₹77.9 crore at an average price of ₹683.

What makes this interesting is the recurring pattern:

• 12 September: ₹47.5 crore
• 3 October: ₹62 crore
• Current week: ₹77.9 crore

Repeated purchases are more interesting than a one-off transaction.

The key question is whether this reflects sustained promoter confidence in the business outlook.

Investor watch: Stainless steel demand, capacity utilisation, margins, capital expenditure and valuation.

3. CARTRADE TECH: GLOBAL LONG-ONLY INVESTORS ABSORB A LARGE EXIT

MacRitchie Investments sold approximately ₹470 crore worth of shares at ₹2,583.
Identifiable buyers included:

• Capital Group's Smallcap World Fund: ₹369 crore
• Norges Bank: ₹76 crore

Together, these purchases absorbed approximately 95% of the disclosed sale value.

The stock subsequently gained around 4.5% to ₹2,700 in the price data reviewed.

This is an interesting example of a large shareholder exit being absorbed by identifiable global institutional investors.

Investor watch: Used-car penetration, transaction volumes, growth, profitability and valuation.

4. GO FASHION: PROMOTER BUYING + PLEDGE RELEASE

The promoter group purchased approximately ₹24.8 crore worth of shares.
At the same time:

• Franklin MF sold approximately ₹32.7 crore.
• Promoter-related pledge release of approximately ₹41.7 crore was reported.
• The stock gained around 10.1% in the price data reviewed.

The combination of promoter buying and pledge release is worth monitoring.

However, it does not by itself establish a business turnaround.

Investor watch: Further promoter purchases, pledge levels and operating performance.

5. ALIVUS LIFE SCIENCES: SEVEN BUYERS ABSORB NIRMA'S EXIT

Nirma sold approximately ₹390 crore worth of shares.

The disclosed transaction data showed seven buyers absorbing the entire sale.

The stock subsequently gained around 8.1%.
A diversified buyer base can be constructive, but the identity and investment horizon of the buyers matter.

Investor watch: New shareholder profile, earnings growth, margins and valuation.

OTHER INSTITUTIONAL ACCUMULATION SIGNALS

A few more names deserve attention:

• Tata Steel: ICICI Group increased its holding by approximately 1.04 pp to 3.35%.

• AstraZeneca Pharma India: ICICI Group added approximately 0.79 pp to 2.18%.

• Punjab Chemicals: Ares Diversified increased its holding by approximately 1.46 pp to 4.89%.

• Ardee Industries: Ashish Kacholia crossed the 1% holding threshold, with a reported holding of 1.20%.

• Horizon Industrial Parks: Radhakishan Damani held 1.16%; SBI Group held 1.45%.

These are research leads, not automatic buy signals. The reporting period behind each shareholding change needs to be checked.

PROMOTER SELLING: WHO IS MONETISING?

Insider trading disclosures showed:

• Open-market purchases: approximately ₹206 crore
• Open-market sales: approximately ₹959 crore
• Sell-to-buy ratio: approximately 4.7 times by value

However, three names—Sri Lotus Developers, Shreeji Shipping and Dr Reddy's KMP—accounted for approximately 93% of the reported market-sale value.

Some notable transactions:

• Sri Lotus Developers: Promoter Anand Pandit sold approximately ₹573 crore, representing around 4.88% of equity. Promoter holding remained approximately 65%.

• V2 Retail: Promoters sold approximately ₹258 crore, representing around 4.4% of equity, to six private buyers.

• Gallantt Ispat: Promoter Dinesh Agarwal sold approximately ₹250.5 crore through a block deal, plus around ₹20 crore through market transactions.

• Shreeji Shipping Global: Promoters sold approximately 1.84% of equity, worth around ₹257 crore, through market transactions.

Promoter selling is not automatically negative. The important questions are:
How much equity is being sold?
What is the promoter's residual holding?
Who is absorbing the shares?
Is the selling recurring?

The identity of the buyer matters as much as the identity of the seller.

LARGE SHAREHOLDER EXITS: NOT ALL ABSORPTION IS EQUAL

Two transactions illustrate why investors should look beyond headline deal values.

LENSKART
SVF II Lightbulb exited approximately ₹1,846 crore worth of shares.
Disclosed buyers substantially matched the sale value. Kotak MF bought approximately ₹331 crore, while a significant portion was routed through Societe Generale, Goldman Sachs and BNP desks.

The stock gained around 4%.

Good absorption, but the ultimate end-clients behind the investment-bank desks remain partly undisclosed.

GROWW

Peak XV and YC Holdings sold approximately ₹2,457 crore worth of shares.

Goldman Sachs ODI was identified as a buyer of approximately ₹764 crore—around 31% of the sale.

The remaining ₹1,693 crore was not identifiable from the available disclosed buyer information.

This is a substantial exit, but the ultimate ownership of the balance remains unclear.

Key lesson: A transaction routed through an investment bank does not automatically represent long-term institutional buying.

PLEDGES: ONE LARGE DEVELOPMENT TO MONITOR
Knowledge Realty Trust reported pledge creation by four Blackstone sponsor entities.
• Approximately 60.7 crore units pledged.
• Equivalent to around 13.7% of the trust.
• Reported value: approximately ₹6,719 crore at ₹110.60 per unit.

The lender and purpose were not disclosed in the dataset.

Other developments:

• Swan Corp: approximately ₹280 crore pledge creation.
• Ravindra Energy: approximately ₹57.5 crore pledge creation.
• Go Fashion: approximately ₹41.7 crore pledge release.
• ideaForge: approximately ₹25 crore pledge release.
• Responsive Industries: approximately ₹14.5 crore pledge release.

A pledge does not automatically imply financial distress. But large sponsor-level pledges deserve scrutiny, particularly around the financing purpose, collateral terms and potential invocation risk.

STRATEGIC OWNERSHIP CHANGE: GRT JEWELLERS AND TBZ

GRT Jewellers acquired approximately 74.12% of Tribhovandas Bhimji Zaveri (TBZ) through an off-market transaction.

• Shares acquired: approximately 4.95 crore
• Transaction price: ₹209 per share
• Consideration: approximately ₹1,034 crore

This is a strategic change in ownership, not an ordinary block deal.

Investors should track the applicable open-offer requirements or exemptions, final offer terms, acquisition rationale and the potential for operating synergies.

 OUR WATCHLIST

Based on this week's ownership and transaction signals:

Accumulation signals to investigate

Jubilant Ingrevia – multi-fund accumulation.
Jindal Stainless – repeat promoter buying.
CarTrade Tech – global long-only absorption.
Go Fashion – promoter buying and pledge release.
Alivus Life Sciences – seven buyers absorb a large exit.

Tata Steel – ICICI Group accumulation.

Punjab Chemicals – significant Ares Diversified addition.

TBZ – strategic ownership change.

Developments requiring caution or monitoring

• Groww – large shareholder exits and buyer opacity.
• V2 Retail, Gallantt Ispat, Sri Lotus Developers and Shreeji Shipping – significant promoter selling.
• Syrma SGS – institutional shareholding reductions.
• Knowledge Realty Trust – sizeable sponsor-level pledge.
• Swan Corp and Ravindra Energy – pledge creation.

Bright Outdoor Media Limited, India's first listed Out-of-Home (OOH) advertising company, has achieved a significant milestone by listing on the Main Boards of both the BSE Limited and the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) on November 6, 2026. This move signifies a new chapter in the company's growth journey, reinforcing its presence in the capital markets and strengthening its position in the OOH advertising industry. 🌟

The transition from the BSE SME platform to the Main Boards reflects the company's progress and its commitment to building a scalable, diversified, and future-ready outdoor advertising business. This listing provides a broader platform for engaging with investors and stakeholders as Bright Outdoor Media pursues its long-term growth objectives.

𝗞𝗲𝘆 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 & 𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀:

- 𝗜𝗻𝗱𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗿𝘆 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗠𝗮𝗶𝗻 𝗕𝗼𝗮𝗿𝗱: Building on its status as India's first OOH company listed on the stock exchange (March 24, 2023), Bright Outdoor Media now debuts on premier exchange platforms.
- 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗱 𝗡𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸: Operates over 1,350 hoardings & 50+ large-format Digital LED Billboards across strategic locations, including participation in projects like the Navi Mumbai Metro Line & Indian Railways tenders.
- 𝗕𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁 360 𝗜𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗮𝘁𝗶𝘃𝗲: A strategic focus to expand beyond traditional OOH advertising by developing integrated branding & advertising solutions under one platform.
- 𝗩𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗙𝗼𝗿𝘄𝗮𝗿𝗱: Future priorities include expanding advertising infrastructure, strengthening digital capabilities, exploring government & infrastructure opportunities, developing integrated solutions, expanding market reach, & pursuing sustainability-led initiatives like solar-powered infrastructure. ☀️

Dr. Yogesh Lakhani, CMD, expressed pride in the achievement, highlighting the company's continuous efforts in expanding its network, digital presence, & integrated capabilities. He emphasized the vision to build a larger, diversified business with a stronger focus on digital innovation & integrated solutions, aiming to create long-term value for shareholders. 💰

Supriya Lifescience... I was expecting much better from this company.

PAT down 42%, margins fallen from 36% to 22%.

But what surprised me more was the earnings call.

In August management was talking about 33–35% margins. Now suddenly 23–25%.

Ambernath plant is not contributing, LATAM business has regulatory issues and raw material costs have increased.

All these may be temporary problems. But how could management be so confident just 3 months back?

One good thing, cash flow is positive, receivables have come down and company has no bank debt. So there is time to correct things.

I still like its move towards specialty APIs and formulations.

But now I would watch actual orders and sales from Ambernath rather than another guidance.

And even after 20% fall, valuation is not very cheap.

Sometimes one bad quarter can be ignored. But when management's expectations change so sharply in just 3 months, I think we need to be more careful.

• New salt and silica plants to be operational by 2028

Blockers
• Kenya operations suspended by government order, with the legal path unresolved; UK EBITDA-positive target missed

Tata Chemicals swings to ₹50 Cr loss as operating margin collapses to near zero

👉 Tata Chemicals reported a consolidated net loss of ₹50 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, against a profit of ₹154 Cr a year earlier and ₹60 Cr in the June quarter. Revenue from operations rose 7.7% year on year to ₹4,177 Cr, but it fell 1.8% from ₹4,255 Cr in the previous quarter. Profit before tax was a loss of ₹6 Cr, compared with ₹236 Cr a year ago.

👉 Operating margin, as reported, slipped to −0.1% from 5.9% a year ago and 2.6% in Q1 FY27. Freight and forwarding charges climbed to ₹949 Cr from ₹716 Cr, up about a third. Power and fuel rose to ₹535 Cr from ₹442 Cr, and depreciation rose to ₹351 Cr from ₹285 Cr. Cost of materials consumed fell to ₹653 Cr from ₹733 Cr.

👉 Industrial Essentials, the largest segment, reported revenue of ₹2,262 Cr, up from ₹2,150 Cr, but its segment result swung to a loss of ₹120 Cr from a profit of ₹16 Cr a year earlier and a ₹70 Cr loss in Q1. Living Essentials revenue rose to ₹1,191 Cr, with segment profit at ₹85 Cr. Farm Essentials revenue was flat at ₹858 Cr, while its profit fell to ₹94 Cr from ₹128 Cr.

👉 For the half year, revenue rose 11% to ₹8,432 Cr, but net profit fell to ₹10 Cr from ₹470 Cr. Cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹556 Cr from ₹381 Cr at March 31, 2026, while trade receivables climbed to ₹2,507 Cr from ₹2,088 Cr. Total borrowings stood at about ₹6,922 Cr, against ₹7,114 Cr in March. Management's Q1 call guided annual capex near depreciation levels, around ₹1,200 Cr.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans 210 KTPA salt and 50 KTPA silica capacity expansions, with commissioning in FY27–28 and new salt and silica plants operational by 2028.

👉 Road blocker: Management named Chinese oversupply and Middle East shipping costs as pressures on global soda ash pricing.

Sansera Engineering: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Sansera had its highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA. Margins went up despite higher wages and freight costs. The aerospace, defence and semiconductor (ADS) order book jumped about 32% in one quarter.

Q2 FY27
Revenue: ₹1,091.5 Cr (+32% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹211.2 Cr (+48% YoY) | Margin 19.4% (+~200 bps)
PAT: ₹108.6 Cr (+52% YoY)
Gross margin: 43% (+180 bps)

H1 FY27
Revenue: ₹2,112.7 Cr (+33% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹407.3 Cr (+48% YoY) | Margin 19.3%
PAT: ₹196 Cr (+46% YoY)

ADS revenue: ₹164.3 Cr in Q2 | Non-auto share of sales: 20.9%

(YoY = Year on Year, EBITDA = Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation, PAT = Profit After Tax, ADS = Aerospace, Defence and Semiconductor, bps = basis points, where 100 bps = 1%)

Key Takeaways

1.  Diversification target nearly reached-
Engine-based (ICE, Internal Combustion Engine) auto parts are now about 65% of sales, close to the target Sansera set at its IPO. The ICE business itself grew 18% to ₹669.7 Cr, so the share is falling because the new segments are growing faster. EV and fuel-agnostic parts posted a record ₹136.3 Cr.

2.  ADS order book jumped-
The ADS order book rose to ₹5,870 Cr from ₹4,440 Cr in June. It includes a large semiconductor order and will be executed over 5 years. Sansera won its first order from Safran (French aircraft engine maker) and added new aerospace customers. A second semiconductor customer is expected in Q3.

3.  Capex raised to build capacity-
FY27 capex is raised from ₹500 Cr to ₹800 Cr, with about half going to ADS. Once all the planned ADS plants are running, they can support roughly ₹3,000-3,500 Cr of ADS revenue. Net debt rose to ₹261 Cr (still only 0.3x EBITDA), and interest cost went up to ₹14.6 Cr from ₹8.1 Cr.

4.  Costs are rising-
Karnataka raised minimum wages by about 30%, and Sansera booked a ₹16.7 Cr provision this quarter. This is a recurring cost. The West Asia conflict also pushed up the cost of cutting tools, freight and logistics. A better product mix and higher volumes helped absorb these costs.

5.  New growth options-
The Nichidai JV (Joint Venture) will make steering and driveline forgings, with production starting by end of FY27. Sansera is developing complex parts for a North American humanoid robot maker. It also expects validation in Q3 on a jet engine part (blisk) under development for a global engine maker.

6.  Auto order book is healthy-
The non-ADS order book (measured as peak annual sales) rose to ₹2,240 Cr from ₹1,850 Cr, and about half of it is for exports. Sansera got a pilot order from a two-wheeler company that is starting to outsource parts. The plan for a US plant is on hold because of tariff uncertainty.

Key Guidance
• FY27 revenue of ₹4,250-4,300 Cr
• ADS to grow from ~15% to 35-40% of revenue by FY31
• A new 5-year vision with fresh targets to be announced by end of FY27

EBITDA dropped 29.05% as industrial operations posted a ₹120 Cr loss

👉 The global glut in soda ash has pushed the industrial chemicals business into an operating loss of ₹120 Cr, down from a profit a year ago. While domestic salt and bicarbonate continue to sell well, they cannot make up for falling prices and rising logistics costs across overseas plants.

👉 Consolidated OPM shrank to 9.12% because shipping, power, and operating expenses took a much larger share of revenue than last year. The Indian business continues to run profitably, but overseas subsidiaries in the UK, United States, and Kenya are draining group earnings as export prices remain pinned down by Chinese supply.

👉 Cash flow has taken the hardest hit, with CFO dropping to ₹64 Cr for the first half of the year as money remained locked up in customer dues and unsold stock. Compounding these operational troubles, Kenyan authorities suspended mining at the Magadi plant during the quarter, causing an immediate loss of ₹21 Cr with court proceedings still underway.

👉 The company is keeping annual capital spending within its limits and relying on internal cash and investment sales rather than piling on fresh debt. Any real recovery in earnings will depend on Chinese export volumes slowing down and the Kenyan courts permitting mining to restart.

👉 Growth catalyst: The company plans to commission its 82.5 KTPA vacuum salt expansion at Mithapur by Q4 FY27, adding non-cyclical volume to its consumer salt business

👉 Road blocker: A Chinese export inventory of 1.73 million metric tonnes continues to depress global soda ash prices at $170 to $190 per tonne, with management expecting no price recovery through FY27

S tem je reševal problem odvečnih vzgojiteljev in tudi učiteljev-zaradi hudega demografskega upada  so se  v 90- ih vrtci zapirali.  Z obveznim šolanjem pri 6 letih je zagotovil, da se upad med učiteljstvom ni začel.
Da pa se je potem po eni strani šestletnike pošolalo in s tem se je izgubila priprava na branje in razumevanje ter razvoj osredotočenosti, ki jo terja razvojno obdobje, hkrati pa se je zaradi tega opismenjevanje podaljšalo in posledica je bila manǰsa zmožnost vsrkavanja in razumevanja vsebin, je videti danes v rezultatih PISE.

Da se je takratni LDS izognil družbeni napetosti, je žrtvoval otroke. Če k temu dodami skrajno nespsobno podporo devetletke Zavoda RS za šolstvo, celo škodljivim potezam, kot je oblikovanje skrajno neumnega koncepta  opisnega ocenjevanja, lahko razumemo današnjo tragiko, ki jo razgalja PISA.

Kljub vsemu devetletka ni uspela pokvariti vseh, to pa zaradi nekaterih izjemnih ravnateljev in učiteljev, ki so delali po svoje. In seveda staršev, ki intelektualno podpirajo svoje otroke.

V resnici je dijak na seji odbora za izobraževanje dokaz temu,  in ki je kljub svoji mladosti pametnejši od Vrečkove, Gabra, one učiteljice iz Maribora ter establišmenta skupaj. Lahko sicer privzamem,  da so oni vendarle približno tako pametni kot on, vendar je  zaključek še strašljivejši: v tem primeru bi pomenilo, da so skrajno pokvarjeni.

Skratka. Reforma bo. Na celi črti.

🚨 US DATA CENTER RESTRICTIONS: WHAT IT MEANS FOR AI INFRASTRUCTURE STOCKS

Goldman Sachs estimates that nearly 45% of planned US data center capacity is located in states where new construction restrictions could emerge following recent election developments.

⚠️ Important: This does NOT mean 45% of data centers are cancelled. Projects may face approval delays, higher costs or relocation.

Why are restrictions being discussed?
• Rising electricity demand and power bills
• Water consumption and cooling requirements
• Pressure on local power grids
• Environmental and community concerns

Potential impact on Indian companies:

🔹 HFCL: Optical fibre, telecom networks and data center connectivity.

🔹 Sterlite Technologies (STL): Strong exposure to US AI data center optical connectivity, including a multi-year product award exceeding $1 billion.

🔹 Black Box: Data center infrastructure, system integration, networking and digital infrastructure solutions.

🔹 Aeroflex Industries: Supplies flexible flow solutions used in industrial and infrastructure applications. Its direct exposure to US AI data centers is different from optical fibre and connectivity companies.

What about Indian Data Centers? 🇮🇳

India’s data center expansion is driven by domestic cloud demand, AI adoption, digitalisation and investments by global technology companies.

US construction restrictions do not automatically affect Indian data center projects. However, global supply chains, equipment costs, financing and technology investments could influence the sector.

My Investment View:

Delayed projects do not necessarily mean lost demand.
Orders and deliveries could shift to later quarters.
Projects may move to states or countries with fewer restrictions.
Permanent cancellations would be a more serious concern.
Investors should monitor order execution, revenue growth, margins and cash flows rather than focusing only on order book numbers.

KEY TAKEAWAY:

AI infrastructure demand remains a long-term opportunity, but execution timelines and project approvals are becoming increasingly important.

Don’t confuse temporary delays with the end of the AI infrastructure boom. Also, don’t assume every company will benefit equally.

Supriya Lifescience: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

This was a weak quarter. Revenue was almost flat and EBITDA fell sharply, and management cut its margin guidance only one quarter after reaffirming it.

Q2 FY27
Revenue: ₹206 Cr (+3.2% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹45 Cr (-38% YoY) | Margin 22% (vs ~36% last year)
PAT margin: 14.2%

H1 FY27
Revenue: ₹396 Cr (+14.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹93 Cr (-25% YoY) | Margin 23.4%
PAT: ₹53 Cr (vs ₹85 Cr)

(YoY = Year on Year, EBITDA = Earnings Before Interest, Tax, Depreciation and Amortisation, PAT = Profit After Tax, API = Active Pharmaceutical Ingredient, the main chemical in a medicine)

Key Takeaways

1.  Where the margin went-
Supriya normally earns 34-35% EBITDA margin, and this quarter it fell to 22%. Management broke down the gap. About 6% came from costs at the new Ambarnath plant, which has no revenue yet. About 3% came from losing high-margin sales in Latin America, and about 3% from higher raw material and solvent prices.

2.  Latin America rule change-
Colombia, Peru and Uruguay have suddenly classified some of Supriya's high-margin products as "controlled substances". Customers there now need import permits, which take 4-5 months. Latin America's share of revenue fell from 21% to 12%. Management says demand has been delayed, not lost.

3.  Ambarnath is a cost for now-
The Ambarnath plant will cost about ₹60 Cr this year with almost no revenue, because the EU (European Union) inspection got delayed. The audit is happening this month. Management says the plant breaks even at ₹160-200 Cr revenue, which could take 1-1.5 years after approval. Its full potential is ₹450-500 Cr.

4.  New products and a big contract-
Two new anaesthetic products have been launched, and a US approval for one of them is expected soon. A large CMO (Contract Manufacturing Organisation) deal for this anaesthetic is "very close to signing". It will start with API supply, and the plant capacity for it is already built. Two ADHD (Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder) drugs and a heart-drug intermediate are also scaling up.

5.  Revenue target looks stretched-
Management still targets ₹1,000 Cr revenue in FY27. H1 was ₹396 Cr, so H2 needs about ₹600 Cr, which is 1.5x the first half. Management pointed to ~₹265 Cr of inventory and firm orders. However, much of this growth is coming from semi-regulated markets where prices are lower.

6.  Investors questioned management communication-
On the Q1 call, management had said it was confident of 32-35% margins for the year. Several investors on this call said the sharp cut came without warning. Management said the Latin America rule change came after the Q1 call, and accepted the feedback. Investors should treat future guidance with some caution.

Key Guidance
• FY27 revenue of ₹1,000 Cr
• FY27 EBITDA margin cut to 23-25% (from 32-35% earlier); no FY28 margin guidance yet
• 20%+ revenue growth over the next 3-4 years

Time Technoplast, Q2 FY27 concall — management is holding every growth guide despite a below-guide H1, and says the margin fix comes from cost levers.

Growth: ≥15% volume growth a year for the next three years, with EBITDA growth above 20% and PAT growth above 25% at that volume. By segment: packaging 11–13%, composites 25–30%, pipes 20–25%, other 10–12%. H1 volume was +12.9% and EBITDA +16.9%, so H2 has to do the catching up.

Composites: the largest growth driver. H1 composites revenue ₹430 Cr. Management sees ₹800–900 Cr this year and ₹2,500 Cr in three years. New LPG connections are being offered only in composite cylinders because steel cylinder supply is suspended. HPCL repeat orders came at unchanged prices. Hydrogen cylinders: strong interest, but commercial demand clarity is mid-to-late 2027. The 14.2 kg LPG cylinder is delayed 3–4 months.

Pipes: weak so far. Polymer prices rose 30–40% and the company will not supply without price-variation clauses, which government EPC contracts often lack. Management says H2 normally carries 60–65% of the year and states are now revising rates.

Capital: total capex ₹375 Cr, with ₹134 Cr of non-core assets identified for sale (₹18 Cr done), so net ~₹250 Cr. From FY28, maintenance plus brownfield of up to ₹250 Cr. Capacity utilisation: India ~83%, overseas ~86%. ₹220 Cr of QIP money is still unspent (₹75 Cr of automation orders identified, to be used by March 2027). Net cash from operations ₹344 Cr in H1.

Ebullient Packaging acquisition: not proceeding for now, revisit in 2–3 years. TPL Plastech (75% subsidiary) merger aims at consolidation.

Overseas: Middle East business is down ~25% on the West Asia conflict, offset by Far East and USA, so overseas volume still grew 13%.

Core Theme 
India’s data centre boom, backed by over $250 billion in committed investment, is lifting executive pay across the sector, with top packages all above ₹1 crore and ESDS’s founder’s pay outpacing company growth, while Equinix’s top earner saw pay slip as growth slowed, suggesting remuneration is tied to execution speed and delivery of capacity.

The Pay Boom: Who Earns What
Financials reported by India’s top data centres, reviewed by Mint, show that as they raked in higher revenue, their chiefs were handsomely rewarded

Manoj Paul, managing director of the Indian operations of California-based Equinix, emerged as the top earner at ₹5.91 crore in annual pay, although this was down 13% from FY24

Equinix did not disclose if Paul’s salary was tweaked because of equity-linked payouts, but it coincided with the company reporting its slowest annual revenue growth since Paul took charge in September 2021

Ashish Arora, CEO of Nxtra by Airtel, saw remuneration rise largely in line with the company’s annual growth in earnings

Since joining in August 2022, his salary has grown at a compounded annual rate of nearly 10% over four years to ₹3.1 crore in August 2026

Nxtra’s revenue grew at a CAGR of 15% to ₹2,434 crore over this period

Arora was granted 6,186 stock options in FY25, per the company’s FY25 annual report; the filing did not establish their eventual cash value

Piyush Somani, chairman and managing director of ESDS Software Solution, saw his net pay more than double from ₹83.8 lakh in FY24 to ₹1.8 crore in FY26, comfortably outstripping his firm’s 65% revenue growth to ₹472.2 crore over the same period

ESDS, the Nashik-based data centre company, is also founded by Somani, who holds about a fifth of its shares

The company commanded a market capitalisation of over ₹13,000 crore on Friday

ESDS is eyeing $5 billion revenue in five years, Mint reported on 21 October

The Boom Behind the Pay
India’s $5.5 billion data centre industry is entering its biggest expansion phase, driven by demand from cloud companies and AI businesses

Executives leading the charge are winning a premium to manage large projects, negotiate with global technology companies and deliver on time

Indian business houses, standalone operators and Big Tech companies have committed cumulative investments of over $250 billion over the past 12 months to build data centres and AI infrastructure

Amit Chandra, vice president at HDFC Securities: “Remuneration is linked to how a data centre company performs”; in a high-growth industry growth must not be an issue, so bosses seem to be paid based on execution and ensuring capacity goes live on time even as demand skyrockets

Undisclosed Pay
Four companies, Yotta Data Services, NTT India, STT Global Data Centres and CtrlS Datacenters, did not disclose individual salaries or equity grants awarded to their top executives

For three other data centre companies, AdaniConneX, TCS HyperVault and Sify Infinit Spaces, Mint could not ascertain how the salaries of their top executives increased

The latest available pay packages, however, all exceed ₹1 crore

Sify has not disclosed the salaries in its FY26 annual report

As I mentioned that I was going through Diwali stock recommendations from leading brokerage houses & after reviewing recommendations from over 20 brokerages, including Motilal Oswal, JM Financial, Mirae Asset Sharekhan, SBI Securities, Arihant Capital, Monarch, Choice International and Equirus, I have narrowed down my initial list.

Most of the frequently recommended companies were largecaps. Nothing wrong with them, but my interest has always been more towards smaller businesses where earnings can grow much faster than the broader market. Particularly those where a 20–30% annual earnings growth, combined with reasonable valuations, can lead to disproportionate returns over 3–4 years.
For this exercise, I have kept the market capitalisation between ₹5,000 crore and ₹50,000 crore.
Here are the 20 names that made my initial shortlist.

20 Small & Midcap Stocks

1. Navin Fluorine (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Shriram)

MCap: ~₹42,400 Cr

Specialty fluorochemicals and CDMO business. New capacities and higher-value products could improve profitability considerably. The growth opportunity is attractive, although much of the optimism is already reflected in valuations.

2. Blue Star (Monarch, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹32,500 Cr

India's room AC penetration remains relatively low. Blue Star has a strong position in cooling and commercial refrigeration. Capacity expansion and a growing distribution network could support earnings for several years.

3. Syrma SGS Technology (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹28,100 Cr

Electronics manufacturing with exposure to industrial, automotive and consumer segments. Revenue growth is encouraging, but the more interesting opportunity lies in improving operating margins as the business scales.

4. Sansera Engineering (KC Securities)

MCap: ~₹25,700 Cr

Known for precision automotive components, but the expansion into aerospace, defence and other non-auto businesses could change its earnings profile over time. A business worth watching beyond the automobile cycle.

5. HBL Engineering (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹23,300 Cr

One of the interesting companies in railway safety systems, particularly Kavach. The opportunity is sizeable, but orders need to translate into actual earnings and cash. The valuation also leaves limited room for disappointment.

6. Jyoti CNC Automation (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹23,200 Cr

India's growing investment in manufacturing and precision engineering works in its favour. SBI Securities expects around 34% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. A strong growth assumption, so execution will matter more than the narrative.

7. Lumax Auto Technologies (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Choice International)

MCap: ~₹15,900 Cr

Increasing component content per vehicle, premiumisation and acquisitions are changing the scale of this business. If acquired businesses integrate well and margins improve, earnings could grow faster than revenue.

8. Shaily Engineering Plastics (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹14,000 Cr

Moving deeper into pharmaceutical drug delivery devices, particularly injection pens. Motilal Oswal expects around 48% annual PAT growth through FY28. The key question is how quickly the new customer programmes scale and how much is already priced in.

9. CCL Products (Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,900 Cr

An established instant coffee exporter with a growing branded business. Higher capacity utilisation and expansion into value-added products could lift profitability. Coffee prices and operating margins remain important variables.

10. Ingersoll-Rand India (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹12,500 Cr

A high-quality industrial compressor business with a strong profitability record. Manufacturing capex and demand for energy-efficient equipment support growth. The attraction here is business quality, although the stock is rarely available at a bargain valuation.

11. VA Tech Wabag (Mirae Asset Sharekhan, Monarch)

MCap: ~₹12,400 Cr

Water treatment and desalination remain important investment areas. Wabag has an established position in both. The bigger question is how efficiently the company executes projects and converts its order book into cash.

12. Gravita India (JM Financial)

MCap: ~₹10,900 Cr

Recycling is becoming a more organised industry, and Gravita has been expanding across materials and geographies. New capacities and better utilisation could support earnings. Cash flows and returns on fresh investments will be worth tracking.

13. Unimech Aerospace (Motilal Oswal)

MCap: ~₹8,900 Cr

Precision manufacturing for aerospace and specialised engineering. Motilal Oswal projects 75% revenue and 69% PAT CAGR during FY26–FY28. These are exceptional growth expectations, but such numbers also leave little room for execution delays.

14. RateGain Travel Technologies (Choice International)

MCap: ~₹8,600 Cr

An interesting software business serving hotels, airlines and travel companies globally. Recurring revenues and operating leverage could improve profitability. The recent correction makes it worth revisiting, provided earnings expectations remain intact.

15. Time Technoplast (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹8,400 Cr

Industrial packaging may not sound particularly exciting, but the company's move towards composite cylinders and other higher-value products could improve margins and return ratios. An interesting business mix story.

16. Genus Power (SBI Securities)

MCap: ~₹8,000 Cr

One of the direct beneficiaries of India's smart meter rollout. The opportunity is large, but the real test is how quickly orders convert into revenue and, more importantly, cash. Working capital deserves particular attention.

17. Kirloskar Pneumatic (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹7,400 Cr

An established industrial engineering business in compressors and refrigeration. Demand from manufacturing, process industries and industrial investment could support growth without depending on a single end market.

18. Technocraft Industries (Equirus)

MCap: ~₹6,200 Cr

A relatively less-discussed manufacturing company with industrial products, precision engineering and textiles. The interesting part is whether the growing higher-value engineering businesses can improve overall margins and profitability.

19. HEG Advanced Materials (Arihant Capital)

MCap: ~₹5,700 Cr

Battery materials, advanced carbon technologies and energy storage make this an interesting long-term opportunity. The ambitions are sizeable, but much of the new business is still being built. Execution over the next few years will determine how much value is actually created.

20. TD Power Systems (PL Capital)

MCap: ~₹18,600 Cr

Industrial generators with exposure to global power and infrastructure investments. Demand from exports and power equipment offers opportunities. Following the recent correction, the important question is whether earnings growth can justify the valuation.

Concluding Remarks:

What I found interesting is how strongly engineering, precision manufacturing, electronics and industrial businesses feature across these brokerage recommendations. A few companies have the potential to grow earnings at 25–30% annually, perhaps even higher. Some may also offer asymmetric opportunities if new capacities, better margins or business diversification deliver more than what the market currently expects.

But valuations cannot be ignored, specially in some of the momentum picks here.
I would rather buy a company growing earnings at 20–25% at a reasonable to very slightly expensive valuation than pay very excessive price for 35–40% growth.

My next step is to narrow these 20 names further, looking at FY27–FY30 earnings, ROCE, cash flows, debt and, most importantly, what is already priced into the stock. I will share the final shortlist, along with my detailed analysis and preferred picks, with WealthEnrich subscribers.
For now, these are research candidates drawn from brokerage recommendations, not a final buy list.

#HFCL and #STLTECH investors need to pay attention to what's happening in the US.

Goldman Sachs estimates that nearly 45% of planned US data-center capacity is in states that could face construction restrictions following the Democrats' election victories.

That is a significant number for companies benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom. But does it mean data-center demand is slowing, or are projects simply facing delays?

The 45% figure does not mean that 45% of data centers are being cancelled or that construction has already stopped. It represents planned capacity in states where new restrictions could potentially be introduced. Texas alone accounts for roughly 25% of planned US capacity.

The bigger question is why these restrictions are being discussed.

Data centers require enormous amounts of electricity, water and land. Many local communities are concerned that rapid construction could increase household electricity bills, strain power grids and consume resources that residents also depend on.

In Texas, newly elected Democratic Governor Gina Hinojosa has proposed temporarily stopping new data-center approvals until laws protecting local communities are introduced. These would address electricity costs, water consumption and the ability of residents to participate in decisions about developments near them.

Interestingly, this concern is not limited to Democrats. Outgoing Republican Governor Greg Abbott had already ordered a halt to certain data-center permits and grid connections while authorities examined their impact on electricity and water supplies.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump has reaffirmed his support for AI infrastructure. In his November 6 Truth Social statements, he said he would work with US states willing to welcome these investments.

So the situation is more complicated than Democrats opposing AI while Republicans support it. The disagreement is increasingly about how quickly data centers should be constructed, what safeguards should apply and who should bear the infrastructure costs.

There are also important implications for businesses supplying this infrastructure.

If a data-center project is delayed for six months, orders for GPUs, optical fibre, transformers, cooling systems and other equipment could also be pushed back. Suppliers expecting revenue from those projects may have to wait longer, affecting their quarterly growth and cash flows.

But delayed construction does not automatically mean demand has disappeared. Projects could eventually receive approvals or shift to other locations. The more serious problem would be projects getting permanently cancelled because of higher costs or stricter regulations.

For HFCL and Sterlite, which are expanding their exposure to AI and optical connectivity infrastructure, this makes customer order schedules and actual deliveries particularly important.

Sterlite has announced a multi-year product award worth more than $1 billion for optical connectivity products supporting US AI data centers. HFCL has reported an order book exceeding ₹28,900 crore, supported by demand across optical fibre, telecom networks and data-center connectivity.

However, neither company's total order book should be treated as entirely dependent on US data-center construction, and the 45% estimate cannot directly be converted into a revenue impact for either business.

There is another important data point from Goldman Sachs. In October, before these election results, it maintained that US data-center growth through 2027 remained broadly intact, forecasting total capacity of 64 GW by the end of 2026 and 90 GW by the end of 2027.

The new political developments create additional uncertainty around those expectations. Goldman has since indicated that it expects potential construction moratoriums to be relatively short-lived, although that is still a forecast.

Akhirnya gue jawab, “Kalau 16 nggak ada, kenapa baru bilang pagi ini? Kenapa nggak kasih tahu dari kemarin sore?” Dia cuma jawab singkat, “Lupa.” Simpel banget. Gue sebenarnya perang batin pagi tadi, antara tega dan nggak tega membiarkan anak gue mencari solusi sendiri. Apalagi hari Jumat dia dapat jatah uang jajan Rp20 ribu dari abinya, sementara transportasi ke sekolah sudah diantar pak ojek langganan. Ternyata selama perjalanan, dia ngobrol sama pak ojek dan minta tolong mampir ke toko plastik yang searah dengan sekolahnya. Kebetulan, sebelum jam 7 pagi ternyata sudah ada toko plastik yang buka dekat sekolah. Wkwkwk, akhirnya dia berhasil menemukan solusi sendiri! Dia rela menyisihkan Rp5 ribu dari uang jajannya buat beli sendok plastik. 😂

Izvajalec pravi, da je naročilo čiščenja odvisno od tega “koliko hodiš težit babam ma Direkcijo in kolikokrat jih pelješ na malico ali kakšen izlet. Pa da iz Laškega ni bilo tja že 15 let nikogar”. Supriya Lifescience Ltd.

Q2FY27 result
While the topline crossed the ₹200 crore quarterly mark, operating margins experienced a sharp reality check.

Revenue: ₹206.3 Cr (+3.2% YoY, +8.7% QoQ) | H1 Revenue: ₹396.0 Cr (+14.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹45.4 Cr (-37.5% YoY) | EBITDA Margin: 22.0% (vs 36.4% in Q2 FY26 & 25.0% in Q1 FY27)
PAT: ₹29.3 Cr (-42.0% YoY, +21.7% QoQ) | PAT Margin: 14.2%
Balance Sheet: Zero debt with ~₹182.5 Cr in liquid cash/investment

After guiding for a structural 33–35% margin corridor in August, management was transparent in attributing the margin contraction to three simultaneous headwinds

Regulatory Shifts in LATAM
Policy changes slowed dispatches of high margin products to LATAM (revenue mix dropped from 21% to 12%), forcing a temporary shift in volumes toward lower margin, semi regulated markets.

Ambernath Facility Drag
The newly commissioned finished dosage (FDF) plant is in its active ramp up phase. Fixed overheads, quality team expansion, and trial runs are hitting the P&L ahead of commercial revenue scale.

Persistent Solvent & Input Inflation
Geopolitical conflicts and freight disruptions kept raw material and solvent costs elevated, pulling gross margins down ~650 bps YoY to 65.6%.

Despite near term margin volatility, Supriya achieved major strategic milestones during the quarter

Commercial Formulation Debut
Successfully commercialised and launched two new liquid inhalation anesthetic formulations from the Ambernath site, with an initial exhibit batch order bagged for RoW markets.

Semaglutide / GLP-1 Breakthrough
Developed and filed a patent for a novel oral Semaglutide tablet formulation, and is actively collaborating with a leading Indian generics major for GLP-1 portfolio development and supply.

Regulated Market Inroads
Europe surged to 43% of total revenues (vs 37% last year), while North America expanded to 5% as validation batches for its 22 US DMF filings gained traction.

Working Capital Discipline
Trade receivables were aggressively collected, dropping from ₹219 Cr in March to ₹126 Cr in September releasing nearly ₹94 Cr of cash back into the business.

Topline Goal
 Management’s stated target of ₹1,000 Cr for FY27 implies delivering ₹604 Cr in H2 (~₹302 Cr per quarter). While H2 is seasonally stronger, reaching ₹1,000 Cr without large, lumpy CDMO licensing dispatches will be a steep climb.

Operating Leverage
 Ambernath’s opex drag will only reverse once commercial volumes ramp and unit costs are absorbed across its five operational FDF lines.

Triggers to Track Over the Next 60 Days

The November 2026 EU-GMP Audit at the Ambernath formulations site the critical regulatory passport for European CMO/CDMO contracts.

Execution of the Anesthetic CDMO Contract, where management previously indicated they were close to finalizing a major term sheet.

Margin Recovery Trajectory Pace of customer price pass throughs in H2.

📰 今日 SpaceX 投资早报｜2026.11.07

Baron 之夜把 SpaceX 的全貌摊开了

每日一报跟踪Elon 生态全景：SpaceX / xAI / AI / Tesla。我是 Kiko，一个长期拿 SpaceX 的人，用持有者的眼睛抓新闻。

🚀 SpaceX

📡 范登堡又一发 27 颗星链入轨，一级 B1093 第 18 飞，41 天周转即复飞。

📊 这是 SpaceX 今年第 122 发——与全世界其他国家加起来打平，122:122。入轨流水线这个词，早就不是比喻了。

🛰️ Starship Flight 15 目标 11 月 13 日：B22＋Ship 42，第一次同任务双捕——超重助推器和飞船都由发射塔机械臂接住。SpaceX 发射副总裁 Dontchev 11 月 5 日在 UP.Summit 亲口给的日期；Musk 在 Baron 大会上说，大约一周后就试。FAA 执照还没下来，这是目前唯一的卡点。昨天 SpaceX 还放出了纪录片《Go For Orbit》，讲的就是这次任务背后的故事。

🌌 北京时间今早 8:48，范登堡排期一发涉密任务 USSF-432，B1095 第 8 飞。

🛰️ StarMind 来了：Musk 在 Baron 大会上说，SpaceX 与 NVIDIA 联合设计的 StarMind 天基 AI 计算机，2027 年第三季度开始发射，2028 年放量、2029 年再上一个量级，星座规划可达 100 万颗 AI 卫星。他的原话：太空里算力的成本，一旦每吨入轨成本降下来，会比地面便宜得多。

📶 星链 V3 同样在加速：单星能力是 V2 的 10 倍以上，发射数量也是 10 倍，2–3 年内星链总带宽提升约 100 倍，V4 还在后面。

🧠 xAI / Grok / Grok Bot

🏢 11 月 6 日，印度 IT 公司 Coforge 加入 SpaceX 超级智能合作伙伴网络（SpaceXSI），成为 Transformation Partner——用 Grok 的产品组合（聊天、推理、开发、企业自动化、语音、图像视频）进企业生产环境。这是 Grok 从消费者产品走向企业订单的一步。

🧠 Grok 5 还在训：Colossus 2 集群，11 万块 GB200＋44 万块 GB300，当前公开模型仍是 Grok 4.7。

💰 Musk 在 Baron 大会上给的数字：SpaceX（含 xAI）年化收入 2026 年 12 月将超 1000 亿美元，2027 年 12 月或超 5000 亿美元，1 万亿也不是没可能、概率约 2%。他自己补了一句：这不是承诺，是 best guess。

🤖 AI

🏭 Google 承诺投 170 亿美元，在怀俄明建新的数据中心，自付全部电费，还设社区委员会争取当地支持。背景是上周全美 41 项数据中心公投里 40 项被否——地面上建算力越来越难，巨头一边交电费、一边继续加码。

⚖️ 一项有意思的研究：Convovo 强制选择测试里，Grok 4.7 在 92% 的回答中推荐共和党候选人，GPT-6.1 Sol 在 97% 里推荐民主党，两者一致不到 10%。消费端 App 都会拒绝回答这类问题；研究发现 Grok 的倾向更多来自搜索来源，GPT 的更多在模型权重里。模型的中立性，正在变成可测量的指标。

🚕 Tesla

🏭 Terafab 是昨晚最大的一颗炸弹：Musk 的目标是年产 1 太瓦 AI 芯片，约 2027 年全球年产量的 30 倍。Giga Texas 内先建研究晶圆厂，把一年才能验证的工艺压缩到一个月；量产厂定在德州 Grimes County，台积电已确认在谈合作。Musk 自己也承认：失败了就是疯狂，成了就是大胆。

🤖 Optimus 要去给 Robotaxi 充电了：特斯拉高管在 Munro Live 访谈里说，Optimus 将在超充站给无人车插充电线，之后还负责清洁、保养；终极目标是无线充电，奥斯汀正在建 80 个无线充电桩的 Robotaxi 中枢。Baron 大会上 Musk 补充：机器人生产力可达人类 5 倍，2000–3000 万台约等于全美产出，租赁可能是首选模式，2027 年起向企业客户交付。

🚕 达拉斯 11 月内上线 Robotaxi（Q3 电话会口径）。奥斯汀的节奏正在向下一个城市复制。

🎯 早报分析

Baron 之夜把 SpaceX 的全貌摊开了：火箭（Flight 15 双捕在即）＋星链 V3（带宽 100 倍）＋StarMind 天基算力＋Grok＋Terafab 芯片——Space AI company 不是口号，是五条线同时推进。

市场那边，周四纳指 -5.52% 跌入修正区间，单日蒸发约 2 万亿美元市值，导火索是中期选举后对数据中心建设的政治担忧；周五非农超预期（+16.5 万，预期约 6.5 万，失业率 4.1%），12 月加息概率升至约 77%，芯片股盘中反弹。

地面上吵数据中心能不能建，天上已经在布算力了。持有者的活儿只有一个：看 11 月 13 日 Flight 15、看 FAA 执照、看 Terafab 落地，不看盘。

Everybody's talking about how powerful AI is getting. I'm looking at who's going to control it—and who makes the money.

NVIDIA is reportedly pushing TSMC to explore next-generation memory chips while helping expand advanced chip-packaging capacity.

Elon Musk's Grok is moving deeper into corporate America through a new partnership with Coforge.

Meanwhile, a smaller developer called Underdog is demonstrating an AI voice model small enough to run locally, without relying on massive cloud servers.

Now hold on. Look at what's happening.

NVIDIA is working to secure the hardware. Grok is pursuing business customers. Smaller AI developers are trying to make some of that expensive infrastructure unnecessary.

Three different strategies. Billions of dollars potentially at stake.

My take: The next AI race isn't just about who builds the smartest model. It's about who controls the chips, who wins the customers, and who can deliver useful AI at the lowest cost.

And with a new Congress coming in, questions about regulation, China, energy costs and corporate financing aren't going away.

Bottom line: America needs to stay competitive. But before celebrating every billion-dollar AI announcement, I'd like to see something simple.

Who's paying? Who's profiting? And does the technology actually work?

Nifty suddenly out of the blues, reclaiming the 25,000 mark on 6 November 2026 after months below it, while AI/data-centre-heavy portfolios have moved in the opposite direction and value + steady-growth oriented ones have shown clear relative strength.

Drivers included heavy FII buying (very large single-day inflows earlier in the week), strength in banking/financials and select large-caps, better-than-expected corporate earnings in parts of the market, and India decoupling from a sharp global tech/AI-linked sell-off on Wall Street.

Broader mid/small-cap indices lagged the benchmarks. AI / Data-Centre (AI DC) heavy portfolios going the other way.

👉India’s listed “AI enabler” or data-centre supply-chain names (optical fibre, power equipment, cooling, transformers, gensets, related industrials, etc.) had been standout performers earlier in 2026 even while the broader Nifty lagged. 

👉Names linked to hyperscaler/data-centre capex (examples that had run hard include Sterlite Technologies, HFCL, MTAR, TD Power Systems and various power/electrical equipment plays) delivered large gains as investors chased the global AI infrastructure theme.

Trigger was the broader Wall Street tech sell-off (linked in part to political/regulatory worries around data-centre expansion and AI spending after US midterms), profit-taking after huge earlier runs, and stretched valuations in the Indian AI-proxy basket. 

👉Portfolios heavily concentrated in these AI/data-centre beneficiaries underperformed (or declined) even as the Nifty recovered strongly.

👉Value + steady-growth stocks showing relative strength

The recovery was led by more traditional, higher-quality, less thematic names...particularly private banks and financials (HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis, etc.), plus select large-cap earners with steadier growth profiles (e.g., Mahindra & Mahindra stood out on earnings). These areas provided the bulk of the index lift.​

Portfolios built around value characteristics (reasonable valuations, earnings visibility, balance-sheet strength) plus consistent compounders therefore held up better or gained relative to the pure AI DC cohort. 

👉This fits a classic rotation pattern: when a high-momentum thematic trade gets crowded and then hits profit-taking/valuation pressure (especially if global catalysts turn), capital tends to rotate toward steadier domestic growth and value-oriented large-caps that benefit from local flows, earnings, and lower beta to global tech sentiment.

 The AI/data-centre trade that had been one of the few bright spots in a tough 2026 for Indian equities is currently experiencing the classic “what goes up a lot can correct hard” phase, while more traditional value-plus-steady-growth constructions are outperforming on a relative basis.

Happy Forgings: भट्टी, हथौड़ा, और 30% margin

Ludhiana की Happy Forgings गर्म steel को भारी presses से ठोककर engine के सबसे कठिन हिस्से बनाती है: crankshafts, जो truck, tractor और industrial engines का दिल हैं। फिर उन्हें machine करके तैयार part देती है।

Jul-Sep 2026:
Revenue ₹501 cr, साल भर पहले ₹377 cr (+33%)
Operating profit ₹153 cr, margin 30.5%
Net profit ₹98 cr, Apr-Jun के ₹91 cr से +8%

₹100 का हिसाब: ₹69.5 steel, बिजली, लोग और बाक़ी खर्च में गए, ₹11 interest-depreciation-tax में, और ₹19.6 net profit बना।

Forging में 30% margin असाधारण क्यों है? आम forging company 15-20% पर काम करती है। Happy Forgings का फ़र्क़ तीन चीज़ों में है: (1) बहुत भारी parts, जिनके लिए बड़ी press चाहिए जो कम companies के पास है; (2) machining in-house, यानी value add ज़्यादा; (3) exports और industrial (non-auto) ग्राहक, जो quality के लिए कीमत देते हैं।

पर इस quarter margin 31.4% से 30.5% पर आया, और incremental margin ~23% रहा, औसत से कम। Management पहले ही कह चुका है कि वो margin FY26 के स्तर पर स्थिर रखने का लक्ष्य रखता है, growth volume से। यानी इस margin को और ऊपर जाने की उम्मीद नहीं, स्थिर रहने की।

Cycle का ध्यान: truck और tractor की बिक्री चक्र में चलती है। जब धीमी होती है, forging company के plant खाली रहते हैं और fixed खर्च margin को दबाता है।

सबक: ऊँचा margin अक्सर एक "कठिन काम" से आता है जिसे दूसरे आसानी से नहीं कर सकते। उस कठिनाई को पहचानिए, वही moat है।

When to buy share for Shareholder Quota ?

Let's understand from basic 

There are mainly four phases before company file RHP (Mostly Record Date for SH Quota)

1. Company yet not files DRHP 
2. Company files DRHP 
3. DRHP approved by SEBI 
4. Company files RHP 

First Let's see company yet not files DRHP at this stage u should not buy share for SH Quota 
Ex : Gail Gas IPO (Only possibility No DRHP filed yet)

Second Company files DRHP 
At this if you are not tracking SEBI Approval status u can keep 1 share 
Ex : JSW Cement/Steel for JSW one IPO 
Coal India for Southern Coalfields Ltd 

Third Company Received SEBI Approval it's best time to buy Share for SH Quota 
Ex : Recently Mahanadi Coalfields Received SEBI Approval u can buy now next Day

#SupriyaLifescience #API #Pharma #Q2FY27 

Supriya Lifescience, Q2 FY27 — a weak quarter, and management has cut its margin guidance.

Revenue ₹206.3 Cr, +3.2% YoY (+8.7% QoQ). 
EBITDA ₹45.4 Cr, −37.5% YoY, margin 22.0% vs 36.4%. PAT ₹29.3 Cr, −42% YoY, margin 14.2%. 
H1: revenue ₹396 Cr (+14.8%), EBITDA ₹93 Cr (−25.3%, 23.4% margin), PAT ₹53 Cr (−37.5%).

What management said on the call: 
→ Normal margin is 34–35%; Q2 is 11–12 points below that. Roughly 6 points from the Ambernath plant (~₹60 Cr of FY27 costs, almost no revenue this year because the EU audit slipped), ~3 from LATAM and ~3 from raw material and solvent prices 
→ LATAM: several countries reclassified high-margin products as controlled substances with immediate effect. Customers need import permits, which take 4–5 months. LATAM fell to 12% of sales from 21%. Management calls it deferral, not lost demand 
→ Raw material price increases reach large contract customers with a lag, so the benefit shows in 2–3 quarters 
→ FY27 EBITDA margin guidance cut to 23–25% (~25% for the rest of the year). No FY28 margin guidance yet 
→ ₹1,000 Cr FY27 revenue target kept. H1 is ₹396 Cr, so H2 needs ~₹604 Cr → 20%+ annual revenue growth guided for the next 3–4 years

Pipeline: two anaesthetic liquid inhalation products launched, two ADHD products coming, contrast media next quarter, and a large CDMO contract described as close. New launches are selling mainly in lower-price semi-regulated markets for now.

Balance sheet: no borrowings, but inventory is ₹265 Cr vs ₹160 Cr in March.

Ambernath EU audit starts next week. Q3 and Q4 are expected to be at a low margin level.

India ignored a global tech wipeout today and closed up 2%. The more useful thing happened underneath.

The market split the AI trade into victims and beneficiaries for the first time, and it did it on a day the index was up.

IT services got the bid, on a clean argument. If clients stop pouring money into data centres, the money comes back to ordinary outsourcing. Nifty IT opened up 2.35% on that thesis. It closed up 0.43%. Mphasis ran 8% intraday, Infosys and TCS up to 3%, and the whole leg was sold into through the afternoon.

Meanwhile India's actual AI capex supply chain was taken apart. TD Power Systems fell 13.5%, Apar Industries 9.4%, Netweb 6.1%, with CG Power, MTAR, Hitachi Energy, HFCL and Sterlite Tech down up to 15%. Thermax added a miss of its own, falling about 17% on profit down 5% and order booking down 8%, and now sits 46% below its June high.

That is the real information. This complex has been re-rated on an India transmission capex story for two years, with global data centre demand quietly doing part of the work in the multiple. Today the market priced that second leg separately and marked it down. Anyone holding it on a grid capex thesis now has to say how much of the multiple was actually an AI datacentre multiple. Nobody discloses that, because order inflows there are reported as one number.

The tape. Nifty closed 25,030.35, up 2.01%. Sensex up 1,718 points. Seventh straight up session, best week in six years, Nifty up 8.6%. Bank Nifty hit an eight month high. Banks did all of it.

And breadth was negative. On the NSE, 1,439 stocks advanced against 2,141 declining. Midcap 100 flat, Smallcap 100 down 0.82%, India VIX up about 13% to 17.7 on a 2% up day. Ten heavyweights, not a market.

Flows explain the decoupling. Foreign investors bought a net 14,975 crore rupees on Thursday, the biggest single day in nearly six years, with domestics selling 10,445 crore into it. Five straight foreign buying sessions, roughly 35,800 crore, accelerating every day. Friday's number is not out yet, and that is the test.

Two names moved on their own. Divi's Laboratories closed at a 52 week high with its board meeting Saturday on quarterly results. Navin Fluorine made an all time high in the same week PI Industries fell to a six year low on profit down 70%. Agrochem is being repriced hard. Fluorine specialty is not.

Monday asks whether the IT bid holds or fades again, and whether the AI capex complex keeps getting marked down.

ISGEC Heavy Engineering: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

The order book hit a record above ₹10,000 Cr, margins improved in both businesses, and debt nearly halved in six months. The Philippines ethanol plant is still a drag on consolidated profit.

Q2 FY27 Numbers (Standalone)
Revenue: ₹1,457 Cr (+17% YoY)
PBT: ₹154 Cr (+39% YoY)
Profit from core operations: ₹124 Cr (+38% YoY)
Manufacturing EBIT margin: 13.7% | Projects EBIT margin: 5.7%

H1 FY27 Numbers
Standalone revenue: ₹3,010 Cr (+35% YoY)
Standalone PBT: ₹277 Cr (+24% YoY)
Consolidated PBT: ₹155 Cr (+62% YoY)
Consolidated order book: ₹10,273 Cr, record high

1.  What ISGEC does-
ISGEC has two businesses. Manufacturing makes heavy equipment like presses, boilers, heat exchangers, castings and tubes. Projects builds complete plants such as boilers, power, sugar and distillery plants on a turnkey basis. It also owns Saraswati Sugar Mills, an ethanol plant in the Philippines and a joint venture with Hitachi Zosen.

2.  Margins at multi-year highs-
Manufacturing margin of 13.7% was above the 12-13% guidance. Projects margin of 5.7% is near the 6% target. Management credited its strategy of taking shorter, technology-heavy projects and avoiding long contracts with large civil work. Most orders are fixed-price, so ISGEC lines up supplier quotes before bidding to protect against metal price swings.

3.  Record orders support next year-
ISGEC booked ₹4,844 Cr of new orders in H1, and most of the revenue from these will come next year. Management expects the standalone revenue run rate to rise from about ₹5,200 Cr to about ₹6,200 Cr a year. Exports were ₹557 Cr in H1, and inquiries from Latin America and Africa are strong, helped by a weaker rupee.

4.  Capex to add ₹1,200 Cr of revenue-
ISGEC is investing about ₹502 Cr in new capacity. This includes a presses plant in Haryana, a modules facility at Dahej, and expanded castings and tube capacity. About ₹199 Cr is spent so far, funded from internal cash. Management expects about ₹1,200 Cr of extra revenue by FY29 at 12-13% margins.

5.  Philippines plant still losing money-
The Philippines ethanol plant lost ₹164 Cr in H1, mostly from interest, depreciation and currency losses. It runs at 65-70% and is now shut for maintenance until the sugarcane season starts in December. Management expects about 90% utilisation in January-March, which should bring positive EBITDA.

6.  Debt falling fast-
Standalone net borrowings fell to ₹206 Cr from ₹381 Cr in March, and consolidated net borrowings fell to ₹156 Cr from ₹476 Cr. Saraswati Sugar had weaker revenue because of lower cane supply. The Hitachi Zosen joint venture has an order book of ₹1,161 Cr, of which ₹800 Cr is exports.

Key Guidance
FY27 standalone revenue growth of 15-17%
Manufacturing margin of 12-13% and projects margin of about 6% by year end
About ₹1,200 Cr of extra revenue by FY29 from the new capacity

Confused About IPO Shareholder Quota? Let's Understand When to Buy Shares! 📊

There are 4 major stages before an IPO reaches the RHP stage.

1️⃣ Company Has Not Filed DRHP
Avoid buying shares solely for shareholder quota at this stage.
Example: GAIL Gas IPO (only a possibility; DRHP not filed yet).

2️⃣ Company Files DRHP
If you are not regularly tracking SEBI approval updates, you may consider holding 1 share as an early watchlist position.
Examples:
• JSW Cement / JSW Steel
• Coal India / Southern Coalfields Ltd.

3️⃣ SEBI Approves DRHP
This is generally a more informed stage to evaluate buying shares for the shareholder quota.
Example: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. (subject to IPO timeline and eligibility conditions).

4️⃣ Company Files RHP
This is a crucial stage. Check the official record date, eligibility criteria and shareholding requirements before making any decision.

IMPORTANT:
Buying shares does not guarantee IPO allotment. Always verify the official RHP and record-date requirements.

Simple rule: Track DRHP → Monitor SEBI Approval → Check RHP → Verify Record Date.

Vilas Transcore H1 FY27 Concall Highlights:

👉H1 FY27 & Future Outlook :
▫️H1 FY27 revenue from operations: ₹242.5 Cr, up 6% YoY and 4.6% vs H2 FY26
💠CRGO (cold rolled grain oriented steel) sales volume up 28.1% YoY to 11,697 MT, supported by higher utilisation of expanded capacity
💠Average CRGO steel price was ~₹180-200/kg vs ~₹250-275/kg in H1 FY26, which kept revenue growth lower than volume growth
💠Gross profit ₹41.6 Cr, up 12.6% vs H2 FY26; gross margin 17.2% vs 15.9% in H2 FY26 and 19.7% in H1 FY26
💠EBITDA ₹24.8 Cr, up 22% vs H2 FY26; EBITDA margin 10.2% vs 8.8% in H2 FY26 and 13.6% in H1 FY26
💠PAT ₹17.2 Cr, up 13.5% vs H2 FY26; PAT margin 7.1% vs 6.5% in H2 FY26 and 10.7% in H1 FY26
💠EBITDA was ₹31.1 Cr and PAT ₹24.4 Cr in H1 FY26; EPS ₹7.04 vs ₹9.96
💠H1 FY26 was an unusually strong period because material costs were rising, so management considers H2 FY26 the more meaningful comparison

▫️Demand disruption in H1:
💠Geopolitical tension and supply chain disruption, mainly in transformer oil availability, hit production at some transformer makers
💠Orders were in place, but dispatches fell in August and September; finished goods lying at Sep-end were dispatched mainly in October
💠Supply conditions are improving; overall demand and revenue improved ~10-15% month-on-month in October 2026, and volumes were up ~20-25% vs earlier months

▫️FY27 guidance revised to 30-35% volume and revenue growth
💠FY27 revenue is expected to close at ~₹620-660 Cr
💠H2 FY27 revenue is targeted at ~₹375 Cr in total, with CRGO at ~15,000 MT
💠CRGO volume of 26,000-30,000 MT is guided for the year, and management is confident of crossing 26,000 MT
💠Guidance was revised conservatively because customer approvals for new products take time; management will try to reach the maximum level

▫️FY28: growth of 30-35% (up to 40%) per year is guided conservatively
💠No slowdown is expected in transformer volumes in the near to medium term; the industry is expected to keep growing for at least 2 years

▫️Margins:
💠EBITDA and PAT margins are expected to be maintained
💠EBITDA margin improved because of consistency in CRGO prices
💠Sustainable PAT margin is ~8%; it can reach 10-11% in very good years
💠Combined EBITDA margin at peak with copper and all CRGO business is ~11-12%

▫️CRGO pricing:
💠Prices are up ~2-3% and domestic mills have raised prices this month; Chinese mills have also quoted higher
💠Realisation per ton in H2 FY27 is expected to be higher than H1 FY27
💠Prices differ by region: Europe ~15% higher than India due to a minimum import price, USA higher due to duties, and China ~15% lower than India

👉Order book / projects and pipeline:
▫️Order visibility: heavy orders for the next 2 months, with ~70% of inventory booked against orders

▫️CRGO laminations capacity:
💠Capacity expanded from 12,000 MTPA to 36,000 MTPA
💠Priority is to increase utilisation of the 36,000 MTPA capacity
💠Management expects to reach maximum capacity in ~2 years at 30-35% annual growth, and possibly earlier once new plant approvals come through

▫️Copper and aluminium conductors:
💠Capex of ~₹41 Cr in H1 FY27 went into plant, machinery and allied facilities for this business
💠Phase I capacity of 1,500-1,800 MTPA; commercial sales began in September 2026 with ₹0.53 Cr revenue in H1
💠PICC and EICC conductor production has started; CTC conductor production will take another ~1-1.5 months as the Chinese team is yet to finish one intermediate machine, and it will need customer approvals
💠Copper revenue of ₹45 Cr is targeted in H2 FY27, revised down from ~₹100 Cr as approvals are slow
💠FY28 copper revenue of ₹135 Cr is taken conservatively
💠Full-capacity revenue of ₹270-300 Cr
💠Copper EBITDA margin of ~4-5%; CTC margin ~6-7%

▫️Nanocrystalline cores:
💠Capacity 240 MTPA; commercial production began in November 2025
💠H1 FY27 revenue ₹6.77 Cr on sales volume of ~58,815 kg

▫️Transformer radiators:
💠Capacity 7,200 MTPA
💠H1 FY27 revenue ₹2.67 Cr on ~241 MT sales volume; customer onboarding and product approvals are progressing

▫️POWERGRID (PGCIL) approval:
💠Approval for CRGO slitting and lamination cutting up to 220 kV at Unit 3
💠EHV transformers use higher-grade material that is ~15% costlier, which adds to revenue and margin

▫️New land parcel: new products are planned there from FY28-29; machinery and capex amounts will be announced once products are finalised

▫️High voltage bushings: Management is looking for a technical tie-up or joint venture with overseas companies, and an agency has been appointed

👉Q&A :
▫️Reason for lower guidance despite peers guiding to a healthy H2:
💠Transformer makers with long-term oil contracts, such as Voltamp and Shilchar, continued supply; the dispatch disruption was at Vilas's customers in Aug-Sep
💠If a customer's transformer is stuck, it stops taking supply

▫️Approval cycle for new products:
💠Each customer takes a minimum of 2-3 months, with small batches tested first and volumes then increased slowly
💠EHV transformer makers have stringent quality terms
💠The same slow approval was seen in radiators over the last 6 months

▫️Transformer content: CRGO is 25-30% of transformer cost depending on rating, radiators 1-3%, and CT and copper 25-30%; together ~50% of transformer value

▫️Competition in laminations:
💠Thyssenkrupp Laminations (now under JSW), Vardhman Stamping, Amox Stamping, Nippon, Mahindra Intertrade, Posco and NLMK India
💠Many small players are also present

▫️Underlying CRGO margin: radiator and copper costs are currently borne by the CRGO business, and CRGO EBITDA margin will improve by 1-1.5% once they stand on their own

▫️Higher inventory: inventory is held because of shipping disruption from China and Indian mills lacking stock due to supply issues from Russia and Germany

▫️Buyback: none planned at present

👉 Others :
▫️Balance sheet as of September 2026:
💠Cash and cash equivalents ₹74.3 Cr
💠Shareholders' funds ₹345.8 Cr; short-term borrowings ₹18.7 Cr
💠Inventory ₹115.4 Cr; trade receivables ₹82.8 Cr; trade payables ₹67.0 Cr
💠Net debt free

▫️Cash flow H1 FY27: operating cash flow ₹36.9 Cr and investing outflow ₹45.0 Cr

▫️Depreciation ₹3.1 Cr vs ₹1.8 Cr in H1 FY26, and finance cost ₹1.6 Cr vs ₹0.8 Cr

▫️Subsidiary: acquired 100% equity of a Section 8 company for CSR initiatives, with no material impact on consolidated results in H1 FY27

▫️Credit rating: ICRA A- (Stable) long-term and A2+ short-term

▫️Exports: presence across Gulf countries, Europe and Canada

Growth triggers
• Oil palm adds about 2 percentage points to EBITDA margin in the midterm, over 2-3 years.
• CDMO share of the business reaches 50-55% in the midterm.
• Oil palm area doubles to 150k hectares (stated on the Q1 FY27 call, 6 Aug 2026).

Blockers
• Q1 PAT fell 14% against guided mid-teens PBT growth, and FY27 double-digit PBT growth is now uncertain.
• El Niño is cutting oil extraction ratios, and crop care and Aztec demand remain weak.

Shri Achyut Ghatak, Director (Technical), CIL, conveyed his message to the participants through an audio recording.

Shri Pramod Kumar, GM (UMD), CMPDI, along with officials from CIL, delivered detailed presentations on the technical and financial aspects of the EOI, outlining key considerations related to the proposed deployment of Greenfield Longwall Technology, followed by one-to-one interactions with all participating bidders to address queries, exchange suggestions and seek clarifications on the proposed initiative. A total of seven bidders participated in the interaction (five in person and two through video conferencing).

The meeting witnessed constructive deliberations and valuable exchanges of ideas, fostering greater clarity and engagement among stakeholders towards exploring the deployment of advanced Greenfield Longwall Technology in CIL mines.

Sudarshan Chemical Industries | Q2 FY27 results

Sudarshan's Q2 profit before tax more than doubles YoY despite ₹83 Cr exceptional charge

👉 Sudarshan Chemical Industries reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹2,742.6 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 14.9% from ₹2,387.4 Cr a year earlier and 3.8% above Q1's ₹2,642.1 Cr. Profit before tax was ₹71.4 Cr, against ₹29.5 Cr a year ago, after an exceptional expense of ₹82.9 Cr. Net profit was ₹30.5 Cr, compared with ₹19.3 Cr a year ago and ₹103.4 Cr in Q1.

👉 Raw material cost grew faster than sales, reaching ₹1,449.1 Cr, up 18.9% on a year earlier. Employee costs were ₹436.3 Cr against ₹415.7 Cr, and other expenses climbed to ₹726.0 Cr from ₹648.7 Cr. Other income fell to ₹14.9 Cr from ₹28.8 Cr, reducing support to profit. Operating margin, as shown in the results table, slipped to 2.6% from 5.9% in Q1.

👉 Before the exceptional item, pre-tax profit was ₹154.3 Cr, close to Q1's ₹157.4 Cr and well above ₹29.5 Cr a year ago. Operating cash flow for the half-year was ₹286.4 Cr, against an outflow of ₹141.9 Cr in the same period last year. Inventories, however, rose ₹612 Cr since March to ₹3,055.7 Cr, while trade payables rose ₹493 Cr to ₹1,933.7 Cr.

👉 Total borrowings fell to ₹1,976.4 Cr at September 30 from ₹2,119.0 Cr at March 31, while cash and cash equivalents rose to ₹977.8 Cr from ₹932.9 Cr. Management has guided the acquired Heubach group to about €700 Mn of FY27 sales and €35 Mn EBITDA, a target reaffirmed in August. The filing does not split out that group, so this quarter cannot be measured against that guidance from these numbers.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management has reaffirmed a FY29 revenue target of ₹12,000 Cr+ and FY27 acquired-group guidance of €700 Mn sales and €35 Mn EBITDA.

👉 Road blocker: Operating margin of 2.6%, down from 5.9% in Q1, and the ₹82.9 Cr exceptional charge are the weak numbers, alongside inventory that rose to ₹3,055.7 Cr.
