हिंदुओं की समस्या यह है कि उन्होंने अपने ग्रंथ नहीं पढे हैं, और वह 2014 के बाद ही हिंदू बने हैं। ना उन्होंने वेद दर्शन उपनिषद रामायण महाभारत पढे हैं। यहां तक की उन्होंने गीता भी नहीं पढी है।
लोग सोचते हैं कि रामायण पूरी तरह वाल्मीकि रामायण पर बनाई जानी चाहिए थी, पर सच कहूं तो हिंदू उसे झेल भी नहीं पाएगा, और डायरेक्टर प्रोड्यूसर को मारने से पहले खुद अपने नाखूनों से अपना सीना फाड़ लेगा।
कुछ लोग अभी बकवास कर रहे हैं कि माता सीता श्री राम को सीधे राम क्यों बोल रही हैं? मैंने कहा न यह लोग 2014 के बाद हिंदू बने हैं। और तब से केवल हिंदू नाम के कारण माइलेज ले रहे हैं। अच्छा वक्त बीता पिछले एक दशक में, बढ़िया होता एक दो धार्मिक पुस्तक पढ़ लेते तो आज उछल-उछल कर हिंदुत्व की बात न करनी पड़ती। पढ़ते रहे हैं रामचरितमानस और सब कुछ चाहिए वाल्मीकि रामायण के हिसाब से!

माता सीता एक दो बार नहीं बल्कि कई बार उनको राम और राघव कह कर बुलाती हैं। अब तुमको यह वोकिज्म लग रहा है। क्योंकि अब तुम हर चीज को अपने ग्रंथ के नहीं बल्कि ट्रोल्स और पश्चिम की नजर से देखने लगे हो। अब हम एक प्राइम हिन्दुत्व में जी रहे हैं जहाँ हम अपने धर्म ग्रंथ की भाषा आदि अपने-अपने पैमाने पर सेट करके ही मानेंगे। उसी से पता लगेगा कि सबसे बड़ा हिंदू कौन है।

कुछ लोग रामानंद सागर को ही वाल्मीकि समझकर कह रहे हैं कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने माता सीता को कभी हाथ में अस्त्र-शस्त्र लेते हुए नहीं दिखाया इसलिए अब जो भी दिखाएगा वह हिंदुत्व विरोधी हो जाएगा। जबकि वह यह भूल जाते हैं की माता सीता एक क्षत्राणी थी और वह धनुर्विद्या तथा तलवार चलाने में महारथी थी। अगर वह भगवान शिव का पिनाक उठाकर रख सकती थी तो क्या वह तलवार नहीं चला सकती थी? लेकिन यहां भी लोगों को हॉलीवुड की नकल पहले दिखने लग जाती है अपने ग्रंथ नहीं।

फिर कुछ लोगों ने आपत्ति जताई कि क्योंकि रामानंद सागर ने तो विवाह स्थल पर ही परशुराम संवाद दिखाया था इसलिए जो यह नहीं दिखाएगा वह भी हिंदू विरोधी होगा जबकि वाल्मीकि रामायण में यह प्रकरण मिथिला में ही परंतु बारात वापसी के मार्ग में बताया गया है।

फिर कुछ लोगों को समस्या हुई की इसमें तो सूर्पनखा का नाक काटते समय फेमिनिज्म को बढ़ावा दिया गया है जबकि रामानंद सागर की रामायण में स्वयं राम लक्ष्मण से कहते हैं कि तुमने अच्छा नहीं किया।

फिर यह बात उठा दी गई कि रावण का महिमा मंडन किया जा रहा है, उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया गया। जबकि रामानंद सागर ने स्वयं हनुमान जी से और श्री राम जी से रावण का महिमा मंडन करवाया था। किसी ने उसे रेपिस्ट नहीं दिखाया हालाँकि वो था। हर चीज दिखाई नहीं जाती, पढी सब जाती हैं। परंतु रामानंद सागर की रामायण देखते समय हमारी आंखों में आंसू आ जाते हैं और हम कहते हैं कि यह हमारा इतिहास है इस पर हमें गर्व है इसने वर्ल्ड रिकॉर्ड बना दिया।

यह किसी फिल्म का प्रमोशन नहीं बल्कि मैं इस पोस्ट के जरिए वाल्मीकि रामायण का प्रमोशन करना चाहता हूं। जितने में आप एक टिकट लेंगे उससे कम पैसे में एक वाल्मीकि रामायण आ जाएगी जो आपके घर में अगले 50 साल तक रहेगी और आपकी पीढ़ियां उसको पढेंगी। लेकिन समस्या यही है कि पढ़ना आसान नहीं होता और हिंदू के लिए तो बिल्कुल भी नहीं, पर फिर भी मैं कहूंगा...

Are Groww (Billionbrains Garage Ventures) and National Stock Exchange (NSE) Technology Companies? Absolutely! Both are technology-driven businesses, although their business models are different.

Groww and NSE represent India's rapidly expanding digital financial infrastructure. Groww, operated by Billionbrains Garage Ventures, is a fintech platform whose core business is built around technology, digital brokerage, mobile applications, cloud infrastructure, data analytics and seamless online investing. Its ability to scale customers without proportionately increasing physical infrastructure is its biggest strength.

Similarly, the National Stock Exchange (NSE) is fundamentally a technology-driven financial market institution. Its business depends on sophisticated trading engines, high-speed order matching, electronic trading platforms, risk-management algorithms, cybersecurity, data centres and massive transaction-processing capabilities.

Neither is a conventional IT services company like TCS or Infosys. However, technology is the backbone of their operations, scalability and competitive advantage.

My view: Both deserve recognition as technology-led financial businesses. India's digital financial revolution will create enormous long-term opportunities for such platforms.

Core EBITDA up 88% to ₹47.17 Cr as Gaming revenue doubles to ₹408.47 Cr

👉 Operating profit grew 88.26% YoY to ₹47.17 Cr as revenue reached ₹410.26 Cr, with operating margin improving 72 bps to 11.50%. The entire top-line expansion came from Gaming and IT services, where sales doubled to ₹408.47 Cr, while employee costs remained modest at 0.4% of revenue compared to 0.3% a year ago.

👉 Cash generation supported the reported numbers during the first half of the year. Operating cash flow stood at ₹107.12 Cr, converting cleanly against net profit of ₹76.82 Cr. Trade receivables dropped by 52% to ₹2.58 Cr, and the company closed the quarter with ₹21.74 Cr in cash and zero net debt.

👉 Behind the headline numbers, structural concentration remains high. Standalone operations in India brought in just ₹4.07 Cr of revenue, meaning over 97% of group profit originates from foreign subsidiaries. Meanwhile, the High Frequency Trading segment shrank 93.7% YoY from ₹28.29 Cr to ₹1.78 Cr, and intangible assets of ₹306.73 Cr make up 71% of total assets.

👉 On the capital front, the company completed a ₹14.83 Cr preferential allotment in late October 2026 as part of a larger ₹73.63 Cr equity raise. The board has also approved enabling resolutions to raise up to ₹1,000 Cr via debentures and expand its Memorandum of Association into data centers, renewable power, and defense technology.

👉 Growth catalyst: The planned rollout of Phase 1 20MW capacity of the 100MW data center targeted for Q4 FY27 could establish a domestic revenue base beyond offshore gaming

👉 Road blocker: Intangible assets and goodwill totaling ₹334.23 Cr represent 77% of group assets as of September 2026, leaving earnings exposed if foreign game intellectual property is impaired

Supriya Lifescience | Q2 FY27 results

Supriya Lifescience profit falls 42% to ₹29.2 Cr as margin drops to 18%

👉 Supriya Lifescience reported standalone revenue from operations of ₹206.3 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 3.3% from ₹199.8 Cr a year earlier and 8.8% from ₹189.7 Cr in the June quarter. Net profit fell 42.1% year on year to ₹29.2 Cr, from ₹50.4 Cr, while profit before tax fell 44.7% to ₹37.8 Cr. Other income was ₹2.3 Cr. Exceptional items were nil.

👉 Operating margin fell to 18.1% from 33.7% a year ago and 21.2% in the June quarter. Cost of materials was ₹92.5 Cr, or 44.8% of revenue, against 30.4% a year earlier and 57.7% in the June quarter. A ₹21.4 Cr rise in stock of finished goods and work-in-progress, against ₹53.0 Cr in Q1, lowered the cost line. Other expenditure rose 35.6% to ₹63.7 Cr and depreciation rose 42.5% to ₹9.5 Cr.

👉 Inventories rose 66% to ₹265.2 Cr from ₹159.6 Cr at March 31, absorbing ₹105.6 Cr of cash, while trade receivables fell to ₹125.6 Cr from ₹219.4 Cr, releasing ₹93.9 Cr. Operating cash flow for the half year was ₹60.9 Cr, against ₹137.5 Cr for all of FY26. Capital spending was ₹35.4 Cr. The company has no borrowings, and cash plus bank balances rose to ₹75.9 Cr from ₹37.5 Cr.

👉 Revenue grew 14.8% in the first half to ₹396.0 Cr, below the 20% annual growth management reaffirmed in June. Reaching the ₹1,000 Cr FY27 revenue target would need ₹604 Cr in the second half, about ₹302 Cr a quarter, against ₹206.3 Cr in Q2. Happy Forgings | Record volumes, a larger capex plan, and a cash-conversion test

Happy Forgings crossed ₹500 crore of quarterly revenue in Q2 FY27. The more useful detail is how it got there: finished-goods volumes rose 24.8% YoY and EBITDA per kg increased to ₹82 from ₹77 a year earlier.

Revenue reached ₹501 crore, up 32.7%. EBITDA grew 32.2% to ₹153 crore and PAT rose 32.8% to ₹98 crore. Realisation increased 6.3%, helped by raw-material pass-through, negotiated conversion-cost recovery and product mix. The growth therefore has a substantial volume component, rather than relying entirely on higher selling prices.

The profit-per-kg improvement deserves attention because EBITDA margin slipped 11 basis points YoY and 76 basis points sequentially to 30.6%. Freight and other cost pressures are absorbing part of the benefit from stronger volumes and price resets. Investors should track both percentage margins and per-unit profitability.

The expansion announcement connects directly to that operating picture. The board approved another ₹500 crore of capex across FY28 and FY29. Management said roughly 70% will go into machining, with the remainder in small forging presses. H1 machining utilisation was 77%, against 60% for forging. Management expects machining utilisation to approach 90% by Q4, explaining why value-added capacity is getting priority.

This new programme is separate from the existing ₹650 crore heavy-component expansion. The latest call adds an important clarification: management described secured data-centre-related orders as approximately ₹300 crore per annum, with a contract running to 2033. That is management's stated annual business visibility, not current revenue or a guarantee of full utilisation.

The conversion timetable still matters. Cold trials are planned for January–February, hot trials for March, followed by sampling. Heavy-component revenue is expected from Q3/Q4 FY28. The August call already set that revenue timetable and expected a meaningful contribution from FY29, so the latest wording should not be mistaken for a fresh revenue delay. Equally, the ₹500 crore order-closure objective for March remains a target, not an achieved order book.

Against previous commitments, execution is encouraging but incomplete. August's high-teen full-year volume-growth guidance is supported by 24% H1 growth. The above-30% margin ambition is holding. However, OEM price revisions have not prevented sequential margin compression, and the solar-power savings remain ahead rather than in reported earnings.

Cash conversion is the main counterweight. H1 operating cash flow fell to about ₹124 crore from ₹217 crore a year earlier, while PAT rose 35.8%. Management cited receivables growth and ₹35 crore of supplier advances and expects normalisation. Gross borrowings and lease liabilities also rose to approximately ₹543 crore from ₹330 crore at March-end. With capex increasing, that cash-flow recovery needs to show up in the accounts.

Kyro view: the current volume growth and improving EBITDA per kg make the execution case more credible. The next proof points are Q3 recognition of North American PV shipments, recovery in cash conversion, and heavy-line trials progressing into customer approvals. The longer-term opportunity is substantial, but the earnings contribution will arrive in stages.

CIL’s Listing-Bound Subsidiaries Log Fall in E-Auction Premiums: MCL’s Average Premium Drops Nearly 66% to ₹274 Per Tonne in FY26 From ₹802 in FY24; Incremental Revenue Falls 60% to ₹728 Crore

Core Theme 
MCL and SECL are heading toward listing with sharply lower e-auction premiums, as MCL’s much larger offering of coal in auctions found far fewer takers, cutting premiums by about two-thirds and incremental revenue by 60%, a trend that weakens a key source of higher realisation ahead of their stock market debut.

The Core Finding: Premiums Collapse
The average e-auction premium realised by Coal India’s two major subsidiaries, Mahanadi Coalfields (MCL) and South Eastern Coalfields (SECL), proposed for stock market listing, has declined by as much as two-thirds over the past two financial years

MCL and SECL are the largest and second-largest subsidiaries of Coal India in terms of coal production

According to MCL’s draft red herring prospectus (DRHP), its average premium over the notified price fell to ₹274 per tonne in FY26 from ₹802 per tonne in FY24, a decline of nearly 66%

Incremental revenue generated through premiums over notified prices also fell 60% to ₹728 crore in FY26 from ₹1,833 crore in FY24

How Coal Is Sold: FSAs vs E-Auctions
MCL and SECL sell coal mainly through two routes: Fuel supply agreements (FSAs) signed with consumers and competitive e-auction windows

Under FSAs, prices are set by Coal India and provide a stable revenue stream to the company

In e-auctions, prices are determined by demand-supply dynamics, and consumers pay premiums over and above notified prices or the benchmark prices at which bidding starts

Companies selling coal through e-auctions earn incremental revenue or “higher realisation” in the form of premiums paid by buyers

MCL: Offered vs Booked Volumes
The decline in premiums came despite a substantial increase in the quantity of coal offered through e-auctions

MCL offered 72.26 million tonnes (mt) in FY26, compared with 28.65 mt in FY24

The quantity booked rose only to 26.49 mt from 22.86 mt over the same period

Consequently, the proportion of coal offered that was booked declined from nearly 80% in FY24 to around 37% in FY26

Rumah tersebut kemudian dikenal sebagai Rumah Pengasingan Cut Nyak Dien.

Masyarakat Sumedang pada masa itu tidak mengetahui bahwa perempuan tua yang tinggal di lingkungan mereka adalah seorang pemimpin perlawanan besar dari Aceh.
Ia lebih dikenal dengan sebutan Ibu Perbu (Ibu Prabu) atau Ibu Ratu.
Dalam pengasingan, Cut Nyak Dien menghabiskan waktunya dengan mengajarkan agama Islam ke penduduk setempat.

Pada 6 November 1908, Cut Nyak Dien wafat di Sumedang.
Ia kemudian dimakamkan di kompleks pemakaman Gunung Puyuh, Sumedang Selatan dan makam ini baru dikenali sebagai makam Cut Nyak Dien di tahun 1959 atas permintaan Gubernur Aceh saat itu, Ali Hasan, yang meminta untuk dilakukan pencarian makam Cut Nyak Dien di Sumedang berdasarkan data Belanda.

Dalam dokumennya, Pemerintah Belanda hanya menyebut ada satu tahanan politik perempuan Aceh yang dikirim ke Sumedang. Sehingga dapat disimpulkan, Ibu Prabu adalah Cut Nyak Dien.

Godrej Agrovet Ltd reports strong Q2 FY27 financial performance with a 17% revenue increase to ₹2,995 Cr, driven by growth in animal nutrition, oil palm, and B2C foods. This growth is significant as it reflects resilience amid challenging operating conditions, highlighting the company's ability to manage input cost inflation while maintaining profitability.

Company Snapshot: 
Godrej Agrovet Ltd operates in the agribusiness sector, focusing on animal nutrition, crop care, and food products. The company reported TTM Revenue of ₹11,844 Cr.

Key Highlights:
Revenue Growth 
- Q2 FY27 revenue increased by 17% YoY to ₹2,995 Cr. 
- H1 FY27 revenue grew by 13% YoY to ₹5,847 Cr. 

Profitability 
- PBT rose by 5% YoY to ₹131 Cr in Q2 FY27. 
- Profit After Tax (PAT) increased by 22% YoY to ₹103 Cr in Q2 FY27. 

Segment Performance 
- Animal nutrition revenue grew by 14% in Q2 FY27, with cattle feed volume up ~8% and layer feed up ~15%. 
- Oil palm revenue surged by 28% in Q2 FY27, driven by higher CPO (+23%) and PKO (+20%) realizations. 
- Crop care revenue rose by 42% YoY, although profitability was impacted by poor demand. 

International Growth 
- ACI-GAVL, the Bangladesh joint venture, reported a 32% revenue increase, supported by a 21% rise in volumes across poultry, cattle, and aqua segments. 

Core Growth Triggers: 
- Plantation Expansion 
- Investing in plantation expansion and commissioning of the Khammam complex, CPKO refinery, and biogas plant. 
- Expected to enhance oil palm revenue through increased production capacity. 

- Premiumization Strategy 
- Exiting the shrimp segment to focus on more profitable and scalable segments in animal nutrition. 
- Aimed at improving margins and market positioning. 

What's Already in the Price: 
The reported revenue growth and profitability metrics align with market expectations, indicating that while the results are strong, they reflect ongoing trends rather than unexpected developments.

Key Risks to Trigger Thesis: 
- Input Cost Inflation 
- Continued inflation may pressure margins, as seen with flat EBITDA despite revenue growth. 
- Crop Care Demand 
- Poor demand for cotton herbicides could further impact profitability in the crop care segment. 

Executive quote: 
"Despite the challenges, our strong performance in animal nutrition and oil palm reflects our strategic focus on premiumization and operational efficiencies." – Vivek Pritamlal Raizada, Managing Director.

The strategic outlook remains positive as Godrej Agrovet continues to leverage its strengths in key segments while navigating market challenges.

Godrej Agrovet Q2 profit rises 21.9% to ₹102.8 Cr, helped by other income

👉 Godrej Agrovet reported consolidated revenue of ₹2,995 Cr for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, up 16.7% from ₹2,567 Cr a year earlier and 4.9% above the June quarter's ₹2,855 Cr. Net profit was ₹102.8 Cr, up 21.9% YoY from ₹84.3 Cr but down 19.9% from ₹128.3 Cr in Q1 FY27. The unaudited results were approved by the board on November 6, 2026, with an unmodified limited review opinion.

👉 Operating profit fell faster than revenue grew. Profit before other income was ₹121.4 Cr, down 4.6% from ₹127.3 Cr, and the operating margin slipped to 4.7% from 5.2% a year earlier and 6.3% in Q1. Other income rose 179.5% to ₹21.8 Cr from ₹7.8 Cr, and that gain lifted pre-tax profit 6.0% to ₹143.2 Cr.

👉 Net profit grew faster than pre-tax profit because tax expense fell. Total tax was ₹40.5 Cr against ₹50.7 Cr in Q2 FY26, made up of current tax of ₹42.1 Cr and a deferred tax credit of ₹1.6 Cr. Profit attributable to owners of the company was ₹115.2 Cr, while the non-controlling interest recorded a loss of ₹12.5 Cr.

👉 Pre-tax growth of 6.0% falls short of the mid-teens PBT growth management guided on the August 5 call. On the August 6 call, management linked weaker crop protection volumes to a dry June that delayed Kharif sowing, and it targeted double-digit revenue growth for FY27. Revenue growth of 16.7% in Q2 sits within that target.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management guided annual capex of ₹300–350 Cr and aims to double its oil palm area to 150,000 hectares, building on the ₹300 Cr Khammam Integrated Oil Palm Complex.

👉 Road blocker: Management pointed to a dry June that delayed Kharif sowing and hurt domestic crop protection volumes, and the Q2 operating margin fell to 4.7%.

Tega Industries | Q2 FY27 results

Revenue soars 949% to ₹4,254 Cr; net loss narrows to ₹58.8 Cr

👉 Tega Industries reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹4,254 Cr for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, up from ₹1,723 Cr in the June quarter and ₹405 Cr a year earlier. The jump reflects the Molycop acquisition, whose step-down subsidiaries have been consolidated from 1 June 2026. Total income was ₹4,295 Cr, with other income of ₹41 Cr.

👉 Operating margin fell to 1.7% in the quarter from 13.9% a year earlier and negative 6.7% in June. Cost of materials consumed rose to ₹2,414 Cr, other expenses to ₹797 Cr, and depreciation to ₹169 Cr. Finance costs reached ₹292 Cr against ₹117 Cr in the previous quarter, and non-current borrowings now stand at ₹11,035 Cr.

👉 Net loss attributable to Tega's owners narrowed to ₹47.5 Cr from ₹86.2 Cr in June; the loss for the period, including minority holders, was ₹58.8 Cr. Pre-tax profit of ₹72.9 Cr was erased by ₹131.7 Cr tax expense. Net operating cash flow for six months was ₹713 Cr, while cash and equivalents fell to ₹716 Cr from ₹1,164 Cr in March after ₹5,816 Cr went on acquisition of a subsidiary.

👉 Trade receivables rose to ₹2,559 Cr from ₹452 Cr and inventories to ₹5,543 Cr from ₹437 Cr between March and September. Goodwill climbed to ₹5,133 Cr from ₹74 Cr. Management's FY27 guidance is 15% consumables growth and 25% equipment growth, but the filing gives no segment split for the quarter, so progress cannot be checked. A ₹126 Cr order win from Kalpataru Projects was reported in September.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management guided 15% consumables growth and 25% equipment growth for FY27, as recorded in the June 2026 earnings call notes.

👉 Road blocker: Operating margin fell to 1.7% from 13.9% a year ago, and finance costs of ₹292 Cr in the quarter are now a major drag on earnings.

Time Technoplast, Q2 & H1 FY27 — record revenue, EBITDA and PAT, but growth quality is the thing to read closely.

Q2: income ₹1,996 Cr, +32.0% YoY. 
EBITDA ₹265 Cr, +18.4%, margin 13.3% vs 14.8%. 
PAT ₹146 Cr, +26.6%. 
Volume +13.8%. 
H1: income ₹3,690 Cr, +28.8%. 
EBITDA ₹490 Cr, +16.9%, margin 13.3% vs 14.6%. 
PAT ₹262 Cr, +24.6%. 
Volume +12.9%.

Thing to focus on,  is Volume growth, not revenue growth

Revenue is growing ~16 points faster than volume. Management says it passes polymer cost through on agreed formulas to hold absolute EBITDA, which lifts revenue but dilutes margin %. 
Still, H1 volume (+12.9%) and EBITDA (+16.9%) both sit slightly below what management guided for FY27 (volume ~15%, EBITDA 19–20% growth). H2 can close the gap since guidance is a full-year number, so this is a watch item, not a miss.

Segments (H1, value): IBC ₹489 Cr (+30.7%), CNG cascades ₹274 Cr (+28.7%), LPG cylinders ₹118 Cr (+8%), packaging ex-IBC ₹2,471 Cr (+28.8%), PE pipes ₹173 Cr (+26.6%).

The balance sheet is clearly positive. Borrowings ₹558 Cr vs cash ₹594 Cr, so the company is now net cash (~₹36 Cr) against net debt of ~₹60 Cr in March. Operating cash flow ₹372 Cr in H1 against capex of ₹174 Cr. ROCE 18%.

Orders and corporate actions: → HPCL: 1,40,000 composite LPG cylinders, ~₹38 Cr → PSU Type-IV CNG cascade order, ~₹83 Cr → NTPC hydrogen cascade trial order, ₹2.5 Cr → Order book: CNG cascades ₹210 Cr, PE pipes ₹195 Cr, plus a ₹375 Cr packaging tender confirmed → Ebullient Packaging acquisition dropped; TPL Plastech merger board-approved, effective 1-Apr-2026 subject to NCLT

Question for the concall: is the margin dip pure input-cost pass-through, or is there pricing pressure?

The 9:15 | 6 November 2026

Morning. The AI trade broke overnight and India opens into the wreckage. GIFT Nifty is quoted around 24,420, down about 167 points, and that is the politest number on any screen today.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4% to 7,353.73, its worst session since April 2025. The Dow dropped 1,833 points. The Nasdaq lost 5.5% and is now roughly 12% below its record close a month ago. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index fell 12.2% in one session. Asia followed hard: Kospi down 8.7% to 4,911 and a circuit breaker tripped, Nikkei down as much as 7%, SK Hynix off 11.7%, Samsung nearly 10%, TSMC 8.5%, SoftBank 11%. Shanghai was off only 1.1% and Hang Seng 0.6%, so this is a memory-and-semis event rather than a general Asia event.

The explanation on offer is the US midterms: Democrats took Congress on 3 November and the market has decided that means tighter AI scrutiny and a slower data-centre build-out. I would hold that loosely. A 12% semiconductor day usually has more positioning in it than politics. US futures were green in the Asian session and the US 10-year is at 4.838%, near its lowest since 9 September.

Now the part that matters more for India than the Nasdaq does. Crude has snapped back. Brent January is around $99.86, up 1.6%, a second straight gain, with WTI at $91.62. Iran said three more tankers were hit in the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, and ANZ reckons flows through the strait are under 60% of capacity. The best macro gift India had this week, Brent settling at a two-month low after an 8% collapse on Wednesday, has been handed back in two sessions. Brent is still down about 12% on the week, but a market that spent Thursday buying paints, airlines and OMCs on $94 crude now has to look at $100 again.

Gold and silver futures are softer, down about 0.93% and 1%, with spot gold near $4,086. Awkward timing, because today is Dhanteras.

Domestically, the new thing is Coal India: subsidiary Mahanadi Coalfields has SEBI clearance for an IPO that is entirely an offer-for-sale of up to 66.18 crore shares. MCL was 28% of Coal India's FY26 coal production, so this is a value-unlock question for the parent, not a listing-day story. ONGC printed standalone PAT of Rs 15,488.6cr, up 57.3%, plus a record Rs 8 interim dividend, all earned on crude that no longer exists at that level. Prestige Estates profit fell 44%.

Three things to watch. Whether the foreign bid holds: FIIs net bought Rs 14,975cr on Thursday, the biggest day of a five-session run, with DIIs selling Rs 10,445cr into it, and a global risk event is the cleanest test that run has faced. Crude at $100 and what it does to the pass-through trade. And IT at the open, with Infosys and TCS the local proxy for a 12% SOX day.

More after the close.

Tega Industries: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

This was the first full quarter including Molycop, which is now most of group revenue. Tega's own business grew 19%, and management said the one-time acquisition costs are now over.

Q2 FY27 Numbers (Consolidated)
Revenue: ₹4,254 Cr
EBITDA before one-time costs: ₹608 Cr, margin 14.2%
Tega legacy business revenue: ₹482.5 Cr (+19% YoY)
Tega legacy EBITDA: ₹93.7 Cr (+11% YoY), margin 18.8%
Molycop revenue: ₹3,771.6 Cr | EBITDA: ₹514.4 Cr, margin 14%

H1 FY27 Numbers
Consolidated revenue: ₹5,977.5 Cr
EBITDA before one-time costs: ₹872 Cr, margin 14.4%
Reported loss: ₹167 Cr | PAT excluding one-time items: ₹45.2 Cr
Tega legacy revenue: ₹914.3 Cr (+20% YoY), EBITDA margin 20.4%

1.  What the combined company does-
Tega makes mill liners, which are linings that protect the inside of the large mills that crush ore at mines, and some mining equipment. Molycop, acquired from 1 June 2026, makes grinding media, the steel balls tumbled inside those mills to crush ore. Both sell to the same copper and gold mines, so the deal combines two products that mines buy repeatedly.

2.  Consumables strong, equipment delayed-
Tega's consumables, mostly mill liners, grew 26% in Q2 and 30% in H1, with margins above 20%. Equipment sales were weak because customers have not yet cleared shipments, though Q2 was 72% higher than Q1. The equipment order book is healthy, and management expects a strong H2. It cut its growth guidance to 15% from 25%.

3.  Molycop steady, big mines recovering-
Molycop's volumes were flat compared with last year and margins held at 14%. Two large customers are still recovering. The Grasberg mine in Indonesia runs at about 67% after a 2025 accident and should reach full capacity by end-2027. Cobre Panama is only processing stockpiled ore until mid-2027. High copper and gold prices are pushing mines to process more ore.

4.  One-time costs now behind-
Acquisition costs of ₹257.6 Cr in H1 pushed the reported result into a loss, though these costs fell sharply in Q2. Management said there will be no more one-time charges from Q3. The tax rate was high because some expenses were not allowed as deductions, and it should come down.

5.  Early signs of cross-selling-
A mine that buys Tega's liners placed a trial order for 500 tonnes of Molycop's grinding media. If it succeeds, this could become 20,000-30,000 tonnes a year. Separately, Tega plans cost savings by setting up a global support centre, moving headquarters to a lower-cost location and cutting overheads. Management expects these to lift Molycop's margin by 100 bps.

6.  Debt reduction is the top priority-
Gross borrowings are about ₹11,500 Cr, of which 96% is long-term. Tega repaid ₹100 Cr in October from a preferential share issue and plans to sell non-core assets over 12-18 months to cut debt. A new Chile plant starts commercial production in March 2027.

Key Guidance
Growth guidance cut to 15% from 25%
Molycop EBITDA margin to rise about 100 bps from cost savings
Long-term group EBITDA margin goal of 17-18%, with no timeline

① Tesla and SpaceX Plunge as Market Values Shrink

November 5 closing prices:

🔴 TSLA: $343.69 (-10.77%), intraday low $338.15.

🔴 SPCX: $123.39 (-9.22%), intraday low $120.39.

Both fell for a second consecutive day. Reuters reported that their combined market value losses this week were estimated to have exceeded $380 billion at one point.

Three major concerns:

• Potential regulatory changes following Democrats’ midterm victories.

• Political uncertainty surrounding Texas AI data centers and the proposed Terafab project.

• Increased scrutiny of a potential Tesla–SpaceX merger.

But the Nasdaq also fell roughly 5.5%. Politics alone cannot explain the selloff.

My take: Investors are reassessing the returns on massive AI capital spending. For Tesla and SpaceX, delivering cash flow matters more than ambitious growth narratives.

② Goldman Sachs Flags Risks to 45% of Planned U.S. Data Center Expansion

Goldman Sachs warns that Democratic victories could encourage additional states to impose temporary moratoriums on new data centers.

Under this scenario, roughly 45% of planned U.S. capacity expansion could face disruption.

For SpaceX’s AI business, the challenge goes beyond GPU prices. Power availability, permits, and deployment timelines determine when computing assets can generate revenue.

Important: 45% represents potential exposure, not confirmed project cancellations.

③ FAA Proposes Major Space Launch Regulatory Reform

On November 5, the FAA proposed simplifying commercial launch and reentry regulations.

The changes address flight-abort requirements, debris-risk assessments, and licensing procedures.

The agency also plans broader licensing reforms in 2027, supporting a national goal of at least 1,000 annual launches and reentries by 2030.

For SpaceX, faster approvals could enable more frequent Starship launches.

The proposed rules are not yet fully in effect.

④ Robotaxi Industry Faces New State-Level Regulatory Uncertainty

The midterm elections have changed the political landscape in several key states.

Tesla’s Cybercab and Waymo’s expansion plans could face changes in autonomous-vehicle safety regulations.

But election results do not automatically mean driverless operations will be restricted.

The key questions: Will incoming state governments change operating permits, safety reporting requirements, or deployment rules?

⑤ Waymo and Lyft Expand Nashville Robotaxi Operations

Lyft plans to expand its Waymo fleet operations in Nashville and develop airport service.

Lyft handles vehicle maintenance, charging, cleaning, and other fleet operations.

An important lesson for Tesla:

Robotaxi competition isn’t just about FSD algorithms. It’s also about fleet utilization, operating costs, charging efficiency, and customer experience.

Ultimately, the companies that deliver reliable autonomous rides at sustainable costs will have the strongest business models.

① Tesla、SpaceX双双暴跌，市值大幅缩水

• 民主党中期选举获胜后，监管环境可能改变。

但纳斯达克当天也下跌约5.5%，不能将全部跌幅归因于政治。

我的判断：市场正在重新评估AI巨额资本开支的回报。对Tesla和SpaceX而言，现金流兑现能力比增长故事更重要。

② 高盛警告：美国45%的规划数据中心扩张可能受到影响

Goldman Sachs分析认为，民主党选举胜利可能推动更多州暂停批准新数据中心。

潜在受影响容量约占美国规划扩张的45%。

对SpaceX旗下AI业务而言，风险不仅是GPU价格，还有电力供应、建设许可及设备投产时间。

注意：45%是风险情景，不是已经停建的比例。

③ FAA提出商业航天监管改革，SpaceX有望受益

11月5日，美国FAA提出简化商业火箭发射和再入审批的规则。

改革涉及飞行中止条件、碎片风险评估及许可程序。

FAA还计划2027年全面改革发射许可制度，以支持2030年每年至少1,000次发射和再入的目标。

对SpaceX而言，审批效率提升可能支持Starship更高频率发射。但新规则尚未全部生效。

④ Robotaxi面临新的州级监管不确定性

美国中期选举改变了部分关键州的政治格局。

Tesla Cybercab与Waymo未来的商业扩张，都可能受到自动驾驶安全监管政策变化的影响。

不过，选举结果不等于无人驾驶禁令。

真正需要关注的是：新一届州政府是否修改无人驾驶许可、安全报告和运营要求。

⑤ Waymo与Lyft扩大Nashville Robotaxi运营

Lyft计划扩大其支持运营的Waymo无人驾驶车队，并推进机场服务。

Lyft负责车辆维护、充电、清洁等运营环节。

这对Tesla是一个提醒：

Robotaxi竞争不仅是FSD算法，还有车队利用率、运营成本、充电效率和用户体验。

未来谁能以更低成本提供可靠的无人驾驶出行服务，谁才更有机会建立可持续的商业模式。

🎙️ Sansera Engineering (SANSERA) earnings call, decoded ⬇️

Sansera Engineering reported a record Q2 FY27, with revenue of ₹10,915 Mn, up 32% YoY, and PAT of ₹1,086 Mn, up 52%. EBITDA grew 48% to a 19.4% margin, against 17.3% a year earlier. Growth was broad: Auto ICE rose 18.2%, tech-agnostic and xEV 27.0%, and aerospace and defence (ADS) 206.5%. Non-auto businesses now make up 20.9% of revenue. Management reiterated FY27 ADS revenue guidance of ₹5,500–6,000 Mn and planned FY27 capex of about ₹8,000 Mn. Against its earlier promises, the quarter met the high-teens to 20% revenue growth and roughly 75–80% ADS growth targets, and exceeded the margin path toward 19%. The Nichidai JV's commercial production has slipped to H2 FY27 from a Q3 start. Management flagged inflationary input costs, geopolitical uncertainty and wage pressures.

Growth triggers
• FY27 ADS revenue guidance of ₹5,500–6,000 Mn.
• Planned FY27 capex of about ₹8,000 Mn.
• Nichidai JV commercial production expected in H2 FY27.

Blockers
• Inflationary input costs, geopolitical uncertainty and wage cost pressures.
• Nichidai JV timeline softened: on stream from Q3 FY27 is now expected in H2 FY27.

Q2 EBITDA margin was 30.6%, down 11 bps YoY and below Q1's 31.3%. Against Q1 promises, volume growth, price pass-through and the 30% margin floor were delivered, though the margin slipped. Management gave no quantified FY27 profit guidance but expects strong full-year profitability. It approved about ₹500 Cr of extra capex, and the ₹650 Cr Dugri heavy-component plant is due in FY28. Raw-material and shipping cost rises may pressure margins temporarily.

Growth triggers
• Dugri heavy-component plant (₹650 Cr) operational in FY28
• About ₹500 Cr extra capex approved, partly debt-funded
• FY27 volume growth to be met or exceeded (no figure given)

Blockers
• Q2 EBITDA margin 30.6%, down 11 bps YoY and below Q1's 31.3%
• Raw-material price rises and geopolitical shipment cost increases may temporarily pressure margins

Sanjivani Paranteral | Q2 FY27 results

Sanjivani Paranteral's Q2 profit rises 156% to ₹4.1 Cr on 63% revenue growth

👉 Sanjivani Paranteral reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹25.3 Cr for Q2 FY27, up 63.2% from ₹15.5 Cr a year earlier and 6.3% from Q1. Net profit rose to ₹4.1 Cr from ₹1.6 Cr, a 156.2% gain, and 64% above the ₹2.5 Cr posted in Q1. Profit before tax was ₹5.5 Cr. Other income was only ₹0.1 Cr, so the gain came from core operations.

👉 Operating margin rose to 21.7% from 14.0% a year earlier and 13.7% in Q1. Material costs were ₹12.1 Cr, against ₹10.7 Cr a year ago, while employee costs rose to ₹2.5 Cr from ₹1.5 Cr. Depreciation climbed to ₹0.7 Cr from ₹0.2 Cr as the Pune plant ramped up.

👉 Half-year operating cash flow was ₹1.3 Cr, against ₹0.1 Cr a year ago, after tax payments of ₹0.8 Cr. Trade receivables rose to ₹17.0 Cr from ₹15.4 Cr at March 31, and other current assets rose to ₹9.5 Cr from ₹5.1 Cr. Total borrowings stood at about ₹16.4 Cr, up from ₹14.3 Cr. Capex in the half was ₹1.7 Cr, down from ₹6.0 Cr a year earlier.

👉 Half-year revenue of ₹49.2 Cr is about a third of the ₹140-150 Cr FY27 guidance management gave in August, which combines ₹80-85 Cr from the base business and ₹60-65 Cr from the Pune IV-fluid plant. Finance costs rose to ₹0.4 Cr from ₹0.05 Cr. The filing's split of profit between owners and non-controlling interest does not add up to the total, so this report uses the net profit line.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management's FY27 guidance of ₹60-65 Cr from the Pune IV-fluid plant, with a 17-18% EBITDA margin target for the IVF business, is the next test.

👉 Road blocker: Half-year operating cash flow of ₹1.3 Cr is small against ₹6.6 Cr of net profit, as receivables rose ₹1.6 Cr.

TEGA INDUSTRIES – Q2 FY27: Looking Beyond the Molycop Acquisition
Tega has reported its first full quarter of Molycop consolidation. While the acquisition has significantly expanded the company's scale, it is important to understand how both businesses are performing independently.

1. Legacy Tega business
- Revenue grew 18% YoY to Rs 498.5 Cr.
- Adjusted EBITDA grew only 10% to Rs 93.7 Cr.
- EBITDA margin stood at 18.8%, indicating some margin contraction.
- Adjusted PAT declined 65% YoY to Rs 15.8 Cr.
- Order book remained healthy at Rs 1,397.6 Cr, up 21% YoY.

The concern here is that EBITDA growth is lagging revenue growth, indicating pressure on operating margins. The sharp decline in PAT is another area that needs attention.

While the order book provides good revenue visibility, I would like to see improvement in operating leverage and profitability in the coming quarters.

2. Molycop's Grinding Media business reported:
- Revenue of approximately Rs 3,771.6 Cr.
- Segment EBIT of Rs 478 Cr.
- EBIT margin of 12.7%.

Molycop brings enormous scale, but its current margin profile is dilutive to the overall group's profitability.

The opportunity lies in improving margins through operational efficiencies, cost optimisation and the targeted USD 20 million synergies over the next 2–2.5 years.

This will be an important parameter to track as integration progresses.

3. Consolidated performance
The combined entity reported:

Revenue from operations of Rs 4,254 Cr.
Adjusted EBITDA of Rs 608.1 Cr.
Reported PAT loss of Rs 58.8 Cr.

The enlarged business is generating substantial operating EBITDA, but high interest costs, depreciation and acquisition-related expenses are weighing on reported profitability.

The challenge now is to convert the significantly larger revenue base into sustainable earnings and cash flows.

 here are three things I would closely monitor:
- Whether legacy Tega can arrest its EBITDA margin decline and deliver better earnings growth.
- Whether Molycop can improve its operating margins through synergies and efficiencies.
- Whether the combined business can generate sufficient free cash flow to reduce acquisition-related debt.

The acquisition has delivered scale, but the earnings story is still evolving.

Interestingly, even the legacy Tega business needs to demonstrate better operating leverage, as revenue growth is currently not translating proportionately into EBITDA growth.

Molycop brings a massive global footprint and a complementary business, but its lower margin profile means there is meaningful work to be done on profitability.

the next few quarters will be crucial in determining whether the enlarged business can convert its scale into better margins, earnings and free cash flow.

In short, the strategic thesis is intact, but execution on profitability and deleveraging remains the key monitorable.

Lumino Industries Ltd - Q2/H1FY27 | Concall Insights

Performance 
•Q2 revenue ₹661 cr (+30% YoY); EBITDA ₹84 cr (margin 12.8%); PAT ₹53 cr (margin 7.9%) 
•H1 revenue ₹1,183 cr (+25% YoY); EBITDA ₹155 cr (margin 13.1%); PAT ₹93 cr (margin 7.8%) 
•H1 operating cash flow positive at ₹56 cr (would have been ~₹125 cr excluding IPO-related trade payable repayment of ~₹68 cr)
•Working capital days improved (group ~66 days from 73; manufacturing ~46 days from 50; EPC ~111 days from 120) 
•Nearly all >6-month debtors as of March realized; WB Electricity Board outstanding reduced to ~₹2 cr (from ~₹140 cr)

Order Book & Mix 
•Order book as of 30 Sep: ₹2,885 cr (manufacturing ₹922 cr + EPC ₹1,963 cr)
•October additions ₹386 cr (manufacturing ₹229 cr + EPC ₹157 cr); total ~₹3,093 cr; plus L1 tenders ~₹555 cr 
•Manufacturing contribution targeted at minimum ~70% of revenue (currently ~70% products / 30% EPC); management focused on reducing relative EPC exposure 
•H1 manufacturing revenue ~₹831 cr (conductors ~65%; cables ~35%); HTLS ~₹50 cr in H1 
•Manufacturing order cycle ~3–6 months; EPC ~3 years — explains revenue mix despite larger EPC book

Capacity & Manufacturing 
•Current capacity: 40,000 MT (Howrah, two facilities); utilization effectively high on value-added mix (AL59/HTLS consume more capacity) 
•New facility at Ranihati (Howrah): +35,000 MT in phases (to total 75,000 MT); Phase 1 +10,000 MT; commercial production of medium-voltage cables (3.3–33 kV) expected Dec 2026/Jan 2027 
•Already has ~₹50–55 cr order book for 11/33 kV cables ahead of start 
•Higher-voltage cables expected to support 1–2% higher EBITDA vs standard; blended manufacturing EBITDA guided 12–13.5%
•Volume growth primarily from new capacity; FY26 utilization ~82–83%; H1 effective utilization high despite lower tonnage due to mix shift to value-added products

Outlook & Priorities 
•Industry tailwinds from renewable capacity addition, Green Corridor Phase III, Gati Shakti, grid modernization, HTLS for capacity enhancement without new RoW, data centres, railway electrification 
•Focus areas: timely execution of order book; expand specialized products (HTLS, higher-voltage cables); efficient utilization of new capacity; working capital/cash flow discipline; selective growth 
•New capacity ramp: expect ~70–75% utilization of Phase 1 (10,000 MT) in next financial year; progressive addition thereafter 
•Exports to 17 countries; US certification obtained for US/Europe markets 
•IPO proceeds used for debt reduction, strengthening balance sheet and freeing internal accruals for growth 
•Management positions company primarily as a product manufacturer (conductors/cables) with complementary EPC capabilities
•Overall, solid revenue growth and improving cash flows supported by a robust order book, with capacity expansion into higher-value medium-voltage cables and specialized conductors providing multi-year visibility on volume growth, product mix improvement, and sustained margins in a favorable power transmission and renewable-driven demand environment.

Two major policy decisions by the Modi government could create significant opportunities across India's energy storage, battery manufacturing and critical minerals ecosystem. And the combined investment opportunity is worth watching closely.

1. ₹14,500 crore push for energy storage: The Cabinet has approved a Viability Gap Funding (VGF) scheme to develop 92 GWh of grid-scale energy storage capacity by FY31, attracting an estimated ₹97,600 crore in investments. 

The capacity includes 60 GWh of pumped hydro storage, 30 GWh of BESSand 2 GWh of emerging storage technologies. 

Importantly, BESS projects will have a minimum 40% domestic content requirement. Potential beneficiaries include battery manufacturers such as Exide Industries and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility, renewable energy and storage developers such as Tata Power, NTPC, JSW Energy, Adani Green Energy and NHPC, and power equipment companies such as BHEL, CG Power and Hitachi Energy India. The opportunity also extends to solar manufacturers such as Waaree Energies and Premier Energies as renewable energy increasingly needs storage solutions.

2. ₹2,814 crore push for critical mineral processing: The government has approved a five-year capital support scheme to establish four processing plants - two for lithium and two for nickel. It will provide a 30% capital subsidy, with support capped at ₹500 crore per lithium beneficiary and ₹900 crore per nickel beneficiary. Cobalt will also be recovered as a by-product of nickel processing. This could create opportunities across the lithium-ion battery supply chain, speciality chemicals, mineral processing, battery recycling and EV manufacturing. Companies worth tracking include Tata Chemicals, Neogen Chemicals, Gravita India, Hindustan Zinc and Hindustan Copper.

Sejal Glass | Q2 FY27 Concall Updatrs:

Sejal is entering its next growth phase, driven by capacity utilisation, UAE order visibility and a shift towards higher-value glass products.

1/ Q2FY27 
• Revenue: 139.9 Cr (+33% YoY)
• EBITDA: 25.7 Cr (+43%)
• EBITDA margin: 18.35% (+132 bps)
• PAT: 14.4 Cr (+78%)

2/ FY27 Guidance🎯
Mgmt reiterated:
• Revenue growth: 25–40%
• EBITDA margin: ~18%
• PAT margin: ~10%

3/ Capacity utilisation – Operating leverage ahead💡
Taloja:
• Tempering utilisation: 69% vs 55%
• IG glass: 40% vs 24%
Erode:
• Tempering: Above 24% vs 13%
• IG glass: Above 18% vs below 5%
Erode has turned EBITDA positive (~10% margin), while Taloja is around break-even.

4/ Revenue potential
Mgmt sees 600–650 Cr revenue potential from existing infrastructure by FY28. Higher utilisation across existing plants is the key driver.💡

5/ UAE – Strong visibility
• Order book: AED 78 Mn (~200 Cr)
• Execution visibility: 6–9 months
• UAE IG capacity utilisation: ~90%
• Five major orders worth AED 27.6 Mn secured in July.

6/ India – Next growth opportunity
• Domestic order book: ~85 Cr
• Execution cycle: 6–8 months
• Focus on larger residential, commercial and infrastructure projects.
• Target revenue mix: UAE 60% / India 40%.

7/ Specialised products – Key FY28 trigger💡
Mgmtt targets value-added products contributing:
• FY27: ~5% of revenue
• FY28: 15–20%
Products include fire-rated, bullet-resistant, digital printed and railway-grade glass.
Fire-rated glass commercial production targeted for Q4 FY27. 

Management indicated EBITDA margins above 30% for this product.💡

8/ New growth opportunities
• Railway-grade glass: Approved vendor at 3 coach factories; tender conversion currently below 5%.
• Fire-rated glass: Indicative India + UAE market opportunity above ₹500 Cr.
• UAE expansion: Third tempering line and fire-rated facilities; ~AED 20 Mn capex, funded 60% through internal accruals and 40% bank finance.

9/ What to monitor
• Taloja turnaround and Erode utilisation.
• Sustaining 18% EBITDA margins.
• Commercial ramp-up of specialised products.
• Working capital and cash-flow conversion.
• Execution of the UAE order book.

Overall crux: Sejal's next growth leg is not merely about adding capacity. It is about sweating existing assets, scaling India operations and moving towards higher-margin specialised glass.
FY28 could be an important year if mgmt delivers on its utilisation and product-mix targets. Execution and cash-flow conversion remain the key monitorables.

What makes "Samhi Hotels" a serious investment case?

👉For context: FY26 revenue was rupees 1248 Crore.

Samhi Hotels (SAMHI) has a secured development pipeline of roughly 1,669-1,700 rooms (on top of ~4,899 operational rooms as of FY26), which is expected to expand the portfolio toward ~6,500–6,600 rooms by FY31.

👉This pipeline, focused heavily on the upscale/upper-upscale segment, is a core driver of management’s outlook for revenue potential rising from ~₹1,280 crore in FY26 toward ~₹2,300 crore from new inventory alone, and ~₹3,000 crore overall over the next four years when combined with same-store growth.

➡️ Breakdown of pipeline

~1,669–1,700 new rooms across ~7 major hotels/projects, with the majority in upscale/upper-upscale.

👉✅️This is expected to lift the share of upscale inventory from ~41% to ~60% by FY2030.

▶️Notable projects:

1. W Hotel, HITEC City, Hyderabad (~170 rooms, upper upscale): Targeted to open around Q2 FY28 (stabilized year FY29); conversion of an existing office building under a long-term variable lease.

2. Westin + Tribute Portfolio, Whitefield, Bengaluru: Dual-branded expansion/rebranding (opening targeted around FY29-FY30).

3. Navi Mumbai dual-branded project (~700 rooms total under Westin upper-upscale and Fairfield by Marriott upper mid-scale, in phases starting with ~400): 👉Largest project by room count; near Navi Mumbai International Airport and DY Patil Stadium.

Construction progressing after MIDC timeline extension; major contribution expected later in the pipeline (around FY31).

4. Noida (~162-room upper-upscale hotel) with Ingka Centres (IKEA Group affiliate): capital-efficient variable lease model (Ingka builds structure; Samhi handles fit-outs); opening targeted FY30.

5. Marriott-branded hotel in Sriperumbudur/Chennai area (~135 rooms), 
additional Hyderabad Financial District mid-scale (~260 rooms under variable lease), 
expansions/rebrandings (including ~473 rooms being converted/upgraded).

👉Limited contribution in the near term (e.g., some openings/impact from FY27-FY28 onward), ramping meaningfully from FY28/FY29 with larger additions in later years (including the bulk of Navi Mumbai).

👉Capex for the pipeline is estimated around ₹2,200 crore, to be funded largely from internal free cash flows.​

➡️ How the pipeline augments growth
Revenue expansion: 

👉Pipeline alone is expected to add ~₹1,000 crore to annual revenue.

👉Combined with same-store growth guidance of 9-11% annually (recently running stronger, e.g., 12.6% same-store revenue and 14.3% RevPAR growth in Q2 FY27), this supports overall revenue opportunity of ~₹3,000 crore over ~4 years & path toward high-teens (or potentially early-20s) revenue growth once new inventory ramps. 

👉New hotels begin contributing more visibly from FY28.​

➡️ Mix shift and margins: 

Higher-ADR upscale inventory drives revenue per key and supports operating EBITDA margins moving toward ~40% as the mix improves.

➡️ Cash flow and balance sheet strength: 

👉Management targets >₹3,000 crore cumulative free cash flow over FY27-FY31. 

This is intended to fund the pipeline with limited additional debt.

Recent GIC partnership (35% stake in an upscale platform) has already helped cut debt and lower interest costs.

➡️ Complementary asset-light growth: 

The RARE India platform (~70-75 hotels / ~1,000+ rooms in experiential/leisure) adds high-margin fee income (meaningful contribution expected from FY28 onward, with Marriott distribution partnership enhancing reach). This diversifies into leisure without heavy capital intensity.

Overall, the pipeline provides visible, multi-year visibility on room additions concentrated in high-demand commercial corridors (Hyderabad, Bengaluru, NCR, Mumbai region, Chennai). 

👉Execution risks (construction timelines, absorption of new supply, macro/demand factors) exist, but management has repeatedly described the pipeline as on track and a key foundation for the next phase of growth.

✅️• RevPAR: +14.3% YoY (to ~₹5,746), led by ARR growth of +9.2%.

✅️• Same-store revenue growth: +12.6% YoY (ahead of the company’s long-term guidance of 9-11%).

👉• Domestic travellers accounted for ~80% of room nights sold (resilient amid geopolitical headwinds).

• Flow-through of incremental EBITDA to incremental revenue ~57%.⁠

👉Balance Sheet & Cash Flow

• Free Cash Flow: ~₹82.7 Cr.
• Net Debt / EBITDA: ~3.1x overall (~2.2x on operating assets).
• Effective interest rate: 7.8% (~300 bps lower since IPO).

➡️ Strong underlying operations: 

Same-store performance beat the company’s own long-term guidance, reflecting resilient domestic demand (80% of room nights). This drove good operating leverage ..... pre-exceptional PBT rose nearly 40% on ~15% revenue growth.

Comparable EBITDA (excluding GST input tax credit impact of ~₹10.3 Cr that was not in the prior-year base) grew over 21%.⁠

👉Why reported PAT fell ~59%: 

Last year’s Q2FY26 PAT was inflated by a large exceptional gain of ~₹84.1 Cr (sale of a business undertaking + reversal of right-of-use asset impairment). 

This quarter had only a modest exceptional gain of ~₹3.9 Cr (from a land-parcel sale). 

Stripping out exceptionals, adjusted PAT grew strongly (~138% YoY). 

Reported EBITDA margin looked slightly softer mainly due to the GST regulation change impact (~300 bps dilution); on a comparable basis, margins held up well or improved sequentially.⁠

👉Other context: 

The company continues to build its pipeline (including the upcoming W Hotel in Hyderabad and other additions) and released its first Sustainability Report. 

Management has guided for same-store revenue growth of 9-11% in FY27 and aims to bring net debt/EBITDA toward 2.5x by FY28.

SAMHI Hotels: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Same-store growth beat the long-term guidance again. The GST drag on margins ends from next quarter, and the W Hyderabad opening is now close.

Q2 FY27 Numbers
Total income: ₹342.7 Cr (+15.6% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹123.8 Cr (+12% YoY), margin 36.1%
EBITDA excluding GST impact: ₹133.8 Cr (+21.3% YoY), margin 39.1%
Profit before tax and one-offs: ₹53.4 Cr (+39.9% YoY)
PAT: ₹41.1 Cr (last year's base had ₹84.1 Cr of one-time gains)
Occupancy: 78.6% (vs 75%) | Same-store RevPAR: +14%

H1 FY27 Numbers
Profit before tax and one-offs: ₹86.2 Cr (+35.4% YoY)
PAT: ₹66 Cr

1.  Hotels are filling up and gaining pricing power-
RevPAR (Revenue Per Available Room) is room revenue divided by all rooms, so it rises when either room rates or occupancy go up. On 37% of nights the hotels were above 90% full, up from 32% a year ago, and full nights allow higher pricing. About 80% of guests were domestic. Bangalore and Hyderabad together absorbed 7.9 million sq ft of new office space this quarter, which feeds hotel demand. Hyderabad RevPAR grew 19.1%, Pune 17.2% and Bangalore 8% on a high base.

2.  GST drag ends from next quarter-
Changes in GST rules took away input tax credit, costing about ₹10 Cr a quarter. Last year's base absorbs this impact from Q3, so management expects reported EBITDA growth in the high teens from here. The GST Council has suggested limited relief for hotels charging below ₹7,500 a night, but the final notification is awaited.

3.  Moving upmarket with W Hyderabad-
The 170-room W hotel in Hyderabad's Hitec City should be built by the end of FY27. Opening is planned for Q2 FY28, with a buffer for fire and other approvals. Once it stabilises in FY29, it could add over 10% to the FY27 revenue base. Upscale hotels earned EBITDA margins about 800 bps higher than the rest of the portfolio in the last six months. Their share of income should rise from 42% to about 60% by FY30.

4.  New hotels funded from internal cash-
The secured pipeline adds about 1,670 rooms and upgrades 473 more. Key projects are the Westin and Tribute in Bangalore (370 rooms), a 162-room hotel in Noida, a 134-room Marriott in Sriperumbudur and 658 rooms in Navi Mumbai. Capex of about ₹2,250 Cr over FY27-31 is planned from internal cash, with net debt staying around current levels.

5.  RARE India, a low-capital fee business-
RARE India's boutique hotels go live on Marriott Bonvoy's Outdoor Collection in December, and SAMHI earns about an 18% commission on bookings. Management expects ₹15-20 Cr of revenue from this in FY28 with almost no capex. The platform has about 70 hotels now and should reach 85-90.

6.  Debt steady, more profit to come-
Net debt is ₹1,458 Cr, or 3.1 times trailing EBITDA (2.2 times after adjusting for money tied up in hotels under construction). Two small hotels worth ₹200-230 Cr may be sold to recycle capital. About ₹100 Cr of deferred tax asset is expected to be recognised in Q4. This is a book entry for past losses that can now be set off against future taxable profit, and it will boost reported PAT.

Key Guidance
Same-store revenue growth of 9-11% over the long term
RevPAR growth of about 14-15% in H2
Net debt to EBITDA of 2.5 times in about 18 months

H1 Revenue Grew 25% to ₹272 Cr, Sharon AI’s 8,200-GPU Sydney Project Set to Go Live in Dec with ₹288 Cr Monthly Billing Potential;  ₹1,500 Cr India AI Factory Targeting ₹1,000 Cr Annual Revenue

1.  Financials (Consolidated)

Q2 revenue ₹138.3 Cr (₹133.7 Cr in Q1; +3.5%)
H1 revenue ₹271.9 Cr (+24.6% from ₹218.4 Cr)
H1 total revenue ₹278.8 Cr, including ₹6.8 Cr other income
H1 EBITDA ₹113.8 Cr (+12.3% from ₹101.3 Cr)
H1 PAT ~₹60.4 Cr (+26.3% from ₹47.8 Cr)

2.  Business Performance

Three segments: infrastructure as a service, managed services, software
AI factory and GPU infrastructure is the new growth driver
Cloud revenue -9% QoQ; infrastructure -4% (analyst figures)
Customers cut from 2,216 to 1,709
Small accounts moved to a virtual subsidiary with profit targets

50-60 customers asked to leave
Focus on top 400-500 customers; may narrow to 250-300
No international design revenue in Q2
CTO and CIO roles redundant; CTO resigned
Chief product officer joined two months ago; chief AI officer in place

3.  Order Book & Demand

India pipeline ~₹3,000 Cr, mostly AI infrastructure
Demand from defence PSUs, government, enterprises and banks
Managed services and software funnel weaker
International pipeline ~50,000 GPUs
Talks with US, South Korean, Taiwanese partners; MOU with Swedish partner
Signing an MSA takes ~2 months

Customers: ~17-18 top AI labs
DPDP law next year may push users off foreign clouds
Domestic cloud and colocation opportunity ~₹3,000 Cr
No major contract or advance in Q2

4.  Capacity & Capex

Sharon AI: 8,200 B300 GPUs, 16 MW, Sydney
Nvidia cluster testing done; handover by 27 November
Then 20 days of customer testing
Ready for service between first week of December and 17 December
Q3 books one month of revenue and profit; Q4 books three

India AI factory: ~₹1,500 Cr capex from IPO and customer advances
1,150-1,200 GPUs; live June-July 2027
Targets ~₹1,000 Cr annual revenue
More GPUs by August-September 2027
Existing data centres ~85% used
Three data centres adding capacity in 2-3 months
Buying powered land (50-100 MW); aims for 1 GW of power

5.  Balance Sheet & Cash Flow

IPO ₹720 Cr raised; ₹46.9 Cr used
~₹650 Cr held in fixed deposits
$140 mn advance paid to Sharon AI
Half amortised over 3 months from go-live; half in months 34-36
Customer advance mirrors the same amount

6.  Margins & Costs

Sharon AI project PAT margin 16-18%
Domestic business PAT margin 26-27%
Rates fixed for 5 years; no gain from higher GPU prices
At current prices PAT could be ~₹150 Cr a month
Future India AI factories can charge higher prices

7.  Guidance & Outlook

No formal guidance
Sharon billing ~₹288 Cr a month once fully live
Quoted monthly PAT ₹50-60 Cr from the project
Payout to Sharon ~₹3,000 Cr a year
Contract of $1,250 mn: 5-year commitment, rate locked 7 years
Take-or-pay with the end customer; dedicated cluster
Domestic revenue (~₹500 Cr) to triple or quadruple in 1-2 years
More AI factories planned quarter on quarter

8.  Key Risks

Sharon AI delivery delay
Prices locked while GPU rates rise
Core cloud and customer decline
Leadership changes
Slow contract signing for new deals

*Sammaan Capital Ltd Initiating Coverage | Rating: BUY*
*Mcap: INR 149.79 bn | CMP: INR 120 | TP: INR 360 | Upside: +200%*

*_Reset done, re-rating ahead_*

*Please find the complete report:*
https://t.co/Jf0ZTYDxbx

*Valuation & View:* We initiate coverage on Sammaan Capital with a BUY rating and a target price of INR 360. Sammaan is a mortgage-led NBFC in the RBI's upper layer, now controlled by Abu Dhabi's IHC, that is turning multi-product after a completed balance-sheet clean-up. The FY26 reset took GNPA and NNPA to nil, and IHC's backing has already lifted the company to AA+ at all three domestic rating agencies. We expect RoE to build from 7.5% in FY27E to about 16% by FY30E. The drivers are a falling cost of funds as the liability side re-rates, monetisation of the legacy pool, new high-yield products (gold, personal loans, micro-LAP) and operating leverage from the branch build-out. We expect PAT to compound at about 44% over FY27E to FY30E. At a CMP of INR 120, the stock trades at about 0.67x FY29E ABV of INR 179 and 14% below IHC's INR 139 entry price, a level we believe gives little credit to the recovery already underway. *We value Sammaan at 2.0x FY29E ABV, a plan-delivery multiple with a 24 to 30 month horizon, to arrive at a target price of INR 360, implying upside of about 200% (12-month discounted value INR 296).*

*Arihant Capital Markets Ltd*

𝗢𝗻𝗘𝗠𝗜 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗦𝗼𝗹𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗟𝘁𝗱: 𝗤2 𝗙𝗬27 𝗘𝗮𝗿𝗻𝗶𝗻𝗴𝘀 𝗖𝗮𝗹𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀 🚀:

OnEMI Technology Solutions Ltd (Kissht) delivered a robust performance in Q2 FY27, marked by significant growth in Assets Under Management (AUM) and Profit After Tax (PAT), alongside strategic shifts towards higher-quality customers and improved operational efficiencies.

𝗙𝗶𝗻𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗛𝗶𝗴𝗵𝗹𝗶𝗴𝗵𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗣𝗔𝗧 𝗗𝗼𝘂𝗯𝗹𝗲𝘀 𝗬𝗼𝗬: Profit After Tax surged to ₹125 Cr, a 100% increase compared to the previous year, and up 31.6% QoQ.
- 𝗔𝗨𝗠 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: AUM reached ₹9,317 Cr, demonstrating a strong YoY growth of 68.4% and 16.4% QoQ.
- 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿 𝗕𝗮𝘀𝗲 𝗘𝘅𝗽𝗮𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻: Served 12.8 million customers (up 22.5% YoY), with active customers growing 58% YoY to 3.61 million.
- 𝗥𝗲𝘃𝗲𝗻𝘂𝗲 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: Total income stood at ₹740 Cr, up 43% YoY.
- 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗠𝗲𝘁𝗿𝗶𝗰𝘀: Return on average AUM improved to 5.78%, and Return on Average Equity was 21.65%.

𝗦𝘁𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗰 𝗙𝗼𝗰𝘂𝘀 & 𝗢𝗽𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹 𝗘𝗳𝗳𝗶𝗰𝗶𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆:

- 𝗦𝗵𝗶𝗳𝘁 𝘁𝗼 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗖𝘂𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗺𝗲𝗿𝘀: The company is deliberately focusing on less leveraged customers with higher credit scores, leading to increased average ticket size (now ₹43,380) and longer average tenure (17.8 months).
- 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗼𝗳 𝗕𝗼𝗿𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: The average cost of borrowing decreased by approximately 70 basis points to 13.76%, with further reductions expected due to improved credit ratings.
- 𝗧𝗲𝗰𝗵𝗻𝗼𝗹𝗼𝗴𝘆 𝗜𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗴𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: AI and machine learning are core to operations, enhancing underwriting (AUC improved to 75%), fraud detection, and collections (voice agents recovering 85% of human caller rates).
- 𝗟𝗔𝗣 𝗕𝘂𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗲𝘀𝘀 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗳𝗶𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗶𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆: The Loan Against Property (LAP) business turned profitable in Q2 FY27, ahead of guidance.

𝗔𝘀𝘀𝗲𝘁 𝗤𝘂𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘁𝘆 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗲𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁:

- 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝗲𝗱 𝗖𝗿𝗲𝗱𝗶𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁𝘀: Credit costs fell to 6.2% of average AUM from 9.3% a year ago.
- 𝗟𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗡𝗣𝗔𝘀: Gross NPA improved to 2.18%, and Net NPA stood at 0.34%.
- 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲-2 & 𝗦𝘁𝗮𝗴𝗲-3: Stage-2 assets reduced to 2.37%, and Stage-3 coverage remains strong at 84.6%.

𝗙𝘂𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗲 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗮𝗻𝗰𝗲:

- 𝗙𝗬27 𝗔𝗨𝗠 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵: Raised guidance from 40%+ to 60%+.
- 𝗜𝗺𝗽𝗮𝗶𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗖𝗼𝘀𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗱𝘂𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻: Target for impairment cost reduction increased to 𝗺𝗼𝗿𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗮𝗻 15% YoY.
- 𝗥𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗿𝗻 𝗼𝗻 𝗘𝗾𝘂𝗶𝘁𝘆: Target remains above 20%.
- 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗡𝗣𝗔: Target remains below 2.25%.

𝗡𝗼𝘁𝗮𝗯𝗹𝗲 𝗤&𝗔 𝗣𝗼𝗶𝗻𝘁𝘀:

- 𝗔𝗨𝗠 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝘁𝗵 𝗗𝗿𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀: Deepening existing customer relationships, increased ticket size for repeat customers, & focus on high-quality borrowers.
- 𝗥𝗢𝗘 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗳𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲: Driven by falling cost of funds, operating leverage, & declining risk costs.
- 𝗧𝗮𝘅 𝗥𝗮𝘁𝗲: Reduction due to ESOP-related tax benefits.
- 𝗟𝗔𝗣 𝗦𝗰𝗮𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴: Expected to grow 15-20% QoQ, with branches showing improved profitability.
- 𝗢𝗿𝗴𝗮𝗻𝗶𝗰 𝗦𝗼𝘂𝗿𝗰𝗶𝗻𝗴: Remains stable at ~30-30.5%.
- 𝗔𝘃𝗲𝗿𝗮𝗴𝗲 𝗧𝗶𝗰𝗸𝗲𝘁 𝗦𝗶𝘇𝗲 𝗖𝗲𝗶𝗹𝗶𝗻𝗴: Currently capped at ₹3 Lakhs, with current average at ₹43,380. Expects incremental upward trend.
- 𝗙𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗿𝗮𝗶𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴: No further fundraising envisaged until AUM reaches ₹30,000 Cr; recent preferential allotment proceeds to be used for balance sheet infusion & AI investments.

The company's disciplined underwriting, prudent funding, & focus on technology-driven risk management position it well for sustained growth.

Wendt India Q2 FY27

Wendt India makes superabrasives: grinding wheels faced with diamond or cubic boron nitride, used to shape metals and ceramics too hard for ordinary abrasives. Diamond is the hardest natural material, so the main way to cut one finished part to a thousandth of a millimetre is with another diamond. The company also builds the grinding machines that spin these wheels, and grinds precision parts itself. It is based in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, with arms in Thailand and Germany.

SAMHI Hotels concall. One simple sum explains the whole story.

For two years, 98% of SAMHI’s revenue has been same-store. No new hotel opened. The company grew 12 to 15% a quarter purely by filling the same rooms at higher rates. Management guides 9 to 11% for that engine and has delivered 10.4% over three years.

Now layer the next bit. W Hyderabad opens in Q2 FY28. At full capacity it should do about ₹170 cr a year, roughly 6 to 7% on top of SAMHI’s revenue base by then.

So the old hotels give you 10%. The new one gives you another 6 to 7%. Put together, SAMHI goes from a 10% growth company to a 16 to 17% one, before RARE adds its first ₹15 to 20 cr of fee income 📈

Then a new hotel every six quarters or so till FY31. Sheraton Hyderabad rooms, Westin Bangalore, the IKEA Noida hotel, Sriperumbudur, Navi Mumbai. The CEO’s words: back to high teens, if not early 20s, which is what this company compounded at from FY12 to FY26.

And the part I care about most as a shareholder: net debt stays at ₹1,450 to 1,500 cr through all of it. ₹2,250 cr of capex funded from cash. Below 3x by March, 2.5x in 18 months. No equity, no stress 🏦

The GST adjustment that has muddied every print for four quarters drops out from Q3. Reported EBITDA growth goes back to high teens on its own.

Execution is the risk, not demand. Fire approvals on W have a cushion built in. Navi Mumbai is a FY31 story. But the growth that was a promise at IPO now has dates on it.

Stay not out

Samhi Hotels reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹338.1 Cr, up 15.4% YoY, with total income up 15.6% to ₹342.7 Cr. Same-store revenue grew 12.6%, above the 9–11% band management had set. The growth was mainly price-led: average rate rose 9% while occupancy gained 3.6 points to 78.6%, and the upscale segment outperformed the broader portfolio by 800 basis points. Reported net profit fell 58.8% to ₹41.1 Cr. Management said profit rose significantly once prior-year one-offs are excluded. Management reiterated a 2.5x net debt/EBITDA target and 60% upscale income by FY30, but the leverage target moved from FY27 to FY28. W Hyderabad is due to open in Q2 FY28.

Growth triggers
• W Hyderabad opening in Q2 FY28
• Net debt/EBITDA of 2.5x, now targeted for FY28 (previously FY27)
• 60% of income from upscale and upper-upscale hotels by FY30

Blockers
• Leverage target slipped from FY27 to FY28 after an analyst's question
• GST changes affect comparable EBITDA, and ₹2,400 Cr of capex through FY31 leaves the balance sheet exposed to rate volatility

Atlanta Electricals – Q2 & H1 FY27 Concall Updates

Q2 FY27: 
Revenue 390.1 Cr (+23.1% YoY), 
EBITDA 59.6 Cr (+8.8%), 
PAT 32.1 Cr (+28%).  

H1 FY27: 
Revenue 856.4 Cr (+35.5%), 
EBITDA 136.7 Cr (+32%), 
PAT 79 Cr (+40.4%).

Q2 margins pressured by higher copper, steel & transformer oil prices + legacy firm-price contracts. Heavy rainfall disrupted manufacturing and deliveries. Mgmt expects better execution and margins in H2.💡

Order book: 3,197 Cr (vs 2,069 Cr YoY). Q2 inflow 421 Cr. 
Inquiry pipeline 19,464 Cr.  
180 Cr finished orders held back by weather/site issues; 70% dispatched in Oct, rest expected in Q3. 
Focus now on execution.💡

Capacity & Capex: 5 plants, 63,060 MVA installed.  
65 Cr IDT facility (+5,000 MVA) targeted by end-Q3 FY27 (also frees Unit 2 for 66/132 kV).  
193.58 Cr tank/frame/radiator facility (backward integration) by Oct 2027.  

Atlanta Trafo (acquired Apr 2025): +15,780 MVA. Preventive maintenance underway; key for utilisation without immediate new greenfield.

Higher voltage:  
400 kV: First 315 MVA manufacturing started Oct 2026. ~184 Cr orders. 

SC testing targeted Q3; commercial from Q4 (subject to approvals).  
765 kV reactor: In-house development; production target Q4 FY27, testing Q4–Q1 FY28.

International & new: First specialised US order. 120 inquiries (9,300 MVA). Two potential long-term partners. Export aspiration 15% in 2 years (India manufacturing via partners). BESS pipeline 3,400 MVA / ₹184 Cr (opportunities, not firm orders).

Guidance: 🎯
40% revenue CAGR aspiration (original 3-year; 1 year done). 
EBITDA margin 16–18% for FY27 & FY28. H2 expected stronger (dispatches, leverage, utilisation). 

Most legacy firm-price contracts to be done in Q3; limited exposure in Q4. Shift to price-variation clauses helps input-cost protection.💡

Risks/monitorables: 
Inventory rose to 632.9 Cr (from 364.1 Cr Mar-26); receivables 372 Cr. Watch cash conversion, margin recovery, Atlanta Trafo utilisation, capex timelines, 400 kV qualification, and conversion of US/BESS opportunities. Customer base up to 285 (from 77 in FY22). Low leverage (FY26 D/E 0.05x).

Growth triggers: 
IDT commissioning, Trafo utilisation, 400 kV execution, 765 kV progress, backward integration, US order conversion, BESS/T&D/renewables.

Outlook: Strong order book + capacity expansion + move up the voltage curve. Opportunity is clear; outcome depends on execution, utilisation, margin recovery and cash conversion.

Samhi Hotels | Q2 FY27 results

Samhi net profit falls 58.8% to ₹41.1 Cr on last year's ₹84 Cr one-off

👉 Samhi Hotels reported consolidated net profit of ₹41.1 Cr for Q2 FY27, down 58.8% from ₹99.8 Cr a year earlier. The comparison is distorted by base effects: Q2 FY26 carried ₹84.1 Cr of exceptional income, against ₹3.9 Cr this quarter. Profit attributable to owners of the company was ₹33.5 Cr, against ₹92.4 Cr a year ago.

👉 Revenue from operations rose 15.4% YoY to ₹338.1 Cr and 10.8% QoQ from ₹305.2 Cr. Other income rose 35.3% to ₹4.6 Cr. Profit before exceptional items and tax was ₹53.4 Cr, against ₹38.2 Cr in Q2 FY26. Tax expense was ₹16.2 Cr, against ₹19.9 Cr a year ago.

👉 OPM was 16.7%, down 2,456 bps from 41.3% a year earlier but up 611 bps from 10.6% in Q1 FY27. Profit excluding other income rose 40.2% to ₹48.8 Cr. Management had flagged mid-scale margin pressure from GST changes on the Q1 call, and said it was pivoting toward upscale assets.

👉 Six-month revenue rose 13.8% to ₹643.3 Cr from ₹565.2 Cr, and operating cash flow was ₹225.8 Cr against ₹165.6 Cr. Capital expenditure was ₹134.7 Cr. Cash and cash equivalents fell to ₹93.8 Cr at 30 September from ₹158.8 Cr at 31 March, while total borrowings rose to ₹1,730 Cr from ₹1,708 Cr.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans to open the W Hyderabad hotel in Q4 FY27 within a pipeline of seven hotels and 1,669 rooms, as stated on the Q1 FY27 earnings call.

👉 Road blocker: Management named mid-scale margin compression from GST changes, and reported OPM of 16.7% was down 2,456 bps year on year.

SAMHI Hotels Q2 FY27. PAT down 59%. Don’t fall for it.

Last year’s Q2 had ₹841 mn of one-offs (land impairment reversal + Caspia Delhi sale gain). This year has ₹39 mn. Strip both and PAT ex-exceptional is ₹372 mn, up 137%. PBT before exceptional ₹534 mn, up 40% on 16% revenue growth. Those are the numbers that matter 📊

Underneath: same-store occupancy 78.6% (vs 75%), RevPAR +14.3%, ARR +9.2%. One in three days was sold out. All this while air traffic in its core cities fell 11-13% and international demand stayed weak. Domestic business travel is carrying the load.

The GST change (12% with ITC to 5% without) shaved ₹103 mn off EBITDA. Ex that, EBITDA grew 21% at a 39% margin. One-time reset in the base, fades as the mix shifts upscale.

Finance cost down 10% YoY, interest rate 7.8% vs 10.8% at IPO. Net debt ₹14.6 bn, up just ₹72 mn since March despite capex on three hotels.

Growth has been same-store only for 6 quarters. That ends Q2 FY28 with W Hyderabad, then 1,669 rooms secured through FY31. Plus RARE India goes live on Marriott Bonvoy in December 🏨

Malgré des difficultés de livraison, de nouveaux paiements ont suivi, dont ceux provenant de la contribution danoise. Le profil de Datasel soulève également des questions. Avant son rachat en mars 2024 par Neco Defence, la société était spécialisée dans le développement de logiciels. D’après les informations recueillies dans le cadre de l’enquête, elle ne disposait ni des installations ni des autorisations nécessaires à la fabrication de munitions. Son site internet utilisait notamment des images issues du jeu vidéo militaire Ace Combat 6 et des visuels générés par intelligence artificielle pour présenter ses capacités industrielles. Son adresse officielle, à La Spezia, était partagée avec un concessionnaire Audi. Des munitions liées aux contrats de Datasel avaient également été jugées défectueuses lors de contrôles effectués en 2025, selon des informations révélées en septembre 2026. Le montant total des avances versées à l’entreprise atteindrait environ 70 millions d’euros.

Advait Energy Transitions: Q2 FY27 Results and Key Takeaways from the Concall

Advait provides power transmission products and is expanding into battery storage and green hydrogen. Profit grew 89% and its order book is up 47%.

Q2 FY27 (consolidated)
Revenue: ₹221 Cr (+40.8% YoY)
EBITDA: ₹32 Cr (+84.4% YoY), margin 14.5% (vs 11%)
PAT: ₹19 Cr (+88.5% YoY), margin 8.7%
H1 FY27 revenue: ₹400 Cr (+45.4% YoY)
H1 FY27 PAT: ₹34 Cr (+77.9% YoY)
Order book (including L1): about ₹1,575 Cr (+47% YoY)

1.  Order book growing fast-
The order book, including projects where Advait is the lowest bidder, grew 47% to about ₹1,575 Cr. It completed orders worth about ₹400 Cr in H1. This gives healthy revenue visibility.

2.  Transmission business steady-
Advait won distribution orders from Gujarat power utilities, including about ₹52 Cr from DGVCL. It also won orders for emergency restoration systems, OPGW (power lines with built-in optical fibre) and stringing tools. India's continued investment in transmission supports demand.

3.  Battery storage push-
Advait won a 150 MW / 300 MWh standalone battery storage project in Junagadh. A 2.5 GWh battery manufacturing plant, expandable to 5 GWh, should start by Q4 FY27. Machinery orders have already been placed.

4.  Green hydrogen progress-
Advait's electrolyser technology, which splits water into hydrogen, is being tested in a 5 MW program. It is engaging with over 13 Indian green hydrogen players. It has also signed an offtake agreement with battery maker Hithium for its upcoming orders.

5.  New integrated factory-
Phase 1 of the integrated manufacturing facility at Gangad, Gujarat should start by Q4 FY27. It will support transmission, substation and renewable energy products.

6.  Big long-term ambition-
Management has outlined a target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years, about 7 times FY26 revenue. It says this depends on investor and funding support. Margins should improve as more revenue comes from manufactured products.

Key Guidance
FY27 capex of ₹300-350 Cr
Battery plant and Gangad facility operational by Q4 FY27
Long-term target of ₹5,000 Cr revenue in about 5 years

#Wockhardt

Revenue growing but margin pressure evident 

That's the real story in its Q2 FY27 consolidated results. 

Revenue reached ₹969 Cr, up 23.9% YoY and 4.3% QoQ.

Demand looks encouraging, but revenue growth alone doesn't tell the full story.

Margins are under pressure.

Derived EBITDA fell to ₹173 Cr from ₹178 Cr last year.

EBITDA margin dropped from 22.8% to 17.9%.

Material costs and other expenses grew faster than revenue. That's eating into profitability.

 Profits tell the same story.

Profit before tax (excluding exceptional items) fell to ₹73 Cr from ₹91 Cr last year and ₹116 Cr last quarter.

More sales, but weaker quarterly profitability.

 Cash flow offers some comfort.

First-half operating cash flow improved to ₹237 Cr from ₹189 Cr.

But investment outflows on property, equipment and intangible assets totaled ₹238 Cr.

 The bigger picture.

Capital work-in-progress stands at ₹676 Cr, while intangible assets under development are ₹1,743 Cr.

There's investment happening, but the results don't disclose commissioning timelines.

Key Takeaway 

Wockhardt's revenue growth is encouraging, but margin recovery is the real test.

Wockhardt | Q2 FY27 results

Wockhardt revenue up 24% to ₹969 Cr, but profit falls 11% on margin squeeze

👉 Wockhardt reported consolidated revenue from operations of ₹969 Cr in Q2 FY27, up 23.9% from ₹782 Cr a year earlier and 4.3% higher than ₹929 Cr in Q1. Total income was ₹980 Cr. Net profit, however, fell 11% year on year to ₹73 Cr, and dropped 31.8% from ₹107 Cr in the previous quarter.

👉 Operating margin fell to 7.4% from 12.1% in Q1 and 11.3% a year earlier, as total expenses rose 27% YoY to ₹907 Cr from ₹712 Cr. Cost of materials consumed climbed to ₹243 Cr from ₹159 Cr. Profit excluding other income was ₹62 Cr, down from ₹70 Cr a year ago.

👉 Other income fell to ₹11 Cr from ₹31 Cr in Q1, and profit before tax was ₹73 Cr, against ₹116 Cr in Q1 and ₹91 Cr a year ago. No exceptional items were booked this quarter, unlike the six months last year, which carried a ₹97 Cr charge. Six-month revenue rose 24.9% to ₹1,898 Cr, with six-month net profit at ₹180 Cr against a loss of ₹26 Cr.

👉 The company record shows FY26 revenue of ₹3,373 Cr beat management's ₹3,033 Cr guidance, though net debt to equity came in at 0.10% against a guided 0.01%. ICRA upgraded the long-term rating to A- (Stable) in May, citing improved financial performance. Q2 is the second quarterly result since then, and operating margin is now the weakest of the three quarters shown here.

👉 Growth catalyst: Management plans to launch Zaynich in the US, India and Europe and double human insulin capacity, according to its June earnings call.

👉 Road blocker: Operating margin fell to 7.4% from 12.1% in Q1, while cost of materials consumed rose 53% YoY to ₹243 Cr.

#Carborundum Universal vs #Wendt India

A note to help investors work through the symphony-cacophony of Murugappa Group’s success stories.

Carborundum Universal (#CUMI) is the stronger choice for most investors seeking exposure to the abrasives and industrial materials theme. Wendt India works better as a smaller satellite holding.

CUMI is a diversified materials company under the Murugappa Group. It operates across abrasives, electrominerals, and ceramics or refractories. Trailing 12-month sales stand near Rs 5,400 cr with a market capitalisation of about Rs 19,000 cr. Trailing PAT is around Rs 188 cr. The stock trades at roughly 75 to 100 times trailing earnings. Return on equity is about 7% and return on capital employed near 10 to 11%. Debt is low.

In the June 2026 quarter, revenue rose 17% year on year and profit after tax rose 23%.

Wendt India is a focused player in super abrasives and precision grinding tools. Trailing 12-month sales are about Rs 270 cr with a market cap near Rs 1,380 cr. Trailing PAT is roughly Rs 20 cr. The stock trades near 70x trailing earnings.

Return on equity is about 5%. The company is nearly debt free. In the September 2026 quarter, revenue grew 28% year on year to about Rs 72.5 cr and profit after tax more than doubled to Rs 5.5 cr.

💯 CUMI owns a 37.5% stake in 🤝 Wendt.

✨ CUMI offers better diversification across products and geographies, higher liquidity, and stronger absolute earnings power. It also gives indirect exposure to Wendt’s super abrasives business.

Wendt has shown cleaner recent operating recovery in its core segment, but its smaller size and lower liquidity increase volatility.

Both stocks look expensive on current trailing earnings because profits have been under pressure. Further upside depends on sustained recovery in margins and volumes.

Sector tailwinds from manufacturing growth, defence, semiconductors, and shifts in Chinese competition support the theme over the medium term.

My way:

Prefer CUMI as the core holding. Consider Wendt only in a limited size if you want concentrated exposure to precision tooling and can accept higher volatility.

Accumulate on dips rather than at current levels. Monitor the next set of quarterly results for confirmation of margin improvement.

He has deep hands-on expertise in injection moulding, composites and interconnection systems, and a proven record of winning new customer accounts, opening new markets and securing long-term revenue through complex, multi-year contracts. Sona BLW Precision Forgings

An impressive quarter, with record revenue, EBITDA and PAT.
Revenue: 1,547 Cr (+35% YoY)
EBITDA: 356 Cr (+23% YoY)
PAT: 223 Cr (+29% YoY)
BEV revenue: +129% YoY, now contributing 51% of automotive revenue.
Order book: 25,100 Cr, with 3,600 Cr of fresh orders.

What makes this quarter interesting is the changing business mix.
EV traction motors are scaling up, differential assemblies are recovering, and newer businesses such as railway systems, sensors and robotics are opening additional growth opportunities.
EV and Robotics/Physical AI already account for 65% of the order book. Importantly, 31 of the company's 75 EPIC programs are yet to enter production.

Is this an inflection?
There are early signs of a meaningful revenue and product-mix inflection, with new programs transitioning towards commercialisation and stronger cash generation.
However, an earnings-margin inflection is not yet evident. EBITDA margin contracted from 25.3% to 23%, reflecting product mix and input-cost pressures.

The next trigger is whether strong revenue growth translates into operating leverage and margin expansion.

Sona Comstar increasingly looks like a broader mobility technology platform rather than just a traditional automotive component manufacturer.
